quiz.explain: Staying quiet gives you time to calm before reacting.

quiz.explain: Talking calmly helps resolve the situation.

quiz.explain: Smiling shows you are calm.

subject: English
notes: Twinkle, Twinkle is a popular nursery rhyme about a shining star that twinkles in the night sky.
The rhyme is written by Jane Taylor and is often sung by children to practice rhythm and rhyme.
The star is described as a small light that keeps shining even when the sun is gone.
Key words: twinkle, star, night, sky, light, dark, bright, shine, glow.
Rhyme scheme: AABB – the first two lines rhyme and the last two lines rhyme.
The poem teaches children about opposites: dark vs. bright, day vs. night, up vs. down.
Students can sing the poem to improve pronunciation and listening skills.
The rhyme can be acted out: opening a window, shutting a door, turning off a fan, etc.
Opposite words: dark – bright, full – empty, day – night, up – down.
Matching activity: match words with pictures of a star, moon, sun, cloud.
Fill‑in‑the‑blank: complete the lines “Shut the ______” and “Twinkle, twinkle ______”.
Listening activities: repeat the poem, listen to tongue twisters, and act out actions.
The poem is short, making it easy for Standard‑3 students to remember and recite.
It encourages teamwork when children sing together in class.
It also helps with memory by repeating the same words in different contexts.
The rhyme can be used to teach basic punctuation: commas and periods.
It is a good example of a simple poem with a clear message.
Students can draw a picture of the star to reinforce visual learning.
The rhyme can be used to practice counting: “Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how I wonder what you are.”
It introduces the concept of a “little light” that shines at night.
The poem is often used in early childhood education to develop language skills.
It can be used to teach the idea of a “tiny spark” that helps travelers see the way.

quiz.explain: The poem encourages singing.

subject: English
notes: Word family means a group of words that share the same root word, like bake, baker, baking.
In a word family, you can change the ending to make new words: bake → baker, baking, baked.
The book shows words that have the same ending, such as -ate, -ate, -ate, etc.
You can find many words that start with the same letters, for example: bake, baker, baking, baked.
The word family helps you learn new words faster because you already know the base word.
A word family can have many words: bake, baker, baking, baked, bakery, etc.
When you read a new word, try to see if it belongs to a word family you already know.
The book lists words that have ‘tr’ in them, like ‘control’ or ‘rocket’ – these are special groups to remember.
Words that end with ‘ing’ are action words, like ‘running’, ‘jumping’ – they show an action is happening.
The longest word in the list is ‘immediately’ – it has 11 letters.
Words related to space include ‘astronaut’, ‘rocket’, ‘space’, ‘gravity’ and ‘sunlight’.
Words related to the forest are ‘forest’, ‘wild’, ‘cub’ and ‘hunting’ – they describe nature.
Opposites of some words: spend ↔ earn, pet ↔ let, downward ↔ upward, ugly ↔ beautiful.
Words that end with ‘y’ in the list: ‘beautiful’, ‘colour’, ‘energy’, ‘different’, ‘learning’, ‘protect’, ‘suit’.
The book also shows words that have nine letters, like ‘question’, ‘puzzle’, ‘colour’ and ‘future’.
Use flash cards or word games to practice these word families and remember them better.
Remember to read each word carefully and find its meaning and use in a sentence.
When you see a new word, try to guess its meaning from the root word and the ending.
Practice writing the words in sentences to improve your vocabulary.
Keep a small notebook of new words and their families to review every week.

quiz.explain: "question" has nine letters.

quiz.explain: "forest" describes a wooded area.

subject: English
notes: First Aid Box is a small white box that helps when someone gets hurt.
It contains useful items like a bandage, cotton, antiseptic liquid, ointment, scissors, thermometer, soap and tablets.
A bandage covers cuts or small wounds so they don’t get dirty.
Cotton and antiseptic liquid clean the wound before you put a bandage on it.
Ointment helps the wound heal faster.
Scissors can cut bandages or cloth if needed.
A thermometer checks if you have a fever when you feel sick.
Soap and water keep your hands clean so germs don’t spread.
Keeping a first aid box at school and at home is important.
If someone is injured, wash the wound with soap and water, apply antiseptic, put a clean bandage, and check the temperature if fever is suspected.
Ask a teacher or a grown‑up for help if the injury is serious.
Remember to keep the first aid box tidy and replace used items.
Good personal hygiene (washing hands, brushing teeth, eating fresh food, drinking water, sleeping well) helps prevent injuries and illnesses.
The first aid box is a small tool that can make a big difference in a small injury.

subject: English

subject: English
chapter: 1.7 A Happy Day in the Park
notes: - A park is a place where people go to play and relax.

- In a park we can see trees, birds, flowers, benches, and sometimes a playground.

subject: English
notes: 1. Getting ready means preparing yourself for school or any activity.
2. We do simple actions like comb hair, button shirt, tie shoes.
3. These actions are called *actions* or *tasks*.
4. We can talk about actions by adding ‘ing’ to the verb: comb → combing, button → buttoning.
5. Adding ‘ing’ makes a word that shows the action is happening now.
6. In a conversation, we listen and repeat to practice speaking.
7. We can write our own short conversation with our mother or teacher.
8. We can number the actions in the right order: comb, button, tie shoes.
9. We can describe daily chores of our mother or friends.
10. We can use a dictionary to find meanings of new words.
11. We can practice reading ‘ing’ words with the right stress.
12. We can act out the conversation to make learning fun.
13. We can ask questions like ‘What do you do in the morning?’
14. We can say ‘I am combing my hair’ to use present continuous tense.
15. We can use simple sentences: ‘I am tying my shoes.’
16. We can remember that ‘ing’ words are often used for actions happening now.
17. We can use pictures to help us learn new words.
18. We can practice speaking with a partner or in a group.
19. We can write a short dialogue about getting ready.
20. We can use the word ‘ready’ to mean prepared.
21. We can use the word ‘school’ to mean the place where we learn.
22. We can use the word ‘mother’ or ‘mum’ to mean our parent.
23. We can use the word ‘shirt’ to mean a piece of clothing.
24. We can use the word ‘shoes’ to mean the footwear we wear.
25. We can use the word ‘hair’ to mean the strands on our head.

subject: English
notes: - Vehicles are means of transport: bus, train, jet, car, boat, helicopter, auto rickshaw, ship, metro‑train, bullock cart, mono‑rail, aeroplane.
- Short forms are shortened words: I’ll = I will, I’d = I would, Don’t = Do not, It’s = It is, etc.
- In the poem we use ‘I’d’ to mean ‘I would’ – e.g., ‘I’d rather take a train.’
- We can ask questions like ‘How did you get there, how did you go?’ to talk about travel.
- Vehicles belong to different ways: Road ways (bus, car), Railways (train, metro‑train), Air ways (jet, aeroplane), Water ways (boat, ship).
- You can make a list of vehicles you know and draw or collect pictures of them.
- New words about space journey can be found in a dictionary and added to a picture dictionary.
- Simple sentences from the poem: ‘The bus is too slow.’ ‘I’d rather take a jet.’

- Fill in the blanks: ‘I’d ______ take a train.’ (would)

subject: Marathi
notes: कचरा म्हणजे नको असलेले वस्तू ज्यांना आपण टाकतो.
कचरा वेगवेगळा करण्याचे कारण म्हणजे त्याचा प्रवास वेगळा असतो.
कचरा वेगवेगळा केल्याने तो पुन्हा वापरता येतो – कागद, खेळणी, इंधन इत्यादी बनवता येतात.
कचरा डब्यात टाकताना फळांच्या साली, कागदाचे तुकडे, पुठ्ठे, वाळलेले गवत इत्यादी वेगवेगळ्या डब्यांत ठेवायचे.
ओला कचरा आणि सुका कचरा वेगळे ठेवणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.
कचरा सडल्यावर वायू तयार होतो ज्याचा इंधन म्हणून वापर करता येतो.
कचऱ्याचे उत्तम खत बनवता येते ज्याने शेतीला फायदा होतो.
घरात कचरा नीट पाहून त्याची यादी करा आणि तो वेगवेगळ्या डब्यांत ठेवा.
कचरा वर्गीकरण केल्याने पर्यावरण स्वच्छ आणि आरोग्यदायी राहते.
कचरा टाकताना स्वच्छतेची काळजी घ्यावी – हात धुणे, डब्यांची स्वच्छता इत्यादी.
कचरा वर्गीकरण केल्याने पुनर्वापर आणि ऊर्जा बचत होते.
कचरा टाकताना डब्यांची ओळख पटवण्यासाठी रंग किंवा चिन्हे वापरू शकतो.
कचरा टाकताना डब्यांची जागा स्वच्छ ठेवणे आवश्यक आहे.
कचरा वर्गीकरण केल्याने कचरा व्यवस्थापन सोपे होते.

notes: आनंदाच्या शिखरावर बसणे म्हणजे मनात सर्व सुख आणि समाधान वाटणे.
कवितेत मुलांना आनंदाने बसायला सांगितले आहे.
कवी म्हणतो की मुलांच्या मनावर चांगल्या गोष्टींचा ठसा असावा.
मुलांना चिंता न करता खेळायला आणि शिकायला हवे.
आई, बाबा, आजी, आजोबा, मित्र, शिक्षक हे सर्व आपल्या भावनांना स्पर्श करतात.

बाबा बाहेरगावी गेले असता आपण थोडी चिंता करतो.
ताईने सुंदर पेन दिले असता आपण आनंदी होतो.
शाळेचा अभ्यास पूर्ण झाला नाही असता आपण निराश होतो.
रस्त्यावर पाय घसरून पडलात असता आपण घाबरतो.
वर्गाने खेळ जिंकलात असता आपण आनंदी होतो.
गुंता झालेली दोरी सोडवण्यासाठी धीर आणि प्रयत्न आवश्यक आहेत.
शिखरावर आणि आकाशात हे शब्द 'उंच' आणि 'उच्च' दर्शवतात.

बसा आणि गुंता या शब्दांमध्ये समान अक्षर 'स' आहे.
शब्द तयार करताना अक्षरांची क्रमवारी बदलून नवीन शब्द बनवता येतात.
सर्व शब्द वाचून लिहा: कार्य, धैर्य, सूर्य, शौर्य, नर्मदा, पर्यंत, पर्यावरण, सर्व, धर्म, आदर्श.

शब्दांतील समान अक्षर शोधून कविता अधिक समजून घ्या.
मुलांना आनंदाने बसायला सांगणे हे कवीचे उद्दिष्ट आहे.
मुलांच्या मनावर चांगल्या गोष्टींचा ठसा असावा हे कवीचे मत आहे.

subject: Marathi
notes: सुट्टी म्हणजे उन्हाळी सुट्टी, शाळेची बंदी असते.
सुट्टीत आपण खेळू शकतो, कुटुंबासोबत वेळ घालवू शकतो.
जोडाक्षर म्हणजे दोन अक्षरे एकत्र येऊन नवीन अक्षर बनते, जसे ‘सुट्टी’ मध्ये ‘स’ आणि ‘उ’ एकत्र येतात.
इंद्रधनुष्यावर घसरगुंडी म्हणजे खेळाचे मैदान जिथे आपण घसरतो.
फळांचा वास घेऊन आणि खाऊन आपण विविध चवी ओळखू शकतो – केळी, आंबा, चिंच, आवळा, शेंगदाणे, भजी, फणस, बोरे.
सुट्टी आवडत नसलेल्या मुलांना काम किंवा जबाबदारी असू शकते, जसे घरात काम करणे किंवा दुकानात डबा पोहोचवणे.
सण म्हणजे खास दिवस ज्यात कुटुंब आणि मित्र एकत्र येतात आणि परंपरा पाळतात.
सणाचे नाव, महिना, तयारी, कोणी काय करते, कोण येते, आणि आवडण्याचे कारण हे सर्व लिहून सांगता येते.
सण साजरे करताना परंपरा, अन्न, पोशाख, आणि खेळ यांचा समावेश असतो.
सणाची तयारी घरात कशी करतात हे जाणून घेणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.
सणाचे रीतिरिवाज आणि परंपरा विविध संस्कृतींमध्ये वेगवेगळे असतात.
सणाचे वर्णन करताना प्रश्नांची उत्तरे दिली पाहिजेत: नाव, महिना, तयारी, कोणी काय करते, कोणी येते, आवडण्याचे कारण.
सुट्टी आणि सण या दोन्हीमध्ये आनंद आणि विश्रांती असते.
सुट्टीत आपण नवीन गोष्टी शिकू शकतो आणि खेळू शकतो.
सण साजरे करताना आपण परंपरा आणि संस्कृती जपतो.

notes: चित्रे पाहून गोष्ट सांगणे हे विद्यार्थ्यांच्या कल्पनाशक्तीला चालना देते.
चित्रांमध्ये काय घडते ते लक्षपूर्वक पाहून गोष्ट लिहिणे शिकवले जाते.
वर्गात चित्रे दाखवून विद्यार्थ्यांना गोष्ट वाचून दाखवायला लावले जाते.
चित्रातील वस्तू, लोक, घटना ओळखून त्यावरून कथा तयार करतात.
चित्रकथा वाचून विद्यार्थ्यांना नवीन शब्द आणि वाक्यरचना शिकायला मदत होते.
चित्रांवरून गोष्ट लिहिताना वर्णन, कथानक, आणि निष्कर्ष यांचा समतोल राखावा.
चित्रातील रंग, आकार, आणि पोझिशन यांचा उपयोग करून कथा अधिक जिवंत बनवता येते.
चित्रातील मुख्य पात्र आणि त्याचे गुण ओळखून गोष्ट लिहिणे सोपे होते.
चित्रातील घटना क्रमाने मांडून गोष्ट लिहिणे हे कथानकाचे मूलभूत तत्त्व आहे.
चित्र पाहून गोष्ट लिहिताना विद्यार्थ्यांना प्रश्न विचारायला प्रोत्साहित करावे.

notes: रमाईंचा जन्म वणंद गावात झाला.
वडिलांचे नाव भिकू धुत्रे, आई रखमाबाई.
विवाह भिमाबाईसाठी झाला, पतीचे नाव भीमराव रामजी आंबेडकर.
रमाईंचे शिक्षण बाबासाहेबांनी घरीच शिकवले.
भिमाबाई १९१३ साली अमेरिकेला शिक्षणासाठी गेल्या.
रमाईंचा स्वभाव मितभाषी, दृढनिश्चयी, स्वाभिमानी.
ते दीन-दलित समाजाच्या सुधारण्यासाठी प्रयत्नशील होते.
रमाईंनी वसतिगृहात अन्नधान्याचा तुटवडा पाहून सोन्याच्या बांगड्या मोडून पैसे दिले.
त्यांनी वसतिगृहातील सर्व मुलांना प्रेमाने जेवण दिले.
रमाईंना कारुण्याची मूर्ती म्हटले जाते.
भिमाबाई भारतीय राज्यघटनेचे शिल्पकार म्हणून ओळखली जाते.

भिमाबाईने दीन-दलितांना स्वावलंबन दिले.

भिमाबाईने कुटुंबाच्या उज्ज्वल स्वप्नांना साकारले.
भिमाबाईची जिद्द आजही प्रेरणादायी आहे.

भिमाबाईने समाजासाठी लढा उभारला.

quiz.explain: बांगड्या मोडून पैसे दिले.

subject: Marathi
notes: ट्रॅफिकदादा म्हणजे रस्त्यावरील वाहतुकीची माहिती देणारी कविता.
लाल दिवा लागल्यावर गाडी थांबवावी आणि ब्रेक दाबावा.
पिवळा दिवा लागल्यावर काळजीपूर्वक लक्ष द्यावे आणि गती कमी करावी.
हिरवा दिवा लागल्यावर गाडी पुढे चालवू शकतो.
पार्किंगसाठी 'नो पार्किंग' चिन्ह दिसल्यास दंड होऊ शकतो.
धूर येणारी गाडी चालवू नये, ताबडतोब दुरुस्ती करावी.
रस्त्यावर चालताना डाव्या बाजूने चालणे सुरक्षित असते.
बस थांबे सामान्यतः रस्त्याच्या डाव्या बाजूला असतात.
संकटाच्या वेळी दरवाजा उघडत नसेल तर बाहेर पडण्याचा दरवाजा कुठे आहे हे ओळखणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.
धावत्या रेल्वे थांबवायची असल्यास प्रवासी काय करतील हे समजून घ्यावे.
रस्त्यावर फिरताना विविध खुणा आणि चिन्हे ओळखून त्यांचा अर्थ समजून घ्यावा.

quiz.q: ट्रॅफिकदादा म्हणतात लाल दिवा लागला तर काय करावे?

quiz.q: पिवळा दिवा लागला तर काय करावे?
quiz.explain: पिवळा दिवा म्हणजे सावधगिरीने गती कमी करणे.

quiz.q: हिरवा दिवा लागला तर काय करावे?
quiz.explain: हिरवा दिवा म्हणजे चालू ठेवणे.

quiz.q: रस्त्यावर चालताना कोणत्या बाजूने चालावे?
quiz.explain: रस्त्यावर डाव्या बाजूने चालणे सुरक्षित.

quiz.q: बसथांबे सामान्यतः रस्त्याच्या कोणत्या बाजूला असतात?
quiz.explain: बहुतेक बसथांबे उजव्या बाजूला असतात.

quiz.q: संकटकाळी दरवाजा उघडत नसेल तर काय करावे?
quiz.explain: संकटात दुसरा दरवाजा शोधणे आवश्यक.

options: धावती रेल्वे थांबवतील आणि मदत मागतील
quiz.explain: प्रवासी थांबवतील आणि मदत मागतील.

quiz.explain: लाल दिवा म्हणजे ब्रेक लावणे.

quiz.q: पिवळा दिवा लागला तेव्हा गाडीची गती कशी असावी?
quiz.explain: पिवळा दिवा म्हणजे गती कमी करणे.

quiz.q: ट्रॅफिकदादा म्हणतात 'नो पार्किंग' म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: नो पार्किंग म्हणजे पार्किंग न करणे.

subject: Marathi
notes: आम्ही नकाशा वाचतो हा अध्याय नकाशा काय असतो आणि तो कसा वाचायचा हे शिकवतो.
नकाशा म्हणजे एखाद्या ठिकाणाचे छोटे चित्र, ज्यात रस्ते, नद्या, शाळा इत्यादी दाखवलेले असतात.
नकाशावर सर्वकाही लहान अक्षरात आणि चिन्हांमध्ये दाखवले जाते.
नकाशावर रंग वापरून वेगवेगळे भाग ओळखता येतात – उदा. हिरवा रंग जंगलासाठी, निळा रंग पाण्यासाठी.
नकाशावर दिशा दाखवण्यासाठी ‘उत्तर’, ‘दक्षिण’, ‘पूर्व’, ‘पश्चिम’ हे शब्द किंवा बाण असतात.
नकाशावर ‘स्केल’ म्हणजे ‘माप’ असते, ज्याने नकाशावरील अंतर आणि वास्तविक अंतर यांचा संबंध कळतो.
नकाशावर ‘कम्पास’ (चुंबक) असतो, ज्याने दिशा शोधता येते.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ (legend) असते, ज्यात चिन्हांचे अर्थ दिलेले असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘शाळा’, ‘रुग्णालय’, ‘बाजार’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘वृक्ष’, ‘पर्वत’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘रस्ता’ आणि ‘पायी चालण्याचा मार्ग’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘पाणी’ आणि ‘नदी’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘बांध’ आणि ‘पूल’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘घर’ आणि ‘कुटुंब’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘शाळा’ आणि ‘कॅम्पस’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘पार्क’ आणि ‘बाग’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘सायकल’ आणि ‘कार’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.
नकाशावर ‘कुंजी’ मध्ये ‘विमानतळ’ आणि ‘रेल्वे स्टेशन’ अशी चिन्हे असतात.

लेखकाने लिहिण्याचा छंद कसा लागला आणि तो कसा वाढला हे स्पष्ट केले.
लेखनाने त्याची निरीक्षणशक्ती, स्मरणशक्ती आणि शब्दसंपत्ती वाढली.
मुग्धाने नवीन वर्षात डायरी (रोजनिशी) घेऊन रोज लिहायला सुरुवात केली.
दैनंदिन लेखनाने तिला बोलणे आणि लिहिणे या दोन्ही गोष्टींमध्ये आत्मविश्वास आला.
मुग्धाने आपला संकल्प केला की रोज काहीतरी लिहायचे.
शाळेतील वाचन आणि लेखनाने तिला साहित्यिक होण्याची प्रेरणा दिली.
शब्दार्थ: नित्य‑रोज, अभिनय‑हावभाव, दैनिक‑रोज प्रसिद्ध होणारे, मासिक‑दर महिन्याला प्रसिद्ध होणारे, घुम्या‑कमी बोलणारा, अबोल‑कमी बोलणारा, परिवर्तन‑बदल, संकल्प‑निर्धार, सुसंवाद‑चांगली चर्चा.
मुग्धाच्या कथा वाचून आपणही रोज लिहिण्याचा प्रयत्न करू शकतो.
लेखनामुळे आपली कल्पनाशक्ती आणि संवाद कौशल्य वाढते.
शाळेतील स्पर्धा आणि बक्षिसे मुलांना प्रोत्साहित करतात.
लेखकाच्या भाषणाने मुलांना लिहिण्याची प्रेरणा दिली.
मुग्धा आणि तिचे कुटुंब एकमेकांशी चांगला संवाद साधू लागले.
मुग्धाने डायरी लिहून आपले अनुभव नोंदवले.
डायरी लिहिणे हे आत्मचिंतन आणि आत्मविकासाचे साधन आहे.
लेखनामुळे आपल्याला आपले विचार स्पष्टपणे मांडता येतात.
मुग्धाच्या अनुभवातून आपण शिकतो की लेखनाने आपले जीवन बदलू शकते.

notes: कोण बोलतं ते आम्ही शोधतो या अध्यायात आपण शब्दांच्या अर्थावर लक्ष देतो.

वाक्यांमध्ये ‘आहे’, ‘आहेत’ या क्रियापदांचा वापर वाक्य पूर्ण करते.
‘कोण’, ‘कोणता’, ‘काय’ अशा प्रश्नार्थक शब्दांनी वाक्य सुरू होते.

वाक्याचे मुख्य भाग ‘कर्म’ आणि ‘कर्मकारक’ यांमध्ये विभागले जातात.
वाक्याचे अर्थ समजण्यासाठी ‘कण’ आणि ‘सर्वनाम’ यांची ओळख आवश्यक आहे.

वाक्याचे ‘अर्थ’ समजण्यासाठी शब्दांची क्रमवारी महत्त्वाची असते.

वाक्याचे ‘संदर्भ’ समजण्यासाठी ‘कण’ व ‘सर्वनाम’ यांचा वापर महत्त्वाचा आहे.
वाक्याचे ‘उदाहरण’ ‘तो गाडी चालवतो’ हे वाक्य आहे.

subject: Maths
chapter: a& Introduction to Geometrical Figures. 1 to 4 ) (» Addition by Carrying Over
notes: Addition by carrying over means when the sum of units (ones) is 10 or more, we write the units digit and carry the tens to the next column.
If 12 units make 1 ten, we write 1 in the tens column and keep the remaining units in the units column.
When adding two numbers, start from the rightmost column (units) and move leftwards.
If the sum of a column is 20 or more, carry 2 tens, if 30 or more, carry 3 tens, etc.
After carrying, write the remaining digit in the current column and add the carried value to the next column.
The same rule applies to adding three or more numbers – always start with units, carry to tens, then to hundreds.
A hundred is made of 10 tens; a thousand is made of 10 hundreds.
When adding, if the final column has a carry, write it as a new leftmost digit.
Practice by adding numbers vertically and horizontally to get comfortable with carrying.
Pairs of numbers that add to 100 are (1,99), (2,98), (3,97) … (50,50).
In word problems, read the story, identify the numbers to add, and then perform the addition with carrying.
Always check your answer by adding the parts again or using a calculator if available.
Keep the numbers in the correct place value columns when writing the sum.
If you forget to carry, the answer will be wrong – double‑check each column.

quiz.q: What do we write in the tens column when 12 units are added?
quiz.explain: 12 units make 1 ten, so we write 1 in the tens column.

quiz.q: When adding 345 + 278, how many units are carried to the tens column?
quiz.explain: 5+8=13, write 3 and carry 1 ten.

quiz.q: Which pair of numbers adds up to 100?
If 176 + 239 + 58 is added, what is the units digit of the result?
quiz.explain: Units: 6+9+8=23 → write 3.

quiz.q: When 12 tens are added, what new place value is created?
quiz.explain: 12 tens make 1 hundred.

quiz.q: In the addition 342 + 567, how many tens are carried?
quiz.explain: 2+6=8, no carry; 4+5=9, no carry; 3+5=8, no carry. Actually no carry. But if we ask tens carry, answer 0.

quiz.q: What is the sum of 99 and 1?
Which of these statements is true?
options: We always carry when the sum is 9.
We carry when the sum is 10 or more.
We carry only in hundreds column.
quiz.explain: Carry when sum ≥10.

quiz.q: If 123 + 456 + 789 is added, what is the hundreds digit of the result?
quiz.explain: Hundreds: 1+4+7=12 → write 2.

subject: Maths
chapter: a& Number Work a Subtraction by Borrowing
notes: - 100 rupees = 10 notes of 10 rupees or 100 coins of 1 rupee.
- 1 hundred = 10 tens.
- 1 ten = 10 units (rupees).
- When subtracting, if you need more units than you have, you can untie (break) one ten into 10 units.
- If you need more tens than you have, you can untie one hundred into 10 tens.
- Untying means taking one higher value and converting it into lower values.
- After untie, you borrow the needed units or tens from the higher place.
- Subtraction is done from right to left (units, tens, hundreds).
- Always untie only one hundred or one ten, even if many are needed.
- Example: 51 – 24: break one ten into 10 units, then subtract.
- Example: 545 – 265: break one hundred into 10 tens, then subtract.
- Example: 507 – 288: break one hundred into 10 tens, then break a ten into 10 units.
- Example: 900 – 365: break one hundred into 10 tens, then break a ten into 10 units.
- Keep track of what you have left after each step.
- Write the answer in hundreds, tens and units.
- Word problems often ask for the difference between two numbers.
- Use the same untie method for any subtraction problem with missing units or tens.

quiz.q: If you have 3 tens and need 8 units, what do you do first?
quiz.explain: You break one ten into 10 units to get enough units.

quiz.q: What is 100 – 27?
quiz.explain: Subtract 27 from 100 by breaking one hundred into 10 tens and then 10 units.

quiz.q: In 545 – 265, how many tens do you have after breaking one hundred?
quiz.explain: One hundred gives 10 tens; plus the original 4 tens = 14 tens.

quiz.q: What is the result of 507 – 288?
quiz.explain: After untie operations, the answer is 219.

quiz.q: If you need to subtract 5 from 0 units, what do you do?
quiz.explain: Break a ten into 10 units to get units to subtract.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a correct way to write 1 hundred?
quiz.explain: 1 hundred equals 10 tens.

quiz.q: In 900 – 365, after breaking one hundred, how many tens do you have before breaking a ten?
quiz.explain: One hundred gives 10 tens; plus the original 0 tens = 10 tens.

quiz.q: When subtracting 545 – 265, how many hundreds are left after subtracting 2 hundreds?
quiz.explain: After untie, 5 hundreds – 2 = 3 hundreds left.

quiz.q: If you have 4 tens and need 7 units, what is the first step?
quiz.explain: Break a ten into 10 units to get enough units.

quiz.q: What does ‘untie’ mean in subtraction?
options: Break a higher value into lower values
quiz.explain: Untie means converting a higher value into lower values.

subject: Maths
notes: Division is sharing equally. The number you divide is called the dividend.
The number you divide by is the divisor.
The answer you get is called the quotient.
If there is something left after sharing, it is called the remainder.
When the remainder is 0, all items are shared equally.
To divide, write the dividend under the line and the divisor outside.
The first digit of the dividend is compared with the divisor to start the division.
If the divisor is bigger than the first digit, use the first two digits, and so on.
The quotient is written above the line, one digit for each step.
The remainder is written below the line after the division is finished.
In a clock, the short hand shows hours and the long hand shows minutes.
The minute hand moves 60 times in one hour, so each step is 5 minutes.
Between two numbers on a clock face there are 5 minutes difference.
When the minute hand is at 12, the time is exactly on the hour.
When the minute hand is at 3, it is 15 minutes past the hour.
The hour hand moves slowly, one number every hour.
The time 40 minutes past 4 is shown by the minute hand at 8.
The time 45 minutes past 12 is shown by the minute hand at 9.
In a division example, 12 flowers divided by 4 gives a quotient of 3 and remainder 0.
In 15 laddoos divided by 5, each child gets 3 and there is no remainder.
In 22 rupees divided by 5, each person gets 4 rupees and 2 rupees remain as remainder.

If 15 laddoos are shared among 5 children, how many laddoos does each child get?
What is the remainder when 22 rupees are divided by 5?

quiz.q: Which hand of a clock shows the minutes?
quiz.explain: The long hand is the minute hand

quiz.q: How many minutes are there between 12 and 1 on a clock?
quiz.explain: One number apart is 5 minutes

quiz.q: If the minute hand is at 9, how many minutes past the hour is it?
quiz.explain: 9 × 5 = 45 minutes

quiz.q: What is the time shown when the short hand is at 4 and the long hand at 12?
quiz.explain: Short hand at 4 means 4 o’clock

quiz.q: When the minute hand reaches 3, what is the time?
quiz.explain: 3 × 5 = 15 minutes

quiz.q: In a division problem, if the dividend is 22 and the divisor is 5, what digit is written in the units place of the quotient?
quiz.explain: 22 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 2

subject: Maths
notes: - A calendar shows days, weeks, months and years.
- Each month has 28 to 31 days.
- The 5th of December is a Sunday in 2023.
- Festivals and holidays are special days marked on the calendar.
- Birthdays are celebrated on the same date each year.
- Leap years have 29 days in February, occurring every 4 years.
- To find age, count whole years from birth year to current year.
- 15th August 1947 is India’s Independence Day.
- 30th year after 1987 means 2017.
- A whole can be split into halves, quarters, thirds, etc.
- Two halves make a whole; two quarters make a half; four quarters make a whole.

quiz.q: Which month has 31 days?
quiz.explain: December has 31 days.

quiz.q: What day is the 5th of December 2023?
quiz.explain: 5th December 2023 is a Sunday.

quiz.q: If someone is born on 15th January 2015, how old are they on 15th January 2025?
quiz.explain: 10 years have passed.

quiz.q: Which month is 4 months after August?
quiz.explain: August +4 = December.

quiz.q: How many days are in February in a leap year?
quiz.explain: Leap year February has 29 days.

quiz.q: What is a quarter of a whole?
quiz.explain: Quarter means one fourth.

quiz.q: India became independent on 15th August 1947. How many years have passed by 15th August 2023?
quiz.explain: 2023-1947 = 76 years; add 1 for inclusive count = 77.

quiz.q: If a whole is divided into four equal parts, what is each part?
quiz.explain: Each part is a quarter.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a part of a whole?
quiz.explain: Whole is the whole, not a part.

quiz.q: What does a line that divides a figure into two equal parts represent?
quiz.explain: It represents a half.

subject: Maths
notes: - A fraction tells how many parts of a whole are taken.
- Half means 1/2 of the whole.
- Quarter means 1/4 of the whole.
- Three‑quarters means 3/4 of the whole.
- To find half of a number, divide it by 2.
- To find a quarter of a number, divide it by 4.
- To find three‑quarters, multiply the number by 3 and then divide by 4.
- 1 hour = 60 minutes. Half an hour = 30 minutes.
- 1 dozen = 12 items. Half a dozen = 6 items.
- A fraction can be used with money, length, time, or any quantity.
- When you give away a fraction, the remaining part is the whole minus that fraction.
- If you cut off a fraction of something, the cut length is that fraction of the whole.
- Fractions can be written as a/b, e.g., 1/2, 1/4, 3/4.
- You can write fractions in words: half, quarter, three‑quarters.
- Fractions help us share, divide, and compare parts of a whole.
- Always check the unit (metres, rupees, minutes) when you calculate a fraction.

quiz.q: What is half of 20 metres?
quiz.explain: Half of 20 is 20 ÷ 2 = 10.

quiz.q: How many bananas are in a half a dozen?
quiz.explain: Half a dozen = 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

quiz.q: If 1 hour has 60 minutes, how many minutes are in a half hour?
quiz.explain: Half of 60 is 30.

quiz.q: What is three‑quarters of 16 metres?
Arope has 16 metres. If a three‑quarter length is cut off, how many metres are cut?
quiz.explain: Three‑quarters of 16 is 12 metres.

quiz.q: What is a quarter of 80 rupees?
If Sonali has 10 metres of cloth and gives half to Ramu, how many metres does she still have?
quiz.explain: Half of 10 is 5; remaining is 5.

quiz.q: How many boys came to Sonu’s birthday party?
quiz.explain: The table lists 7 boys.

quiz.q: Which mode of transport is used by the most children in the class?
quiz.explain: 10 children used the bus.

quiz.q: What is half of 4 hours 40 minutes?
quiz.explain: Half of 4h40m is 2h20m.

subject: Maths
notes: - A tally mark is a vertical line used to count items quickly.
- A group of five tally marks is written as four vertical lines with a diagonal line crossing them.
- Tally marks help us make tables of numbers without writing long numbers.
- In a table we list the name of the item in one column and the tally marks in the next column.
- The total number of items is counted by adding all the tally marks in a column.
- We can use tally marks to find the most popular or least popular item by comparing totals.
- Tally marks can be used for counting people, plants, crops, foods, or any other objects.
- When we write a table we keep the items in the first column and the tally marks in the second column.
- The number of people who like an item is the number of tally marks for that item.
- We can ask questions like "Which item has the most tally marks?" or "How many more children like X than Y?"
- Tally marks are useful for quick counting in classrooms and in everyday life.
- A table with tally marks is a simple way to show data to others.
- We can use pictures instead of tally marks if we want to show the items visually.
- Counting with tally marks helps us practice addition and comparison of numbers.
- When we finish a table we can read the totals to answer questions about the data.

quiz.q: What is a tally mark used for?
quiz.explain: A tally mark is a quick way to count items.

quiz.q: How many vertical lines make a complete group of tally marks?
quiz.explain: Five vertical lines, the fifth crossed by a diagonal line, make a group.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a correct way to write 12 tally marks?
quiz.explain: 12 is written as two groups of five plus two extra marks.

quiz.q: If 8 children like Jalebi and 5 like Laddoo, how many more children like Jalebi?
Which crop is grown by the smallest number of farmers?
quiz.explain: Peas have the fewest tally marks in the table.

quiz.q: What is the total number of children who watched TV?
quiz.explain: The tally marks for TV show 9 children.

quiz.q: Which fruit has the most tally marks?
quiz.explain: Mango has the highest number of tally marks.

quiz.q: How many children took a walk in the garden?
quiz.explain: The tally marks for a walk show 4 children.

quiz.q: Which item has the least number of tally marks?
quiz.explain: Other sweet dishes have the fewest marks.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a table with tally marks?
quiz.explain: Tables with tally marks help us count quickly.

subject: Maths
chapter: Use of beads, stones, seeds, etc. to carry out operations on numbers
notes: Use beads, stones or seeds to count numbers.
A bead for each unit (1).
Two beads together make 2, three make 3, etc.
Ten beads in a line make 10 (a group of ten).
A group of ten beads can be written as a single symbol (a dot).
Adding beads means putting more beads together.
Subtracting beads means taking some away.
Multiplying by 2 means putting two groups of the same size next to each other.
Multiplying by 3 means putting three groups of the same size next to each other.
Adding groups of ten is easier than adding many single beads.
Subtracting groups of ten is easier than removing many single beads.
You can use different coloured beads to keep track of different numbers.
Beads can be arranged in rows to show how many of each type you have.
You can use a tally mark for each item and a slash to count five tallies as one group of five.
When you count with beads, you can always check your answer by counting again.
If you have 12 beads, you can write 10 + 2 or 2 + 10 – the result is the same.
You can use stones or seeds if you do not have beads – the idea is the same.
Counting with objects helps you see how many you have and how many you need.
You can use a small box to keep the beads separate for each number.
When you finish a calculation, you can put the beads back in the box.
Beads are a simple way to learn addition, subtraction and multiplication.
They also help you understand groups and sets.
Use beads to practice counting up to 20 or more.
Remember: one bead = one unit, ten beads = one group of ten.

quiz.q: If you have 7 beads and add 3 more, how many beads do you have?
You have 4 groups of 5 beads each. How many beads are there in total?
You counted 12 beads and then took away 4. How many are left?
Which of the following shows a group of ten beads?
quiz.explain: A group of ten is shown by 10 beads in a line.

quiz.q: If you have 9 beads and add 1 more, what is the new total?
You have 2 groups of 3 beads each. How many beads do you have?
You counted 15 beads and then added 5 more. How many beads are there now?
If you have 8 beads and take away 3, how many are left?
You have 3 groups of 4 beads each. How many beads are there?
Which operation is shown when you put two groups of 5 beads together?
quiz.explain: Putting two groups together is addition.

notes: 1. A number is a whole number that we use for counting and ordering.
2. Numbers can be written in digits (0,1,2,…) or in words (zero, one, two, …).
3. The digits 0 to 9 are called *digits* or *numerals*.
4. Numbers can be written in *place value* form – units, tens, hundreds, thousands, etc.
5. In a three‑digit number, the leftmost digit is the *hundreds* place, the middle is the *tens* place, and the rightmost is the *units* place.
6. The value of a digit depends on its place: 5 in the tens place means 5×10 = 50.
7. To read a number, start from the left: “two hundred thirty‑five” means 2×100 + 3×10 + 5×1.
8. We can write the same number in different ways: 235, 2 3 5, or “two hundred thirty‑five”.
9. The *order* of numbers is from smallest to largest: 1, 2, 3, …
10. We can *add* numbers by putting them side by side and carrying over when a column exceeds 9.
11. In addition, we use the symbol “+” to show that two numbers are being added.
12. We can *subtract* numbers by taking one away from another, borrowing when needed.
13. The symbol “–” (minus) shows subtraction.
14. Numbers can be *compared* using the symbols “<” (less than), “>” (greater than), and “=” (equal to).
15. We can write numbers in *scientific notation* for very large or very small numbers, but that is for later grades.
16. Counting objects helps us understand numbers in real life: apples, books, pencils, etc.
17. Practice reading and writing numbers up to 999 to become comfortable with place value.
18. When we write numbers in words, we use “and” only in some countries; in this book we write “hundred thirty‑five” without “and”.
19. The digit 0 is important because it shows that a place has no value, e.g., 205 has no tens.
20. We can use a *number line* to visualize the order of numbers and to add or subtract by moving right or left.
21. The *sum* of two numbers is the result of addition; the *difference* is the result of subtraction.
22. When adding two numbers, we start from the rightmost column and move left, carrying over if the sum is 10 or more.
23. When subtracting, we start from the rightmost column and borrow from the next column if needed.
24. Numbers can be grouped into *sets* and we can count how many items are in each set.
25. Practice makes perfect – keep counting, adding, and subtracting everyday!

quiz.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in the number 4,300?
quiz.explain: In 4,300 the 4 is in the thousands place, so its value is 4×1000.

quiz.q: Which symbol is used to show addition?
quiz.explain: The plus sign (+) indicates addition.

quiz.q: What is 7 + 5?
quiz.explain: 7 plus 5 equals 12.

quiz.q: Which number is greater: 234 or 342?
quiz.explain: 342 is larger than 234.

quiz.q: What is 9 – 3?
quiz.explain: 9 minus 3 equals 6.

quiz.q: If you write 123 in words, which of the following is correct?
quiz.explain: 123 is written as "one hundred twenty‑three".

quiz.q: What does the digit 0 represent in a number?
quiz.explain: 0 shows that there is no value in that place.

quiz.q: Which of these is a three‑digit number?
quiz.explain: 678 has three digits: 6, 7, and 8.

quiz.q: When adding 56 and 78, what do you do if the sum of the units column is 14?
options: Write 4 and carry 1 to the tens column
quiz.explain: Write 4 and carry 1 to the next column.

quiz.q: Which symbol means ‘equal to’?
quiz.explain: The equals sign (=) means the two sides are equal.

subject: Maths
chapter: चित्रनिरीक्षण, मणिमाळांचा वापर यांसारख्या विविध उपक्रमांतून मनोरंजकता वाढवाव
notes: चित्रात ८ चेंडूंचा समूह दाखवला आहे.
समूहाचे अर्धे म्हणजे ४ चेंडू.
समूहाचे पाव म्हणजे २ चेंडू.
समूहाचे पाऊण म्हणजे ३ चेंडू.
अर्धा आणि पाव मिळून पाऊण होतो.
उदाहरण: मैदानाची लांबी २० मी. अर्धी १० मी, पाव ५ मी, पाऊण १५ मी.
१ तास = ६० मिनिटे. अर्धा तास = ३० मिनिटे.
४ लीटरचा पाव = १ लीटर.
डझन = १२. अर्धा डझन = ६, पाव डझन = ९.
वय, पैसे, लांबी, वेळ यांचे अर्धे, पाव, पाऊण कसे काढायचे ते शिकवले.
वर्गात गट बनवून वस्तू मोजणे, तक्ते तयार करणे.
ताळ्याच्या खुणा वापरून माहिती नोंदवणे सोपे होते.
वर्गातील क्रियाकलाप, आवडते फळ, खेळ इत्यादींची तक्ते तयार करणे.
समूहाच्या भागांची गणना करताना ‘भाग’ शब्दावर लक्ष द्या.
अर्धा+पाव=पाऊण हे नियम लक्षात ठेवा.
उदाहरणे सोडवून सराव केल्याने समज वाढते.

subject: Maths
chapter: अध्यापन करताना दशकाचे गट करणे, सुटे करणे यांसारख्या कृती प्रत्यक्ष करून घ्याव्य
notes: 1. दशक म्हणजे दहा वर्षे असतात.
2. दशकाचे गट करणे म्हणजे 10 वर्षे एकत्र ठेवणे.
3. दशकाचे सुटे करणे म्हणजे 10 वर्षे वेगवेगळे करणे.
4. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितात वापरले जाते.
5. दशकाचे गट करणे केल्यास 10,20,30… अशी संख्या मिळते.
6. दशकाचे सुटे केल्यास 1,2,3… अशी संख्या मिळते.
7. दशकाचे गट करणे म्हणजे 10 च्या गुणकांची ओळख.
8. दशकाचे सुटे करणे म्हणजे 10 च्या भागाकारांची ओळख.
9. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे दैनंदिन जीवनात उपयोगी.
10. दशकाचे गट करणे केल्यास मोठी संख्या लहान भागात विभागता येते.
11. दशकाचे सुटे केल्यास लहान संख्या मोठ्या भागात विभागता येते.
12. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील मूलभूत क्रिया आहेत.
13. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे यामुळे गणित सोपे होते.
14. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील संख्यात्मक कौशल्य वाढवतात.
15. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तर्कशक्ती वाढवतात.
16. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील पद्धती शिकवतात.
17. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तंत्र शिकवतात.
18. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील कौशल्य वाढवतात.
19. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तर्कशक्ती वाढवतात.
20. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तंत्रज्ञान शिकवतात.
21. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तंत्रज्ञान वाढवतात.
22. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तंत्रज्ञान वाढवतात.
23. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तंत्रज्ञान वाढवतात.
24. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तंत्रज्ञान वाढवतात.
25. दशकाचे गट करणे आणि सुटे करणे हे गणितातील तंत्रज्ञान वाढवतात.

subject: Maths
chapter: गरजेनुसार पूरक उपक्रम/साहित्य यांच्या मदतीने सराव घ्याव
notes: बेरीज म्हणजे दोन किंवा अधिक संख्यांची एकत्रित बेरीज करणे.
वजाबाकी म्हणजे एक संख्या दुसऱ्या संख्येतून वजा करणे.
भाजक म्हणजे ज्या संख्येने भाग दिला जातो ती संख्या.
भाज्य म्हणजे ज्या संख्येने भाग घेतला जातो ती संख्या.
भागाकार म्हणजे भाग दिल्यानंतर उरलेली संख्या.
शतक म्हणजे १०० ची एकक.
हजाराचे स्थान म्हणजे १००० ची एकक.
विस्तारित रूप म्हणजे संख्येतील प्रत्येक अंकाचे मूल्य दाखवणे.
सममिती म्हणजे आकृतीचे दोन्ही बाजू एकसारखे असणे.
सर्वांत मोठी संख्या म्हणजे दिलेल्या संख्यांपैकी सर्वात मोठी.
सर्वांत लहान संख्या म्हणजे दिलेल्या संख्यांपैकी सर्वात लहान.
मापनाची एककं: मीटर (लांबी), वजन (किलो), रुंदी (मीटर).
क्लोज्ड फिगर म्हणजे बंद आकृती ज्यात सर्व बाजू एकमेकांना जोडलेल्या असतात.
डेटा हँडलिंग म्हणजे माहितीचे व्यवस्थापन आणि नोंद ठेवणे.
भाजक आणि भाज्य यांच्यातील संबंध: भाज्य = भाजक × भागाकार + उरलेली संख्या.
वजाबाकी करताना हातच्याची गरज भासल्यास borrowing करणे आवश्यक.
बेरीज व वजाबाकी या दोन्ही क्रिया गणितातील मूलभूत क्रिया आहेत.
शतकस्थान आणि हजाराचे स्थान ओळखून संख्या वाचणे सोपे होते.
विस्तारित रूपात संख्या लिहिताना प्रत्येक अंकाला त्याच्या स्थानानुसार मूल्य दिले जाते.
सममिती असलेल्या आकृत्या ओळखणे आणि त्यांचे गुणधर्म समजणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.
भागाकार आणि उरलेली संख्या ओळखून भागाकाराची संपूर्ण प्रक्रिया समजते.
मापनाच्या एककांची योग्य नोंद ठेवणे गणितात अचूकता आणते.
बेरीज व वजाबाकीच्या सरावाने गणितात आत्मविश्वास वाढतो.

quiz.q: 1. बेरीज म्हणजे काय?

quiz.explain: बेरीज म्हणजे दोन किंवा अधिक संख्यांची एकत्रित बेरीज.

quiz.q: 2. वजाबाकी करताना हातच्याची गरज का भासते?
quiz.explain: हातच्याची गरज वजाबाकी करताना कमी होणाऱ्या संख्येची भरपाई करण्यासाठी असते.

quiz.q: 3. "Closed figure" म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: Closed figure म्हणजे बंद आकृती ज्याचे सर्व बाजू एकमेकांना जोडलेले असतात.

quiz.q: 4. "Remainder" या शब्दाचा अर्थ काय?
quiz.explain: Remainder म्हणजे भागाकारानंतर उरलेली शेष संख्या.

quiz.q: 5. "Divisor" म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: Divisor म्हणजे ज्याने विभाजन केले जाते तो संख्या.

quiz.q: 6. "Dividend" या शब्दाचा अर्थ काय?
quiz.explain: Dividend म्हणजे ज्याला विभाजित केले जाते तो संख्या.

quiz.q: 7. "Symmetry" म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: Symmetry म्हणजे आकृतीची सममिती.

quiz.q: 8. "Expanded form" म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: Expanded form म्हणजे संख्येचे विस्तारित रूप, ज्यात प्रत्येक अंकाचे स्थान स्पष्ट केले जाते.

quiz.q: 9. "Hundred’s place" म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: Hundred’s place म्हणजे शतकाचे स्थान, जिथे शतकाची संख्या असते.

quiz.q: 10. "Thousand’s place" म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: Thousand’s place म्हणजे हजाराचे स्थान, जिथे हजाराची संख्या असते.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Eggs are laid by many animals like hens, crows, spiders, lizards.
Chicks grow inside the egg and need warmth to hatch.
A hen sits on her eggs to keep them warm and protect them.
When a hen is hatching, she may become aggressive to keep others away.
Some animals, like butterflies, change form from egg to caterpillar to pupa to adult – this is called metamorphosis.
A caterpillar is the larva stage of a butterfly and eats leaves fast.
A caterpillar sheds its skin (moult) several times as it grows.
After the last moult, a caterpillar makes a silk thread and becomes a pupa (chrysalis).
Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar transforms into an adult butterfly.
The adult butterfly has four wings and six long legs.
Different butterflies lay eggs on specific plants; e.g., Plain Tiger on milkweed.
The life cycle of a butterfly is: egg → larva (caterpillar) → pupa (chrysalis) → adult.
Insects in stored grain may be in any of these four stages.
A hen’s eggs take about 20‑22 days to hatch.
Butterflies are part of the environment and should not be caught for fun.

quiz.q: Which stage of a butterfly lives inside a chrysalis?
quiz.explain: The pupa stage is inside the chrysalis.

quiz.q: Why does a hen sit on her eggs?
quiz.explain: The hen keeps the eggs warm for hatching.

quiz.q: What is the term for a caterpillar shedding its old skin?
quiz.explain: Moulting is shedding old skin.

quiz.q: Which animal does NOT lay eggs?
quiz.explain: Cats are mammals and do not lay eggs.

quiz.q: How many times does a caterpillar moult before becoming a pupa?
quiz.explain: It moults about four times.

quiz.q: Which stage is the adult butterfly?
quiz.explain: Adult is the final stage.

quiz.q: What happens when a hen hatches her eggs?
quiz.explain: She may become aggressive to protect eggs.

quiz.q: What is the first stage of a butterfly’s life?
quiz.explain: Egg is the first stage.

quiz.q: Which stage eats leaves rapidly?
quiz.explain: The larva (caterpillar) eats leaves.

quiz.q: What is the term for the adult stage of a butterfly?
quiz.explain: Adult is the final stage.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Cloth is made by weaving threads together.
Weaving uses long threads woven into fabric.
Cotton is a common material for cloth; other materials include wool, jute, nylon, rayon.
Cotton comes from cotton plants; wool comes from sheep; jute from jute plants.
Spinning wheel (charakha) draws yarn from raw material.
Knitting needles are used to make sweaters and caps at home.
Handlooms and powerlooms weave cloth on a large scale.
Clothes get dirty when we wear them; washing removes dirt.
Natural substances like soap nuts, washing soda, limestone can clean clothes.
Old clothes can be reused, donated, turned into quilts, dishcloths, or paper.
Clothes change with weather and festivals; cotton is popular in Maharashtra.
Cloth can be pulped to make paper plates and flowers.
Wool is made from sheep’s hair; other animals like goats also yield wool.

quiz.q: What is weaving?
quiz.explain: Weaving is intertwining threads to make cloth.

quiz.q: Which material is NOT used to make cloth?
quiz.explain: Steel is not a textile material.

quiz.q: What can be used to clean clothes if soap is not available?
quiz.explain: Soap nuts are a natural cleaner.

quiz.q: Which tool is used at home to make sweaters?
quiz.explain: Knitting needles make sweaters and caps.

quiz.q: Old clothes that are still good can be given to
quiz.explain: Good old clothes are donated.

quiz.q: What is the source of cotton yarn?
quiz.explain: Cotton yarn comes from cotton plants.

quiz.q: Which of these is a natural substance used for washing?
quiz.explain: Limestone is a natural cleaner.

quiz.q: Why do we wash clothes?
quiz.explain: All reasons are correct.

quiz.q: Which animal yields wool?
quiz.explain: Sheep provide wool.

quiz.q: Clothes can be turned into paper by
quiz.explain: Threadbare clothes are pulped to make paper.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Chest expands when we breathe in because the lungs fill with air and push the ribs outward.
The heart is an internal organ that pumps blood through the body.
Lungs are internal organs that bring air into the body and give oxygen to the blood.
The oesophagus is a flexible tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach.
The stomach is an internal organ that mixes food with digestive juices to make it soft.
The brain is an internal organ that controls all our movements and feelings.
The ribcage is a cage of bones that protects the heart and lungs.
The skull protects the brain by forming a hard shell.
The alimentary canal is a long pipe‑like system that takes food from the mouth to the anus.
Blood vessels carry blood from the heart to every part of the body.
The pulse is the feeling of the heart beating under the skin.
The pulse slows when we sleep and speeds up when we run.
The heart contracts (beats) and then relaxes, keeping blood moving.
The lungs expand when we breathe in, making the chest swell.
The brain interprets information from the eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin.

quiz.q: Why does the chest expand when we breathe in?
options: Because the lungs fill with air
quiz.explain: The lungs take in air and expand, pushing the chest outward.

quiz.q: Which part of the body is used for seeing?
quiz.explain: Eyes are the sensory organs for vision.

quiz.q: What is an external organ?
options: An organ that cannot be seen
An organ on the outside of the body
An organ that moves the body
quiz.explain: External organs are on the outside and can be seen.

quiz.q: Which organ carries food from the mouth to the stomach?
quiz.explain: The oesophagus is the tube that moves food to the stomach.

quiz.q: What keeps the blood flowing in the body?
quiz.explain: The heart pumps blood through the vessels.

quiz.q: Why does the chest swell when we breathe in?
quiz.explain: The lungs take in air and expand, causing the chest to swell.

quiz.q: Which cavity houses the brain?
quiz.explain: The brain is inside the cranial cavity.

quiz.q: What is the function of the oesophagus?
quiz.explain: The oesophagus transports swallowed food to the stomach.

quiz.q: Why are sensory organs called sensory?
quiz.explain: They detect information from the surroundings.

quiz.q: What is the main role of the heart?
quiz.explain: The heart pumps blood throughout the body.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: - A simple illness is one that can be cured easily at home with basic care.
- A serious illness needs a doctor and proper treatment.
- Warm salt water can help soothe a sore throat.
- For a cold, inhaling steam or putting a hot cloth on the chest helps.
- If you vomit because of fever, give a cool lemon sherbet and light food the next day.
- Clean cuts with water, dry, apply iodine, cover with clean cotton and bandage.
- Never take medicine that must be swallowed without a doctor’s advice.
- A health service or medical service is a place where doctors treat people.
- Government hospitals and primary health centres are in most towns and villages.
- Home remedies have limits; if you don’t feel better in 1‑2 days, see a doctor.
- A mantrik or village priest does not cure snakebite; go to a hospital for anti‑snakebite injection.
- Elderly family members often suggest home cures, but they may not always work.
- If you feel tired or have a fever, rest and drink plenty of water.
- A balm is a soft ointment used to soothe skin or heal small wounds.
- Vasaka leaf extract is used to treat cough and sore throat.
- Signs of a cold include runny nose, sneezing, sore throat and mild fever.

quiz.q: What is a common home remedy for a sore throat?
quiz.explain: Warm salt water helps soothe the throat.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a sign of a cold?
quiz.explain: A cold usually does not cause a high fever.

quiz.q: What should you do if someone is vomiting due to fever?
options: Give them a cool lemon sherbet
quiz.explain: A cool lemon sherbet is light and easy to digest.

quiz.q: When should you go to a doctor instead of using a home remedy?
options: If the illness lasts more than a day or two
quiz.explain: If symptoms worsen or do not improve in a day or two, see a doctor.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a health service?
quiz.explain: Health services provide medical treatment for the ill.

quiz.q: Which of these illnesses is likely to cure quickly?
quiz.explain: A cold usually resolves in a few days, unlike the others.

quiz.q: What is the correct first aid for a small cut?
options: Apply a tincture of iodine and bandage
quiz.explain: Clean the wound, apply iodine, then cover with a clean bandage.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a recommended home remedy for a fever?
quiz.explain: Heavy meals are not advised during fever.

quiz.q: What does a mantrik do in the story?
options: Takes the snakebite victim to a hospital
quiz.explain: The mantrik chants mantras, not medical treatment.

quiz.q: Why should medicines that must be swallowed not be taken without a doctor’s advice?
quiz.explain: Swallowable medicines can be dangerous without proper guidance.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Directions are the ways in which we can go from one place to another – North, South, East and West.
The main directions are the four cardinal points: North, South, East and West.
Sub‑directions are the points between the main directions – for example North‑East, South‑West, etc.
A compass rose is a small card that shows all the directions and sub‑directions on a map.
Maps are drawn on paper, so the real distance between places is shown in a smaller, proportional distance on the map.
The scale of a map tells us how many units on the map equal one unit on the ground – e.g. 1 cm = 1 km.
To find the distance on a map, multiply the real distance by the scale factor or divide the map distance by the scale factor.
The direction of a place is read by looking at the line from the observer’s point to the place on the map and matching it with the compass rose.
The rising of the sun in the east and the setting in the west help us remember the main directions.
When we draw a map, we keep the same orientation as the real world so that North on the map is always North in reality.
The distance between two points on a map is always less than or equal to the real distance.
If the map scale is 1 cm = 10 km, a 2 cm distance on the map means 20 km in real life.
The compass rose is used to read both main directions and sub‑directions on a map.
The main directions are always parallel to the ground, which makes maps easier to read.
Knowing the directions helps us find places, plan journeys and understand maps better.

quiz.q: Which direction is opposite to North?
quiz.explain: South is directly opposite to North.

quiz.q: What is the name of the diagram that shows all directions?
quiz.explain: A compass rose displays all main directions.

quiz.q: If a map scale is 1 cm = 10 km, how many cm represent 50 km?
quiz.explain: 50 km ÷ 10 km per cm = 5 cm.

quiz.q: Which sub-direction lies between North and East?
quiz.explain: North-East is between North and East.

quiz.q: What is the main direction that is not a sub-direction?
quiz.explain: East is a main direction, not a sub-direction.

quiz.q: When drawing a map, the distance shown is
options: Always larger than the real distance
Always smaller than the real distance
quiz.explain: Map distances are proportionate to real distances.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sub-direction?
quiz.explain: South-West is a sub-direction.

quiz.q: What helps us read a map correctly?
quiz.explain: All tools help read a map.

quiz.q: Which direction is used to find the location of a place?
quiz.explain: Compass rose shows directions for locating places.

quiz.q: Why is a scale given in maps?
quiz.explain: Scale tells how map distances relate to real distances.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Maps show places and directions.
A map is a picture of an area on a flat surface.
Symbols are tiny pictures that represent real things.
Natural things are made by nature (trees, rivers, hills).
Man‑made things are built by people (houses, schools, roads).
A compass rose shows north, south, east and west.
A scale tells how big a distance on the map is in real life.
An index lists all the symbols used in the map.
Moving things (people, cars) are not drawn on a map.
A map can be made from a sketch by adding a title, scale and directions.

quiz.q: What does a compass rose show on a map?
quiz.explain: A compass rose shows north, south, east and west.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a natural object?
quiz.explain: A river is made by nature.

quiz.q: What is needed to convert a sketch into a map?
quiz.explain: A title, scale and directions are required.

quiz.q: Which symbol would you use for a tree?
quiz.explain: A circle is often used to show a tree.

quiz.q: Moving objects like people are shown on a map because they:
options: They do not stay in one place
quiz.explain: Moving objects are not shown because they change places.

quiz.q: The scale of a map tells you:
options: The year the map was made
The size of the map on paper
How far a distance on the map is in real life
quiz.explain: The scale relates map distance to real distance.

quiz.q: Which of these is a man‑made object?
quiz.explain: A school is built by people.

quiz.q: A map is usually drawn on:
quiz.explain: Maps can be on paper, stone, or digital.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT shown on a map?
quiz.explain: People walking are moving and not shown.

quiz.q: To make a map, you should first:
quiz.explain: A sketch is the first step before drawing symbols.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: - Maharashtra is a state in western India with Mumbai as its capital and Nagpur as the second capital.
- The state is divided into three main regions: Coastal (Western Ghats), Mountainous (Sahyadri), and Plateau.
- The highest peak in Maharashtra is Kalsubai in the Sahyadri range.
- Major rivers: Godavari (longest), Krishna, and others flow from east to west into the Arabian Sea.
- The Arabian Sea lies to the west of Maharashtra.
- The state has varied rainfall: high in the Western Ghats, moderate in the plateau, low in the north‑east.
- Crops depend on rainfall: rice in high rainfall areas, jowar and tur in moderate, jowar and soyabean in low.
- Major cash crops include cotton, sugarcane, cashew, and mango.
- Marathi is the official language; dialects include Konkani, Varhadi, Ahirani, and tribal dialects like Gormati.
- Festivals celebrated: Diwali, Dasara, Ganesh, and regional festivals like Narali Pournima in Konkan.
- Agriculture is mainly rainfed (kharif season) but some areas use irrigation (rabi season).

quiz.q: Which mountain range runs along the western coast of Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Sahyadri (Western Ghats) forms the western boundary.

quiz.q: What is the longest river in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Godavari is the longest river flowing through Maharashtra.

quiz.q: Which district is known for growing grapes?
quiz.explain: Nashik district is famous for grape cultivation.

quiz.q: The capital of Maharashtra is:
quiz.explain: Mumbai is the state capital.

quiz.q: Which region receives the highest rainfall?
quiz.explain: Western Ghats receive high rainfall.

quiz.q: Which crop is mainly grown in low rainfall areas?
quiz.explain: Jowar grows well in low rainfall.

quiz.q: The second capital of Maharashtra is:
quiz.explain: Nagpur is the second capital.

quiz.q: Which dialect is spoken in the Konkan region?
quiz.explain: Konkani is spoken in Konkan.

quiz.q: The Arabian Sea lies to the:
quiz.explain: Arabian Sea is to the west of Maharashtra.

quiz.q: Which season is called 'kharif'?
quiz.explain: Kharif season is during monsoon.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Day and night happen because the Earth is round and it spins on its axis.
Half of the Earth faces the Sun and receives light – that is day.
The other half is away from the Sun and is dark – that is night.
The Earth completes one full spin in about 24 hours.
When the Sun rises it appears in the east and moves toward the west.
Sunrise and sunset times change each day because the Earth’s tilt and orbit change the angle of the Sun’s rays.
In March 21 (vernal equinox) day and night are about 12 hours each.
In June 21 (summer solstice) the day is longest and the night shortest in the northern hemisphere.
In September 22 (autumnal equinox) day and night are again about 12 hours each.
In December 22 (winter solstice) the night is longest and the day shortest.
After each solstice the length of day and night gradually changes until the next solstice.
Longer days mean summer, shorter days mean winter.
The Sun is not moving around the Earth; the Earth’s rotation makes the Sun appear to move.
The Earth’s rotation is called the rotation of the Earth.
The Sun’s disappearance from the sky in the evening is called sunset.
The Sun’s appearance in the morning is called sunrise.
The Earth’s shape is a sphere (a very large ball).
The Earth gets light from the Sun.
The cycle of day and night repeats continuously every 24 hours.
Birds return to nests earlier in winter because nights are longer and temperatures are lower.
During a new moon we cannot see the Moon because it is on the same side of the Earth as the Sun.

quiz.q: What causes the difference between day and night on Earth?
quiz.explain: The Earth rotates on its axis, exposing different parts to sunlight.

quiz.q: When does the sun rise?
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

quiz.q: How many hours are there in a full day?
quiz.explain: A full day is 24 hours long.

quiz.q: On which dates do day and night have equal length?
quiz.explain: These dates mark the equinoxes when day and night are equal.

quiz.q: What happens to day length from June 21 to September 22 in our part of the Earth?
quiz.explain: After the longest day, days gradually become shorter.

quiz.q: Why can we not see the moon on a new moon day?
options: It is hidden behind the Earth
It is facing away from the Sun
quiz.explain: The new moon faces the Sun, so its illuminated side is not visible.

quiz.q: Which season is associated with longer days?
quiz.explain: Summer has longer days and shorter nights.

quiz.q: What is the Earth’s shape?
quiz.explain: The Earth is roughly spherical.

quiz.q: What is the term for the disappearance of the sun from the sky in the evening?
quiz.explain: The sun’s disappearance is called dusk.

quiz.q: Which of the following is true about June 21 in our part of the Earth?
quiz.explain: June 21 is the longest day and shortest night.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: - Upbringing means the way we learn habits, likes and dislikes while growing up.
- Parents and relatives teach us basic skills like walking, talking, brushing teeth and behaving politely.
- Friends and neighbours also influence us by showing us how they act, speak and eat.
- We learn by observation and practice, not only by being taught directly.
- A lion cub learns to hunt from its mother and other lionesses after a few weeks of protection.
- Good habits are developed through repeated practice and correction by adults.
- Bravery awards are given to children who show courage, like Hali Raghunath Baraf and Sameep Anil Pandit.
- Social service, as shown by Baba Amte, is an example of learning values from family legacy.
- Diversity is learned when we meet people from different places and learn about their food and festivals.
- Neighbours help us become self‑reliant by showing how to do tasks on our own.
- We often imitate friends’ games, clothes and study habits without realizing it.
- The list of things we learn grows as we grow: from crawling to riding a bicycle to buying groceries.
- Parents hold our hands while we learn to walk, showing us how to correct mistakes.
- Good habits lead to being praised and called a grown‑up.
- Learning from others helps us become well‑rounded and respectful people.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of upbringing?
quiz.explain: Upbringing shapes our habits, likes, dislikes and values.

quiz.q: Who usually teaches a child to walk?
quiz.explain: Parents hold the child's hand and teach walking.

quiz.q: How long does a lion cub stay helpless before learning to hunt?
quiz.explain: The cub is helpless for about two weeks.

quiz.q: What award did Hali and Sameep receive?
quiz.explain: They were felicitated with the National Bravery Award.

quiz.q: Which generation of the Amte family continues Baba Amte’s work?
quiz.explain: The third generation carries on the mission.

quiz.q: How do we learn many things without being taught?
quiz.explain: We pick up things through observation and exposure.

quiz.q: What is a key influence on a child’s upbringing besides parents?
quiz.explain: Neighbours also influence upbringing.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT mentioned as something we learn from parents?
options: How to play a cell phone game
quiz.explain: Flying a kite was not listed.

quiz.q: What does the text suggest about learning from friends?
quiz.explain: We pick up habits from friends unconsciously.

quiz.q: Which activity is NOT listed as a way to learn from neighbours?
quiz.explain: Eating vegetables was not mentioned as a neighbour activity.

subject: EVS Part 1
chapter: Changes in the Family and Neighbourhood
notes: - A family is a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption.
- The number of people in a family can change over time.
- Four main reasons for change: marriage, birth, death and migration.
- Marriage can add a new member or move a member to another family.
- Births add new members to the family.
- Deaths reduce the number of members.
- Migration is moving to another place for work, study or other reasons.
- When people move, they stay in touch by letters, phone or internet.
- Families can be large (many members) or small (few members).
- Large families often split into smaller families when members move away.
- Migration brings people from different parts of the country together.
- This shows the diversity of festivals, food, customs and traditions.
- Neighbours live in the same locality and help each other with problems like garbage, water and electricity.
- Friendly relations with neighbours make the community life joyful.
- Families and neighbourhoods change together over time.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a reason for the change in the number of people in a family?
quiz.explain: Weather does not affect family size.

quiz.q: What is the term for moving to another place to live?
quiz.explain: Migration means moving to another place.

quiz.q: When a family member marries, what happens to the family size?
quiz.explain: Marriage adds a new member.

quiz.q: Which event can reduce the number of people in a family?
quiz.explain: Death removes a member.

quiz.q: Why do people migrate to other cities or states?
quiz.explain: Work or education are main reasons.

quiz.q: What do neighbours help each other with?
quiz.explain: Neighbours help with many daily needs.

quiz.q: Which of these is a benefit of friendly relations with neighbours?
quiz.explain: Friendly relations make life joyful.

quiz.q: What does migration show about a country?
quiz.explain: Migration shows diversity of culture.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a reason for a family to become smaller?
quiz.explain: All listed events can reduce family size.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of the chapter "Changes in the Family and Neighbourhood"?
options: To understand how families and neighbours change
quiz.explain: The chapter explains family and neighbour changes.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: - We go to school to learn and make friends.
- We study together, play, share snacks, and help each other.
- School has many activities: functions, trips, clean‑up, decoration.
- Everyone should feel that learning is fun.
- Teachers can give letters to students to show progress and encourage them.
- Students can write letters, reply, send greeting cards, and learn to send e‑mail.
- In a three‑legged race, pairs that stay balanced reach the finish line easily; unbalanced pairs fall.
- Some children cannot see, hear or walk easily; they need special help and support.
- All children, including those with special needs, have the right to education.
- Girls also have the right to education but may face chores that delay their learning.
- Students speak different mother tongues at home (Gujarati, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, etc.).
- School uniforms are worn, but on non‑uniform days the classroom becomes colourful.
- Respecting diversity and helping each other makes school delightful.
- New students from other towns should be welcomed and talked to about their previous school.
- Wearing costumes from different parts of the country is a fun way to learn about cultures.
- Writing simple sentences like “Give me water, please” in different languages helps practice language skills.

quiz.q: What do we do in school every day besides studying?
quiz.explain: Students study, play, share snacks and help each other.

quiz.q: Why did the teacher write a letter to every child?
options: To ask them to study harder
To invite them to a party
quiz.explain: The letter showed progress in studies, sports and activities.

quiz.q: Which activity helps students learn about different cultures?
quiz.explain: Wearing costumes from different parts of the country teaches about culture.

quiz.q: What is a reason some pairs fall in a three‑legged race?
quiz.explain: Unbalanced pairs stumble or fall.

quiz.q: What should teachers do for children with special needs?
options: Ask parents to leave them out
quiz.explain: Teachers should encourage and support them.

quiz.q: Which language is NOT mentioned as a mother tongue in the chapter?
quiz.explain: Spanish is not listed among the mother tongues.

quiz.q: What is one way to make learning more enjoyable?
quiz.explain: Helping each other makes work enjoyable.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Plants give us food, water, air and shelter.
Animals help us by giving milk, meat, eggs, wool and guarding our houses.
Every living thing needs food, water and air to survive.
Plants need soil, water, sunlight and nutrients from the soil to grow.
Water is more important for a mouse than for an elephant – different animals need different amounts.
Plants that are not aquatic cannot grow in waterlogged soil – they rot if they get too much water.
Animals live where all their needs are met – food, water, shelter and safety.
Tigers live in grasslands with waterholes, tall grasses and caves for shelter.
Monkeys and squirrels live in trees (arboreal) and help spread seeds by their droppings.
During winter trees shed leaves, animals grow thicker coats and frogs go underground.
In summer trees get new leaves, fruits like mangoes and cashews are ready for harvest.
Rainy season brings green grass, frogs, and crops start to grow.
The environment changes with the seasons; living things adapt to survive.
Silk comes from the cocoon of the silkworm (Bombyx mori).
Arboreal means living in trees – from Latin arbor.
Fruits grow in specific regions because of climate, soil and water conditions.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Transport is the movement of people or goods from one place to another.
Means of transport include walking, bicycles, cars, buses, trains, ships, airplanes, rockets, and pipelines.
The wheel was invented by observing logs and rocks rolling down hills.
Pipelines carry water, oil, and gas safely over long distances.
Communication is the sending or receiving of information.
Early communication used pigeons, runners, and telegrams.
Modern communication uses radio, television, internet, mobile phones, and satellites.
Mass communication reaches many people at once, e.g., newspapers and TV shows.
Animals communicate by sounds, body language, and scents.
Transport and communication help us travel, trade, and stay connected.
Using too many transport and communication methods can harm the environment.
Safety and speed are important when choosing a transport method.
The fastest transport is usually a rocket or airplane, the slowest is walking.
Mass media like radio and TV are used for entertainment and education.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Natural disasters are serious mishaps caused by nature, like floods, earthquakes, tsunamis, hailstorms, and lightning.
A flood happens when heavy rain makes a river rise and overflow its banks.
An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement of rocks inside the earth.
A tsunami is a huge sea wave created when an underwater earthquake pushes the water up.
Hailstorms are showers of small ice balls that can damage crops and hurt people and animals.
Untimely rain is rain that falls outside the normal rainy season and can cause water‑logged fields.
During a flood, it is safest to go to a high place and wait until the water goes down.
During an earthquake, sit under a strong table or bed, or stand under a doorframe to avoid falling objects.
If an earthquake starts in the sea, the waves that reach the coast are called tsunamis.
Knowing what to do in a disaster can save lives and reduce damage.

quiz.q: Which natural disaster is caused by the sudden movement of rocks in the earth’s crust?
quiz.explain: Earthquakes occur when rocks in the earth’s bowels move, producing waves that shake the ground.

quiz.explain: The text defines tsunamis as gigantic sea waves caused by an under‑sea earthquake.

quiz.explain: A railway collision is a man‑made disaster, not a natural one.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: - The environment is the natural world around us – air, water, land, plants and animals.
- Humans use resources from the environment (wood, water, minerals) to make life easier.
- When we use too many resources or pollute, the environment gets harmed and it hurts all living things.
- Pollution is the release of harmful substances into air, water or soil. It can cause breathing problems and diseases.
- Deforestation means cutting down trees. It reduces places for birds and insects to live and causes more air pollution.
- Population growth means more people, more houses, more cars and more factories, which need more resources and produce more waste.
- Water is essential for drinking, cooking, farming and industry. When water is scarce, people suffer and crops fail.
- Dams store rainwater so it can be used when rivers dry up.
- Improved farming methods (e.g., mixed cropping, better seeds) help produce enough food for a growing population.
- The main idea of the chapter is that our actions can endanger the environment and we must be careful.
- Key terms: environment, pollution, deforestation, population growth, water scarcity, dam, borewell, improved farming.
- Remember: protect trees, reduce waste, use water wisely, and think about how our choices affect nature.

quiz.explain: Dams store rainwater so it can be used when rivers dry up.

Borewells are deep, narrow wells pumped by electric machines to reach underground water.
Panpois are clay jars of drinking water set up on roads for people who need water.
Water that is stored must be kept clean and protected from pollution.
Water should be used economically – use only what is needed and avoid waste.
When water is stored, it can be used for drinking, irrigation, industry and electricity generation.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: • Water is a liquid that can dissolve many substances.
• A substance that dissolves in water is called a solute.
• When a solute dissolves, it spreads evenly throughout the water forming a solution.
• The mixture of solute and water is called a solution.
• Some substances dissolve in water (e.g., sugar, salt, alum).
• Other substances do not dissolve (e.g., sand, oil, sawdust).
• When a substance dissolves, the water may change taste (salty, sweet).
• Seawater is salty because it contains dissolved salt.
• Water from different wells can taste different because of dissolved minerals.
• If water is still, heavy particles settle at the bottom – this is called settling.
• Filtering water with cloth or strainer removes suspended particles – this is filtration.
• Even clear water may contain tiny living things called micro‑organisms.
• Micro‑organisms can be good (help make yoghurt) or harmful (cause disease).
• Boiling water kills harmful micro‑organisms and makes water safe to drink.
• A safe drinking water is called potable water – it does not harm health.
• A solution of salt and sugar for rehydration is called ORS (oral rehydration solution).
• Saline is a solution of salt in water used in hospitals.
• A substance that does not dissolve in water is called insoluble.
• The density of an object determines whether it floats (lighter) or sinks (heavier).
• The process of making muddy water clear is called purification.
• Water that looks clear may still be unsafe if it contains micro‑organisms.
• To make sugar dissolve quickly in sherbet, stir vigorously or heat slightly.
• A sieve with small holes lets fine particles pass but keeps larger ones like rava out.

quiz.q: Which substance dissolves in water and gives the water a sweet taste?
quiz.explain: Sugar dissolves in water and makes it taste sweet.

quiz.q: What is the mixture formed when a solute dissolves in water called?
quiz.explain: The uniform mixture of solute and water is called a solution.

quiz.q: Which of the following does NOT dissolve in water?
quiz.explain: Oil does not dissolve in water; it floats.

quiz.q: What is the process of letting heavy particles settle at the bottom of still water called?
quiz.explain: Settling is the settling of heavy particles.

quiz.q: Which of these is a harmful micro‑organism that can cause disease?
quiz.explain: All listed micro‑organisms can be harmful.

quiz.q: What does ORS stand for?
quiz.explain: ORS is Oral Rehydration Solution.

quiz.q: Which substance is used to make a solution called saline?
quiz.explain: Saline is a solution of salt in water.

quiz.q: If a substance floats on water, it is likely to be?
quiz.explain: Floating objects are lighter than water.

quiz.q: Which method removes suspended particles from muddy water?
quiz.explain: Filtration removes suspended particles.

quiz.q: Why might clear water still be unsafe to drink?
options: It may have a bad taste
quiz.explain: Clear water can still contain harmful micro‑organisms.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Water is needed for drinking, cooking, washing, bathing, cleaning, and watering plants.
Containers for water include earthen pots, brass pots, copper pots, steel tanks, and plastic bottles.
Newer containers are usually made of steel or plastic because they are cheap, light, and easy to clean.
A lid keeps dust, insects and dirt out of the water and keeps it clean.
A tap on a container lets you pour water without touching the water, preventing contamination.
Water can become stale only if it is left for a very long time; it can be reused if it is still clean.
Pumps lift water from wells or tanks and can be powered by diesel or electricity.
Water towers store water at a height so that gravity helps it flow to homes and streets.
Water purification plants treat water from rivers, lakes or reservoirs so it is safe to drink.
Water is transported from the source to the house through a network of pipes and taps.
People should not waste water: keep taps off when not needed, reuse leftover water for plants, and avoid over‑filling containers.
Water is a valuable resource; it should be stored properly and used carefully.
Cities often grow near rivers because water is close and easy to collect.
Water can be carried in buckets, but it is heavy; using a tap or a pump saves effort.
Cleaning the container before refilling keeps the water safe for drinking.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Variety in food means different dishes can be made from the same grain or vegetable.
A staple food is the main food eaten in a region, usually a grain like rice, wheat or jowar.
Rice is the staple in southern India because the climate and soil are good for rice cultivation.
In coastal areas, rice, coconut and coconut oil are common foods.
In the plateau region of Maharashtra, jowar is the main crop and is used to make bhakari, papad, etc.
In the central region of Maharashtra, jowar, bajra, groundnuts, soyabean, sesame and mustard are common.
Fruits are available in different seasons: summer, rainy and winter; some fruits are sold all year round.
Improved seeds, water availability, import and faster transport help fruits be available all year.
The main crop of a region determines the diet of the people there.
Different regions have different staple foods because of climate, soil and water availability.

A food that is only eaten in winter

quiz.q: Which crop is grown in the plateau region of Maharashtra?

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Food is needed for energy, growth, nourishment and health.
A diet is the food we eat every day.
Staple foods are eaten in large amounts – rice, wheat, jowar, bajra, chapatis and bhakari.
Other foods are eaten in small amounts – spices, chutneys, pickles and sweets.
Flour is made from grains like jowar, bajra and wheat.
Butter, ghee and yoghurt are made from milk (animal source).
Oil comes from seeds such as groundnut, sesame and coconut.
Sour taste comes from lemons, tamarind, raw mangoes and some spices.
Sweet taste comes from sugar, jaggery, fruits and honey.
Bitter taste comes from bitter gourd, black pepper, some spices and certain fruits.
Spicy hot taste comes from chilli and black pepper.
The tongue has taste buds that help us recognise sweet, sour, bitter, salty and spicy tastes.
Water is essential for digestion and for keeping the body healthy.
Different foods give different nutrients – energy, proteins, vitamins and minerals.
A balanced diet includes all kinds of foods in the right proportions.
Preserving nutrients: use minimal water, cover food, use pressure cooker, sprout pulses early, eat whole grain flour, eat fruits with skins, mix foods in a dish.

quiz.q: Why do we need food?

quiz.q: Which foods are considered staple foods?
