quiz.explain: They collected one‑fourth (Chauthai) and one‑tenth (Sardeshmukhi) of revenue.

quiz.explain: The Battle of Palkhed (1715) ended in a Maratha victory.

quiz.explain: Kanhoji Angre commanded the Maratha naval forces.

quiz.q: Which Maratha general captured the forts of Thane and Vasai from the Portuguese?
quiz.explain: Bajirao I led the campaigns in 1739.

quiz.explain: The Marathas obtained the Subhedari (governorship) of these regions.

quiz.explain: Shahu Maharaj was crowned Chhatrapati in 1713.

quiz.explain: These revenues financed the Maratha military.

quiz.explain: The victory at Palkhed opened the way to North India.

subject: History & Civics
chapter: Marathas – The Protectors of the Nation
notes: Marathas were a powerful Indian group who ruled large parts of western and central India in the 18th century.
The Peshwa was the chief military and political leader of the Maratha Empire.
Shahu Maharaj was a Maratha king who helped the Marathas gain more power after Bajirao I.
The Marathas fought against the Afghans led by Ahmad Shah Abdali, who invaded India several times.
In 1751 the Marathas entered a treaty with the Mughal emperor to protect Delhi from Abdali’s attacks.
The Marathas captured Delhi in 1752 and later pushed Abdali’s army as far as Attock (now in Pakistan).
The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was a huge defeat for the Marathas against Abdali’s forces.
After Panipat the Marathas lost much territory but later regained power under Peshwa Madhavrao and Mahadji Shinde.
The Marathas were known for their cavalry, artillery and a strong navy in the Konkan region.
They built many forts, temples and irrigation works, and promoted education and justice.
The Maratha Empire had a complex family tree of Peshwas, with many members sharing the same names.
The Marathas were tolerant of different religions and allowed people of all faiths to serve in their army.
The Marathas fought against the Nizam of Hyderabad, Hyder Ali of Mysore and the British East India Company.
The Marathas’ decline began after the defeat at Panipat and the rise of British power in India.
The Marathas’ legacy includes the city of Pune, the Maratha navy and the concept of a united India.

quiz.explain: Bajirao I was the first Peshwa and the main military commander.

quiz.explain: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was a crushing loss for the Marathas.

quiz.explain: The Marathas were famous for their fast cavalry.

quiz.explain: The Nizam of Hyderabad defeated the Marathas at Rakshasbhuvan.

quiz.explain: Peshwa Madhavrao was known for irrigation projects.

quiz.explain: They captured Delhi in 1752 to protect it from Abdali.

subject: History & Civics
notes: - The Maratha Empire expanded under leaders like Malhar Rao Holkar, Ahilyabai Holkar, Mahadji Shinde, and the Bhosale of Nagpur.
- Malhar Rao Holkar founded the Holkar rule in Indore and built temples, ghats, and water facilities.
- Ahilyabai Holkar was a great administrator, built lakes, temples, and promoted trade and agriculture.
- Mahadji Shinde (Mahadji Scindia) restored Maratha control over Delhi and the North after the defeat at Panipat.
- The Bhosale of Nagpur, especially Raghuji, expanded Maratha influence into the South and East (Odisha, Bengal).
- The Maratha navy, led by Kanhoji Angre, defeated Portuguese, British, and Siddhi naval forces.
- The Maratha Empire faced internal strife and external pressure from the British, leading to its decline by 1818.
- Key titles: Peshwa (prime minister), Sardar (chief), Vakil (chief agent).
- Maratha administration introduced new laws, agricultural cess, and improved irrigation.
- The Marathas used guerrilla tactics and modernized artillery with French help (e.g., de Boigne).

quiz.explain: Malhar Rao Holkar established the Holkar dynasty in Indore.

quiz.q: Which Maratha leader restored Delhi after the defeat at Panipat?
quiz.explain: Mahadji Shinde re‑established Maratha control over Delhi.

quiz.q: What was the main contribution of Ahilyabai Holkar?
quiz.explain: Ahilyabai Holkar built temples, lakes, and promoted agriculture.

quiz.q: Which Maratha ruler was known for modernising artillery with French help?
quiz.explain: Mahadji Shinde employed French officer de Boigne to modernise artillery.

quiz.q: The Maratha navy defeated which of the following?
quiz.explain: The navy defeated Portuguese, British, and Siddhi forces.

quiz.q: The Bhosale of Nagpur expanded Maratha influence into which region?
quiz.explain: Raghuji Bhosale extended Maratha rule into Odisha.

quiz.q: Which title did Mahadji Shinde receive from the Peshwa?
quiz.explain: Mahadji was given the title Vakil (chief agent) by the Peshwa.

quiz.q: What caused the decline of Maratha power by 1818?
quiz.explain: Internal divisions and British military victories weakened the Marathas.

subject: History & Civics
chapter: Life of the People in Maharashtra
notes: - Life of people in Maharashtra during the Maratha period (1630‑1810 CE) was largely agrarian and village‑based.
- Villages were self‑sufficient; main crops were jowar, bajra, wheat, ragi, maize and rice.
- Daily diet consisted of bhakari (flatbread), onions, chutney, vegetables, milk and dahi.
- Barter system was used for everyday transactions; money was rarely used.
- Houses were simple mud or brick constructions; wadas (large houses) were built in cities with one or two storeys.
- Men wore dhoti, kurta, angarakha and mundas; women wore nine‑yard sarees and blouses.
- Festivals celebrated included Gudhi Padwa, Nagpanchami, Bail‑Pola, Dasara, Diwali, Makarsankrant, Holi, Eid and Ganeshotsava.
- Maratha administration had Patil (village protector) and Kulkarni (revenue officer).
- Balutedars were village specialists (blacksmith, carpenter, potter, goldsmith etc.) paid in kind.
- Joint family system was common and important for village affairs.
- Women’s life was confined to household chores; transport was by bullocks, boats and camel riders.
- Education was mainly through pathshalas (Hindu) and madarasas (Muslim); literacy was low among women.
- Maratha rulers promoted architecture (wadas, ghats, forts) and painting (wall paintings, temple murals).
- Sports and games like wrestling, kho‑kho, chess, dice, and folk dances (tamasha, mallakhamb) were popular.
- Two major religions were Hinduism and Islam; the state followed a liberal religious policy.
- Maratha rulers built temples, forts, water supply systems and underground pipes in cities like Pune and Nashik.
- The period saw the rise of Maratha power and the spread of Marathi culture and literature.

subject: History & Civics
chapter: Civics (Introduction to our Constitution ... Fundamental Duties)
notes: Constitution is a written set of rules that governs a country.
It contains the rights of citizens and duties of the government.
The Constitution is made by representatives elected by the people.
It has a preamble that states the aims: sovereignty, socialism, secularism, democracy, republic.
Sovereign means the country is free from foreign control.
Socialist means wealth should be shared and poverty reduced.
Secular means no religion is the state religion and all are equal.
Democratic means people elect leaders and have a say in decisions.
Republic means leaders are elected, not inherited.
The Constitution has three lists: Union (central), State, and Concurrent (both).
Union list includes defence, foreign affairs, railways, etc.
State list includes agriculture, health, local government, etc.
Concurrent list includes education, marriage, etc.
The Constitution also has Directive Principles that guide the government but are not enforceable in courts.
Fundamental Rights are enforceable in courts and include freedom of speech, equality, etc.
The Constitution has a system of separation of powers: Legislature, Executive, Judiciary.
The Constitution was adopted on 26th January 1950 and is celebrated as Republic Day.
The Constitution Day (26th November 1949) marks the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly.
The Constitution of India was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad and led by Dr. B. Ambedkar.
The Constitution has 22 parts, 395 articles and 8 schedules.
The Constitution can be amended by a special procedure involving both houses of Parliament.
The Constitution protects fundamental rights and provides remedies like writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, etc.).
The Constitution also protects rights against exploitation, such as child labour laws and minimum wage acts.
The Constitution guarantees freedom of religion, language, culture and education.
The Constitution includes provisions for a uniform civil code and a directive to promote social justice.

subject: History & Civics
chapter: India before the Times of Shivaji Maharaj
notes: - The last powerful dynasty before Shivaji Maharaj was the Yadava dynasty, whose capital was Deogiri near Aurangabad.
- The Yadavas ruled from the 9th to the 13th century and spread their influence from the Krishna River to the east and west.
- The Gurjara-Pratihara and Rashtrakuta empires were earlier North Indian powers that spread from Kanauj to the south.
- The Chola dynasty (8th–13th century) ruled Tamil Nadu and had naval power in the Indian Ocean, conquering parts of Karnataka and Sri Lanka.
- The Delhi Sultanate began with Qutubuddin Aibak (1206–1210) and later rulers like Alauddin Khalji, Muhammad bin Tughluq, and Ibrahim Lodi.
- The Bahamani Sultanate (1336–1527) was founded by Hasan Gangu and later ruled by the Adilshahi, Nizamshahi, Qutubshahi, and Baridshahi.
- The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646) was founded by Harihara and Bukka and reached its peak under Krishnadevaraya.
- The Mughal Empire (1526–1707) was founded by Babur, expanded under Akbar, and ended with Aurangzeb.
- The Marathas rose under Shivaji Maharaj after the decline of the Bahamani and Mughal powers.
- Key terms: Yadava, Gurjara-Pratihara, Rashtrakuta, Chola, Delhi Sultanate, Bahamani, Vijayanagara, Mughal, Maratha.

subject: History & Civics
notes: - The Bhakti movement was a religious reform movement that started in India around the 7th century and spread across the country.
- It emphasised devotion (bhakti) to a personal god and rejected rigid rituals and caste barriers.
- Famous saints of the movement include Ramanuja, Ramananda, Kabir, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, and Basaveshwara.
- Ramanuja taught that God is loving and accessible to all, not just the elite.
- Ramananda preached that all human beings are equal and that devotion is the path to God.
- Kabir’s verses were simple and used everyday language to reach common people.
- Chaitanya Mahaprabhu promoted devotion to Krishna using songs and dance.
- Basaveshwara in Karnataka introduced the Lingayat faith, rejecting caste distinctions and encouraging simple living.
- The movement also influenced the rise of Sikhism and Sufi traditions, promoting harmony between Hindus and Muslims.
- Key features: use of local languages, emphasis on love and service, rejection of idol worship, and acceptance of all social groups.

subject: History & Civics
chapter: Maharashtra before the Times of Shivaji Maharaj
notes: Maharashtra before Shivaji was ruled by various Muslim sultanates like Ahmadnagar, Bijapur and the Mughals.
The local village head was called a Patil; he collected revenue and maintained order.
A Kulkarni was a village accountant who kept records of land and revenue.
The village was called a Mauja; a larger settlement was a Kasba and the district was a Pargana.
A Pargana consisted of many villages; its headquarters was usually a Kasba.
The people of a village were called villagers or “Mauja” people; they worked mainly in agriculture.
Artisans such as carpenters, blacksmiths and weavers lived in Kasbas and made a living by trading their goods.
The Portuguese, Dutch, French and British established trading posts (peths) near Kasbas to control trade.
A peth was a market area adjacent to a Kasba where merchants and craftsmen sold their wares.
The term “Budruk” meant a larger or older village; “Khurd” meant a smaller or newer village.
During the 1630s a great famine struck Maharashtra, causing crop failure, famine and loss of livestock.
The Deshmukh was the chief of a Pargana, the Deshpande was the chief of all Kulkarnis, and the Patil was the chief of a village.
The Varkari movement, led by saints like Dnyaneshwar, Namdeo, Eknath and Tukaram, promoted equality, devotion and social reform.
The saints used simple Marathi language (abhanga, keertans) to reach common people and to criticize social inequality.
Sant Ramdas Swami, a 17th‑century saint, wrote Dasbodh, a practical guide for self‑development and governance.
The Samarth Sampradaya was a devotional tradition founded by Sant Chokhamela and later followed by Sant Tukaram and others.
The term “Vatan” (Arabic) meant hereditary land granted to a saint, exempt from revenue.
The term “Baluta” was a share of produce paid by peasants to artisans for their services.
The term “Topkar” was a custom headgear worn by Shete and Mahajan, the local merchants and money‑lenders.
The term “Peth” was also called “Topkar” because of the merchants’ headgear.
The Varkari pilgrimage (Vari) to Pandharpur is celebrated every year in the month of Bhadrapada.
The Varkari movement encouraged people to live in harmony, equality and devotion to God.
The saints’ teachings helped people cope with foreign invasions, droughts and famines.
The saints’ compositions are still sung in Maharashtra’s temples and homes.
The saints’ teachings influenced later leaders like Shahaji Maharaj and the Maratha warriors.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was born in 1630 in Shivneri fort near Junnar, Pune district.
He was the son of Shahaji Maharaj, a prominent Sardar of the Deccan.
Shahaji was a valiant, courageous, and intelligent commander who served the Mughals, Adilshah of Bijapur, and Nizamshahi of Karnataka.

Veermata Jijabai, Shivaji’s mother, was a strong political mentor who trained him in administration, military tactics, and moral values such as modesty, truthfulness, vigilance, courage and fearlessness.
Shivaji started his struggle for Swaraj in the Maval region, a hilly and difficult terrain that gave him a strategic advantage.
He captured many forts within his jagir – Torana, Murumbdey, Kondhana, Purandar, Rajgad – to establish control over the surrounding areas.
Rajgad became the first capital of Swaraj, symbolising his independent rule.
Shivaji built a navy after conquering the Konkan coast, recognising the need to counter Portuguese, British and Siddi forces on the western coast.
He entered into treaties with the Adilshah, such as the return of Panhala fort, to secure his position against larger powers.
The royal seal (Rajmudra) of Shivaji listed the Maval valleys and expressed gratitude to his father, emphasising welfare of his people.
Shivaji’s companions included Baji Prabhu Deshpande, Tanaji Malusare, Bajiprabhu Deshpande, and many other Sardars who aided his campaigns.
He captured Javali in 1656, gaining wealth and strategic forts like Pratapgad, Kalyan and Bhiwandi.
The siege of Panhala by Siddi Jauhar lasted five months; Shivaji negotiated a treaty and returned the fort to the Adilshah.
Shivaji’s military strategies relied on surprise attacks, use of geography, and strong alliances with local sardars.
His legacy is the foundation of a sovereign Maratha state, independent from Mughal, Adilshah and other foreign powers.
Swaraj means self‑rule or self‑governance, a concept Shivaji championed through military, administrative and naval strength.
Shivaji’s education included learning about governance, military tactics, and moral virtues from his mother and senior commanders.
The forts of Shivaji were not just military bases but symbols of control over the land and its people.
Shivaji’s naval force was built to protect the Konkan coast and to challenge European powers on the western coast.
The capture of forts like Rajgad and Purandar allowed Shivaji to establish a network of strongholds for Swaraj.
Shivaji’s treaties with Adilshah were strategic, allowing him to focus on other enemies while maintaining peace with the Adilshah.
Veermata Jijabai’s support was crucial in Shivaji’s early life, providing education, training and moral guidance.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was a brave king who fought against the Mughals and the Adilshahi to protect his Swaraj (self‑rule).
He captured many forts such as Chakan, Purandar, Rajgad, Sinhgad, and later Jinji in Tamil Nadu.
The Mughals, led by Aurangzeb, tried to stop him by sending armies and even putting him under house arrest in Agra.
Shivaji escaped from Agra with the help of his friend Moropant Pingale and returned to Maharashtra.
He fought the Mughals in several battles: the raid on Lal Mahal, the campaign to Surat, and the battle at Vani‑Dindori.
In 1665 he signed the Treaty of Purandar with the Mughals, giving them 23 forts but keeping most of his own.  He later broke the treaty to regain the forts.
Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati (king) on 6 June 1674 at Raigad, a ceremony that symbolised his sovereignty.  He had a second coronation on 24 September 1674.
The coronation used both Vedic and Tantric rituals and a special throne made of gold and precious jewels.
After the coronation, Shivaji launched a southern campaign, capturing forts like Jinji and Vellore, which helped him control parts of Tamil Nadu.
He died on 3 April 1680 at Raigad.  His younger brother Rajaram later became king and had to flee to southern forts for safety.
Shivaji’s courage and strategies inspired many Maratha leaders such as Tanaji Malusare, Moropant Pingale, and Prataprao Gujar.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Shivaji Maharaj founded Swaraj and crowned himself king to establish independent rule.
He formed a Council of Eight Ministers (Ashtapradhan Mandal) to manage different departments like finance, agriculture, army, foreign affairs, justice, religion, etc.

Each minister had a specific title: Pradhan (chief), Amatya (finance), Sachiv (secretary), Waknis (correspondence), Senapati (army commander), Dabir (foreign affairs), Nyayadhish (justice), Panditrao (religion).
The Ashtapradhan Mandal was responsible for collecting revenue, maintaining order, and administering conquered territories.
Shivaji’s administration emphasized agriculture as the main occupation and paid farmers for land cultivation and provided bullocks, ploughs, and seeds.
He introduced a feudal system where land was given as jagirs to nobles and soldiers in return for service, but he also kept a strong central control over revenue and land use.
The army was divided into infantry and cavalry; the cavalry had Shiledars (horsemen) and Bargirs (village soldiers).
He built many forts on hilltops and sea forts like Sindhudurg to protect the kingdom and control trade routes.
A dedicated intelligence department, headed by Bahirji Naik, gathered information about enemy movements, especially regarding salt trade from Portuguese territories.
Shivaji’s navy had around 400 ships, including warships like Gurab, Galbat, and Pal. He built sea forts and maintained naval bases to secure the western coast.
He protected the salt industry in Konkan by monitoring Portuguese salt imports and encouraging local salt production.
Shivaji’s policies aimed at welfare: he paid farmers, protected merchants, and ensured justice and religious affairs were managed by appointed officials.
The administration was efficient, with a system of revenue collection, land management, and military organization that kept the Swaraj stable.

Key terms: Swaraj (self-rule), Ashtapradhan Mandal (Council of Eight Ministers), Jagir (land grant), Shiledar (horseman), Bargir (village soldier), Sarnobat (chief officer), Bahirji Naik (intelligence chief).
Shivaji’s governance model combined strong central authority with local administration, ensuring both military strength and economic prosperity.
The forts and navy were crucial for defense and trade control, making Swaraj a formidable power in the region.
Shivaji’s administration is studied as an example of early modern statecraft in India.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was a 17th‑century ruler who founded the Maratha Empire, also called Swaraj (self‑rule).
He fought against the Mughals, Adilshahi, Siddis and Portuguese, winning many fort battles such as Panhala, Sinhagad and Sinhagad.
Shivaji’s administration was based on the principles of justice, equality and welfare of the people (ryots).
He paid soldiers on time and maintained strict discipline in the army. Soldiers were forbidden from looting or harming civilians.
Shivaji followed a tolerant religious policy – he respected mosques, temples and churches and allowed people of all faiths to practice freely.
He introduced the jagir system to reward soldiers and officers with land, but ensured that the revenue went to the state.
Shivaji’s leadership qualities included courage, intelligence, foresight, organisational skill and a strong sense of duty.
He encouraged his associates to be loyal, brave and to sacrifice for the welfare of the state.
Shivaji’s navy was built to protect the coast and to counter foreign invasions; he built forts like Sindhudurg.
He inspired other leaders such as Chhatrasal and later freedom fighters like Mahatma Gandhi and Jotirao Phule.

notes: The Maratha War of Independence was fought after the death of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
Sambhaji Maharaj became the second Chhatrapati and led the war against the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
The war lasted about 27 years (1657‑1684) and is also called the ‘Maratha War of Independence’.
Sambhaji fought many battles, including the siege of Ramsej fort near Nashik and the attack on Goa against the Portuguese.
He was captured and executed by Aurangzeb on 11 March 1689, but his death did not end the war.
After Sambhaji’s death, Rajaram Maharaj became the third Chhatrapati and continued the struggle from the fortified city of Raigad.
Rajaram escaped from Raigad to the stronghold of Jinji and used guerrilla tactics to harass Mughal forces.
Maharani Tarabai, Rajaram’s wife, took charge of the administration and led the Marathas after Rajaram’s death.
Tarabai’s ‘Safe Deposit Locker’ system helped the Marathas win back forts that were surrendered to the Mughals.
The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb could not capture all Maratha forts because of their strong fortifications and the Marathas’ mobility.
The war ended with Aurangzeb’s death in 1707, after which the Marathas gained control over most of western and central India.
Key figures: Sambhaji Maharaj, Rajaram Maharaj, Maharani Tarabai, Santaji Ghorpade, Dhanaji Jadhav, Hambirrao Mohite.
Important forts: Raigad, Ramsej, Goa, Jinji, Panhala, Satara.
The Marathas used a mix of conventional battles and surprise attacks to keep the Mughals on the defensive.
The war demonstrated the Marathas’ determination to maintain Swaraj (self‑rule) against a powerful empire.
The Maratha War of Independence is celebrated as a symbol of resistance and self‑reliance in Maharashtra history.

quiz.explain: She used a ‘Safe Deposit Locker’ system, bribing the Mughal kiledar to hand over the fort.

quiz.explain: The war effectively ended with Aurangzeb’s death in 1707.

quiz.explain: Santaji Ghorpade was famous for surprise attacks and guerrilla warfare.

quiz.explain: The forts were well‑built and difficult for the Mughals to capture.

quiz.explain: Marathas rarely used diplomacy; they relied on warfare and mobility.

notes: मराठ्यांनी १७१०‑१७११ मध्ये मुघलांच्या विरोधात स्वातंत्र्यसंग्राम सुरू केला आणि स्वतःला शासक घोषित केले.
शाहू महाराजांना मुघलांनी कैद केले होते, परंतु १७१३ मध्ये त्यांना मुक्त करण्यात आले.
शाहू महाराजांनी मराठ्यांच्या मदतीने पुणे व आसपासच्या प्रदेशावर नियंत्रण मिळवले.
बाळाजी विश्‍वनाथ हे शाहू महाराजांचे प्रमुख सहकारी होते आणि त्यांनी निजाम-उल-मुल्कची सत्ता घेतली.
बुंदेलखंड व माळवा प्रदेशात बाजीराव (पहिला) यांनी मराठ्यांचे वर्चस्व प्रस्थापित केले.
चौथाई म्हणजे महसुली उत्पन्नाचा एक चतुर्थांश; सरदेशमुखी म्हणजे एक दशांश भाग.
मालव व बुंदेलखंडात बाजीरावाने मुघलांच्या विरोधात यशस्वी मोहिमा केल्या.
भोपाळ व वसई किल्ल्यांवर पोर्तुगीजांचा पराभव बाजीराव आणि चिमाजी यांनी केला.
महाराणी ताराबाई यांनी शाहू महाराजांना छत्रपतीपदावर नेमले आणि मराठ्यांना समर्थन दिले.
महाराजांच्या काळात मराठ्यांनी दक्षिण भारतातही आपला विस्तार केला.

subject: History & Civics
notes: राष्ट्ररक्षक मराठे म्हणजे मराठा साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख शौर्यवान सरदार ज्यांनी भारताच्या उत्तर भागात मुघल व अफगाणांच्या आक्रमणांना तोंड दिले.
बाळाजी बाजीराव (पहिला) आणि नानासाहेब (दुसरा) हे प्रमुख पेशवे होते ज्यांनी मराठा वर्चस्व वाढवले.
नानासाहेबने १७५१ मध्ये पंजाबवर आक्रमण केले आणि १७५२ मध्ये अब्दालीशी करार केला.
अब्दाली (अहमद शाह अब्दाली) हा मुघल साम्राज्याचा बादशाह होता ज्याने मराठ्यांना पराभूत करण्याचा प्रयत्न केला.
पानिपतची लढाई १७६१ मध्ये झाली ज्यात मराठ्यांना पराभव झाला आणि पानिपतचा ताबा गमावला.
माधवराव पेशवा (१७५८-१७६०) यांनी मराठा वर्चस्व पुनर्स्थापित करण्याचा प्रयत्न केला.
सदाशिवरावभाऊने दिल्ली जिंकली परंतु नंतर पराभव झाला.
हैदरअली (इ.स.१७८२) आणि टिपू सुलतान (इ.स.१७९९) हे मराठा वर्चस्वावर प्रभाव टाकणारे प्रमुख शासक होते.
मराठा सैन्याने अफगाण व मुघल सैन्याशी लढाईत शौर्य दाखवले परंतु अनेकदा पराभव झाला.
पानिपतच्या लढाईनंतर मराठा वर्चस्व उत्तर भारतात कमी झाले परंतु पुणे दरबारात पुनः उभे राहिले.
मराठा साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख सरदार: शिंदे, होळकर, रामचंद्र कानडे, बिसाजीपंत, बिनिबाले इत्यादी.
मराठा साम्राज्याने १७५८ मध्ये ४००-६०० किमी विस्तार केला.
अफगाण व मुघल सैन्याने मराठा वर्चस्वाला आव्हान दिले.
मराठा वर्चस्वाचे संरक्षण करण्यासाठी मराठा सरदारांनी विविध मोहिमा केल्या.
मराठा साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख युद्ध: पानिपतची लढाई, बुराडी घाटची लढाई, राक्षसभुवनची लढाई इत्यादी.
मराठा साम्राज्याच्या इतिहासात पानिपतची लढाई एक महत्त्वपूर्ण वळण ठरली.
मराठा वर्चस्वाचे पुनर्स्थापन करण्यासाठी विविध सरदारांनी प्रयत्न केले.
मराठा साम्राज्याच्या इतिहासात पानिपतची लढाई व इतर लढाया महत्त्वपूर्ण आहेत.
मराठा साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख सरदार आणि त्यांच्या योगदानाची माहिती वाचकांना उपयुक्त ठरेल.

quiz.q: मराठ्यांचे पहिले प्रमुख पंतप्रधान कोण होते?
quiz.explain: नानासाहेब पेशवा हे मराठ्यांचे पहिले पंतप्रधान होते.

quiz.q: इ.स. १७५१ मध्ये कोणत्या प्रदेशावर अब्दालीने आक्रमण केले?
quiz.explain: अब्दालीने इ.स. १७५१ मध्ये पंजाबवर आक्रमण केले.

quiz.q: पानिपतच्या तिसऱ्या लढाईत मराठ्यांचा पराभव कोणत्या सैन्याने केला?
quiz.explain: पानिपतच्या तिसऱ्या लढाईत मराठ्यांचा पराभव अब्दालीच्या सैन्याने केला.

quiz.q: सर्वात मोठा मराठा सरदार कोण होता?
quiz.explain: सदाशिवरावभाऊ हे सर्वात मोठे मराठा सरदार होते.

quiz.q: अब्दालीने मराठ्यांना कोणत्या प्रदेशात मदत करण्यास नकार दिला?
quiz.explain: अब्दालीने मराठ्यांना उत्तर भारतात मदत करण्यास नकार दिला.

quiz.q: इ.स. १७५८ मध्ये कोणत्या युद्धात दत्ताजीने शौर्य दाखवले?
quiz.explain: दत्ताजीने पानिपतच्या युद्धात शौर्य दाखवले.

quiz.q: माधवराव पेशव्यांनी कोणत्या सुधारणा केल्या?
quiz.explain: माधवराव पेशव्यांनी दारूगोळा कारखाने सुरू केले.

quiz.q: अब्दालीच्या मृत्यूची तारीख कोणती?
quiz.explain: अब्दालीचा मृत्यू इ.स. १७८२ मध्ये झाला.

quiz.q: पानिपतच्या लढाईत मराठ्यांचा पराभव झाल्यानंतर कोणत्या शहरावर नियंत्रण मिळाले?
quiz.explain: पानिपतच्या लढाईत मराठ्यांचा पराभव झाल्यानंतर पानिपतवर नियंत्रण मिळाले.

quiz.q: इंग्रजी सैन्याने मराठ्यांशी कोणत्या वर्षी युद्ध केले?
quiz.explain: इंग्रजी सैन्याने मराठ्यांशी इ.स. १७९९ मध्ये युद्ध केले.

subject: History & Civics
notes: साम्राज्याची वाटचाल म्हणजे मराठा साम्राज्याचा इतिहास आणि त्याची वाढ-घट.
मराठा साम्राज्याची सुरुवात शिवाजी महाराजांनी केली आणि नंतर पानिपतच्या युद्धानंतर त्याची शक्ती कमी झाली.
इंदौरचे होळकर, नाना फडणवीस, ग्वालियरचे शिंदे, गायकवाड हे प्रमुख सरदार होते.
इंदौरचे होळकर यांनी मराठा सत्तेची पुनःस्थापना केली आणि दिल्लीच्या बादशाहाला गादीवर परत आणले.
नाना फडणवीस यांनी दक्षिण भारतात मराठा सत्तेचा विस्तार केला.
ग्वालियरचे शिंदे यांनी ओडिशा व बंगालमध्ये मराठा प्रभाव वाढवला.
गायकवाड यांनी इंग्रजांना धान्यसामग्री न दिल्याने मराठा-इंग्रज संघर्ष तीव्र झाला.
शिवाजी महाराजांनी आरमार उभारला ज्याने मराठा सत्तेला मदत केली.
इंग्रजांनी १८१७ मध्ये पुणे ताब्यात घेतल्यावर मराठा सत्तेचा अंत झाला.
मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनाचे मुख्य कारण म्हणजे आंतरिक वाद आणि इंग्रजांचा दबाव.
माल्हारराव होळकर यांनी उत्तर भारतात मराठा प्रतिष्ठा पुनःस्थापित केली.
पानिपतच्या युद्धात मराठा सैन्याची शक्ती कमी झाली.
साम्राज्याच्या विस्तारात शेतकरी, कर, व्यापार आणि तलाव-आढावा महत्त्वाचे होते.
माल्हारराव होळकर यांनी शेतकऱ्यांना विहिरी खोदून मदत केली.
मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनानंतर भारतात ब्रिटिश राजवट स्थापन झाली.
मराठा सरदारांनी विविध प्रदेशात प्रशासन व लष्करी कार्य केले.
मराठा सत्तेच्या काळात गनिमी काव्याची पद्धत वापरली.
शिवाजी महाराजांनी आरमाराने समुद्रावर नियंत्रण ठेवले.
इंदौरचे होळकर यांनी धर्मस्थळांची सेवा केली.
नाना फडणवीस यांनी दक्षिणेतील राजकारणाची सूत्रे सांभाळली.
ग्वालियरचे शिंदे यांनी ओडिशा व बंगालमध्ये मराठा प्रभाव वाढवला.
गायकवाड यांनी इंग्रजांना धान्यसामग्री न दिल्याने संघर्ष तीव्र झाला.
मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनानंतर ब्रिटिशांनी भारतावर नियंत्रण घेतले.
मराठा सत्तेच्या इतिहासात विविध सरदारांनी योगदान दिले.
मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनानंतर भारतीय समाजव्यवस्थेत बदल झाले.

quiz.q: इंदौरचे होळकर यांनी मराठा सत्तेची पुनःस्थापना कशात केली?
quiz.explain: होळकरांनी दिल्लीच्या बादशाहाला गादीवर परत आणले.

quiz.q: पानिपतच्या युद्धानंतर मराठा साम्राज्याची शक्ती कशी बदलली?
quiz.explain: युद्धानंतर मराठा सैन्याची शक्ती कमी झाली.

quiz.q: ग्वालियरचे शिंदे कोणत्या प्रदेशात मराठा प्रभाव वाढवले?
quiz.explain: शिंदे यांनी ओडिशा व बंगालमध्ये मराठा प्रभाव वाढवला.

quiz.q: मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनाचे मुख्य कारण काय होते?
quiz.explain: आंतरिक वाद आणि इंग्रजांचा दबाव.

quiz.q: शिवाजी महाराजांनी कोणती पद्धत वापरून समुद्रावर नियंत्रण ठेवले?
quiz.explain: आरमारने समुद्रावर नियंत्रण ठेवले.

quiz.q: नाना फडणवीस यांनी दक्षिण भारतात काय केले?
quiz.explain: दक्षिण भारतात मराठा सत्तेचा विस्तार केला.

quiz.q: गायकवाड यांनी इंग्रजांना काय न दिल्याने संघर्ष तीव्र झाला?
quiz.explain: धान्यसामग्री न दिल्याने संघर्ष वाढला.

quiz.q: इंग्रजांनी १८१७ मध्ये कोणते शहर ताब्यात घेतले?
quiz.explain: पुणे ताब्यात घेतले.

quiz.q: मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनानंतर भारतात कोणती राजवट स्थापन झाली?
quiz.explain: ब्रिटिश राजवट स्थापन झाली.

quiz.q: माल्हारराव होळकर यांनी शेतकऱ्यांना काय मदत केली?
quiz.explain: विहिरी खोदून मदत केली.

subject: History & Civics
notes: 1. महाराष्ट्रातील समाजजीवन हे प्रामुख्याने ग्रामीण व शहरी भागात विभागलेले आहे.
2. गावात बहुतेक लोक स्वयंपूर्ण असत – शेती, पशुपालन व हस्तकला.
3. प्रमुख धान्ये: ज्वारी, बाजरी, गहू, तांदूळ, मका.
4. शेतकरी व गावकरी यांच्याकडे पाट, पाटलाकडे, पाटिलकी यांसारखी साधने होती.
5. गावातील घरांची रचना: एकमजली व दुमजली वाडे, साधी माती-गोट्यांची भिंती.
6. पोशाख: पुरुष लुगडी व चोळी, स्त्रिया अंगरखा व मुंडासे.
7. सण-उत्सव: गुढीपाडवा, नागपंचमी, बैलपोळा, दिवाळी, होळी, ईद, गणेशोत्सव.
8. बालविवाह व बहुपत्नित्व या काळात प्रचलित अनिष्ट चालीरिती होत्या.
9. शिक्षण: पाठशाळा व मदरसा, लेखन व वाचन शिकवले जात.
10. दानधर्म व धार्मिक अनुष्ठाने समाजात महत्त्वाची भूमिका बजावतात.
11. दळणवळण: घाटमार्ग, सडक व नद्यांवरील पूल, होड्या.
12. खेळ: कुस्ती, लाठी, दंडपट्टा, बुद्धिबळ, खोखो, आट्यापाट्या.
13. महिलांचे जीवन: पाठीवरून वाहून नेणे, होड्यांवर प्रवास, शिक्षणाची कमी.
14. महाराष्ट्रातील धार्मिक विविधता: हिंदू व मुस्लिम दोन्ही प्रमुख धर्म.
15. शिल्पकला व वास्तुकला: पाटलाकडे, गंगाराम, नाशिकचे मंदिर, पाटलाकडे वाडे.
16. समाजातील समता व लोकशाहीचे महत्त्व २०व्या शतकात वाढले.
17. संविधानाची ओळख व मूलभूत हक्कांची माहिती महत्त्वाची.
18. समाजात समतेची गरज व लिंगभेदावर चर्चा आवश्यक.
19. स्थानिक शासन व राज्यशासन यांतील फरक समजणे आवश्यक.
20. संविधानातील मार्गदर्शक तत्त्वे व मूलभूत कर्तव्ये यांचा अभ्यास करणे.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख धान्ये कोणती आहेत?
quiz.explain: गावात ज्वारी, बाजरी, गहू व तांदूळ हे प्रमुख धान्ये आहेत.

quiz.q: गावातील प्रमुख पोशाख कोणते?
quiz.explain: पुरुष लुगडी व चोळी परिधान करतात.

quiz.q: सण-उत्सवांमध्ये गणेशोत्सव कसा साजरा केला जातो?
quiz.explain: गणेशोत्सव प्रामुख्याने घरगुती स्वरूपात साजरा केला जातो.

quiz.q: बालविवाह व बहुपत्नित्व या काळात प्रचलित अनिष्ट चालीरिती होत्या. यापैकी कोणती चालीरिती नव्हती?
quiz.explain: सामाजिक समता या काळात नव्हती.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख धर्म कोणते?
quiz.explain: हिंदू व मुस्लिम हे प्रमुख धर्म आहेत.

quiz.q: शिक्षण पद्धतीत कोणते शाळा होते?
quiz.explain: पाठशाळा व मदरसा हे प्रमुख शिक्षणस्थळ होते.

quiz.q: खेळांमध्ये कोणते खेळ प्रचलित होते?
quiz.explain: कुस्ती व बुद्धिबळ हे प्रमुख खेळ होते.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्रातील दळणवळणाचे प्रमुख माध्यम कोणते?
quiz.explain: घाटमार्ग व होड्या हे प्रमुख दळणवळणाचे माध्यम होते.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्रातील समाजजीवनात समतेची गरज कधी वाढली?
quiz.explain: लोकशाही व समतेची गरज २०व्या शतकात वाढली.

quiz.q: संविधानातील मार्गदर्शक तत्त्वे व मूलभूत कर्तव्ये यांचा अभ्यास का महत्त्वाचा?
quiz.explain: संविधानातील तत्त्वे सर्वांना समान हक्क व कर्तव्ये देतात.

subject: History & Civics
notes: संविधान म्हणजे देशाच्या राज्यकारभाराचे नियम लिहिलेले दस्तऐवज आहे.
संविधानात मूलभूत अधिकार, मूलभूत कर्तव्ये, मार्गदर्शक तत्त्वे आणि शासनाची रचना यांचा उल्लेख असतो.
संविधानाची प्रमुख वैशिष्ट्ये – लिखित, सार्वभौम, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, समाजवादी, लोकशाही गणराज्य.
संविधानाची प्रस्तावना (उद्‌देशिका) मध्ये ‘सर्व नागरिकांना समान हक्क, समान संधी आणि बंधुभाव’ यांचा उल्लेख आहे.
संविधानात ‘सर्वसाधारण अधिकार’ (उदा. जीवन, स्वातंत्र्य, समानता) व ‘विशेष अधिकार’ (उदा. शिक्षण, आरोग्य) दोन्ही आहेत.
संविधानात ‘मूलभूत कर्तव्ये’ देखील नमूद आहेत – देशभक्ती, शाळा वाचन, पर्यावरण संरक्षण इत्यादी.
संविधानाची रचना – प्रस्तावना, मूलभूत तत्त्वे, अधिकार व कर्तव्ये, शासनाची रचना, न्यायव्यवस्था, दुरुस्ती प्रक्रिया.
संविधानातील ‘मूलभूत अधिकार’ – जीवन व स्वातंत्र्य, समानता, धर्मनिरपेक्षता, अभिव्यक्ती स्वातंत्र्य, शिक्षणाचा अधिकार, आरोग्याचा अधिकार इत्यादी.
संविधानातील ‘मूलभूत कर्तव्ये’ – देशभक्ती, शाळा वाचन, संविधान वाचणे, पर्यावरण संरक्षण, कायद्याचे पालन इत्यादी.
संविधानाची दुरुस्ती प्रक्रिया – संसद, राज्यसभा, संविधान आयोग, बहुमत मत इत्यादी.
संविधानाच्या ‘मार्गदर्शक तत्त्वे’ – समाजवादी राज्य, धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य, लोकशाही गणराज्य, बंधुभाव, समान कामासाठी समान वेतन इत्यादी.
संविधानात ‘संघराज्य’ – केंद्र व राज्य सरकार यांच्यात अधिकारांचे वाटप (उदा. संरक्षण, परराष्ट्र व्यवहार – केंद्र; शेती, शिक्षण – राज्य).
संविधानात ‘संघराज्य’ मध्ये ‘शेषाधिकार’ – केंद्र सरकारकडे असलेले विशेष अधिकार.
संविधानात ‘निवडणूक आयोग’ – स्वतंत्र संस्था जी निवडणुका न्याय्य व पारदर्शक पद्धतीने घेते.
संविधानात ‘न्यायव्यवस्था’ – स्वतंत्र न्यायालये, न्यायाधीशांची नियुक्ती व संरक्षण.
संविधानात ‘सार्वजनिक स्वच्छता अभियान’ – ‘स्वच्छ भारत’ इत्यादी उपक्रमांचा उल्लेख.
संविधानात ‘समान कामासाठी समान वेतन’ – लिंग, वंश, धर्म इत्यादींवर आधारित भेदभाव न करता वेतन ठरवणे.
संविधानात ‘धर्मनिरपेक्षता’ – कोणत्याही धर्माला राज्याचा धर्म मानू नये व धार्मिक कर लावू नये.
संविधानात ‘सर्वसाधारण अधिकार’ – नागरिकांना कोणत्याही धर्म, जाती, लिंग इत्यादींवर आधारित भेदभाव न करता समान वागणूक.
संविधानात ‘सामाजिक न्याय’ – गरीब-श्रीमंत यांच्यात दरी कमी करणे व सर्वांना समान संधी देणे.
संविधानात ‘परराष्ट्र धोरण’ – जागतिक शांतता व सहकार्य यावर आधारित.
संविधानात ‘सर्वसाधारण शिक्षण’ – ६ ते १४ वर्षे मोफत व सक्तीचे शिक्षण.

quiz.q: संविधानात कोणते अधिकार समाविष्ट आहेत?

subject: History & Civics
notes: शिवपूर्वकालीन भारत म्हणजे इ.स. १२०० पूर्वीचा काळ, ज्यात विविध राजवंशांची सत्ता होती.
यादव राजवंशाची सत्ता महाराष्ट्रात ११व्या शतकात होती.
गुर्जर-प्रतिहार वायव्येकडील आक्रमणांनी आंध्र, कलिंग, विदर्भ इत्यादी राज्यांवर प्रभाव टाकला.
पृथ्वीराज चौहान हे चौहान राजवंशाचे प्रमुख होते आणि त्यांनी मुहम्मद घोरीचा पराभव केला.
मुहम्मद घोरीने ११व्या शतकात भारतात आक्रमण करून सिंध, तमिळनाडू इत्यादी प्रदेश जिंकले.
कृष्ण तिसरा आणि महमूद गझनी यांनी भारतात अनेक स्वारी केल्या.
बाह्मनी आणि विजयनगर हे दक्षिण भारतातील प्रमुख राज्ये होती.
बाह्मनी राज्याची स्थापना १३३६ मध्ये झाली आणि त्याचे प्रमुख सुलतान बहमनी होते.
विजयनगर राज्याची सत्ता १३४७ मध्ये सुरू झाली आणि १५३० मध्ये समाप्त झाली.
मुघल सत्तेची स्थापना बाबरने १५२६ मध्ये केली.
अकबर, हुमायून, शेरशाह, आणिंगजेब हे मुघल साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख सुलतान होते.
अकबराने पानिपतची लढाई (१५५६) आणि पानिपतची दुसरी लढाई (१५५६) लढून मुघल साम्राज्याचे क्षेत्र वाढवले.
महाराणा प्रताप, चांदबिबी, राणी दुर्गावती हे शिख, मराठा आणि आहोम यांच्या संघर्षात महत्त्वाचे होते.
सुलतान शाही, निजामशाही, कुतुबशाही इत्यादी विविध उपराज्ये मुघल साम्राज्याखाली आली.
मुघल साम्राज्याच्या पतनानंतर भारतात विविध स्वायत्त राज्ये उभी राहिली.
शिवपूर्वकालीन भारतात राजकीय, सांस्कृतिक आणि धार्मिक विविधता होती.
यादव राजवंशाची राजधानी घोरी होती.
बाह्मनी आणि विजयनगर राज्यांनी दक्षिण भारतात आपली सत्ता स्थापन केली.
मुघल साम्राज्याने भारतात तोफखाना आणि प्रशासनिक सुधारणा आणल्या.
महाराणा प्रतापाने दीन-इ-इलाही धर्माची स्थापना केली.
शाही आणि उपराज्यांच्या संघर्षामुळे भारतात विविध राजकीय बदल झाले.

quiz.explain: पृथ्वीराज चौहान यांनी मुहम्मद घोरीचा पराभव केला.

quiz.q: बाह्मनी राज्याची स्थापना कोणत्या वर्षी झाली?
quiz.explain: बाह्मनी राज्याची स्थापना १३३६ मध्ये झाली.

quiz.q: मुघल साम्राज्याची स्थापना करणारा शासक कोण होता?
quiz.explain: बाबरने १५२६ मध्ये मुघल साम्राज्याची स्थापना केली.

quiz.q: पानिपतची दुसरी लढाई कोणत्या वर्षी झाली?
quiz.explain: पानिपतची दुसरी लढाई १५५६ मध्ये झाली.

quiz.q: महाराणा प्रताप कोणत्या युद्धात धैर्य दाखवले?
quiz.explain: महाराणा प्रतापाने अकबराविरुद्ध लढाईत धैर्य दाखवले.

quiz.q: विजयनगर राज्याची सत्ता कधी समाप्त झाली?
quiz.explain: विजयनगर राज्याची सत्ता १५३० मध्ये समाप्त झाली.

quiz.q: शाही, निजामशाही, कुतुबशाही हे कोणत्या काळात अस्तित्वात होते?
quiz.explain: हे उपराज्ये मुघल काळात अस्तित्वात होती.

quiz.q: कृष्ण तिसरा आणि महमूद गझनी यांनी भारतात काय केले?
quiz.explain: कृष्ण तिसरा आणि महमूद गझनी यांनी भारतात सैन्य स्वारी केल्या.

quiz.q: राणा प्रतापाने कोणता धर्म स्थापन केला?
quiz.explain: राणा प्रतापाने दीन-इ-इलाही धर्माची स्थापना केली.

subject: History & Civics
notes: भक्ती चळवळ म्हणजे भक्ती आणि प्रेमावर आधारित धार्मिक चळवळ जी मध्ययुगीन भारतात उद्भवली.
भक्ती चळवळीचे प्रमुख तत्त्वे: एकेश्वरवाद, जातिभेद व पंथभेदाचा नकार, सर्वसामान्यांच्या भाषेचा वापर.
संत कबीर, रामानंद, चैतन्य महाप्रभू, नायनार, अळवार, मीराबाई, शंकरदेव, गुरुनानक, शेख महंमद हे प्रमुख संत आहेत.
भक्ती चळवळीने विविध धर्मांमध्ये समन्वय साधला – हिंदू, मुस्लिम, शीख, सुफी इत्यादी.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी लोकभाषेत भजन, गीते आणि ग्रंथ लिहिले ज्यामुळे सामान्य लोकांना धार्मिक शिक्षण सोपे झाले.
संतांनी धर्मभेद, जातिभेद व पंथभेद नाकारून सर्वांना समान मानले.
भक्ती चळवळीने सामाजिक समरसता आणि सहिष्णुता वाढवली.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी विविध प्रदेशांमध्ये पंथांचा प्रसार केला – महाराष्ट्र, कर्नाटक, गुजरात, बंगाल, उत्तर भारत इत्यादी.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी धर्मग्रंथांची अनुवाद आणि संकलन केले – रामचरितमानस, सूरसागर, परमरहस्य इत्यादी.
भक्ती चळवळीने संगीत, नृत्य आणि नाटक यांचा विकास केला – सुफी संगीत, भजन, भजनगायन इत्यादी.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी समाजातील सर्व वर्गांना समाविष्ट केले – स्त्री-पुरुष, जाती, वर्ग इत्यादी.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी धर्मग्रंथांना लोकभाषेत लिहून सामान्य लोकांना समजण्यास सोपे केले.
भक्ती चळवळीने धार्मिक समन्वय साधला – हिंदू-मुस्लिम, शीख-मुस्लिम, सुफी-हिंदू इत्यादी.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी धार्मिक ग्रंथांमध्ये प्रेम, दया आणि सहिष्णुतेचा संदेश दिला.
भक्ती चळवळीने भारतीय धर्मजीवनात धर्मभेद व जातिभेदावर मात करण्यास मदत केली.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी धार्मिक ग्रंथांच्या माध्यमातून समाजात बदल घडवले.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी धर्मग्रंथांमध्ये सर्वसामान्यांना समजणारी भाषा वापरली.
भक्ती चळवळीने धार्मिक समन्वयाच्या दृष्टीने विविध पंथांना एकत्र आणले.
भक्ती चळवळीतील संतांनी धर्मग्रंथांमध्ये प्रेम आणि एकतेचा संदेश दिला.
भक्ती चळवळीने धार्मिक समन्वयाच्या दृष्टीने समाजात सहिष्णुता वाढवली

quiz.q: भक्ती चळवळीचा प्रमुख संदेश काय होता?
quiz.explain: भक्ती चळवळीने सर्व जाती-धर्मांना समान प्रेम आणि समता शिकवली.

quiz.q: संत कबीर यांनी कोणत्या तत्त्वावर भर दिला?
quiz.explain: कबीरने सर्व मनुष्यांना एकच मानले आणि समानतेचा संदेश दिला.

quiz.q: चैतन्य महाप्रभू यांनी कोणत्या भाषेत कृष्णभक्तीचा प्रसार केला?
quiz.explain: चैतन्य महाप्रभू यांनी बंगाली भाषेत कृष्णभक्तीचे उपदेश दिले.

quiz.q: संत मीराबाई यांनी कोणत्या धर्माचे महत्त्व सांगितले?
quiz.explain: मीराबाईने हिंदू धर्मातील कृष्णभक्तीचा प्रसार केला.

quiz.q: संत शेख महंमद यांनी कोणता ग्रंथ प्रसिद्ध केला?

notes: Be the best means doing your best in whatever role you have, not just the most important one.

subject: English
notes: 1. A *Raag* (or *Raga*) is a set of notes used in Indian classical music, sung or played in a fixed combination of 5 to 6 basic notes.
2. A *Raga* is performed at specific times or occasions, e.g., Raag Malkauns is often sung at late night.
3. Musical instruments can be grouped as Indian (e.g., Tabla, Tanpura, Sitar) and Western (e.g., Drum, Piano, Violin).
4. Folk music is simple, often passed down orally, and reflects local culture; classical music is structured, follows strict rules and is taught in schools.
5. The story of Tansen and Emperor Akbar shows respect for a Guru and the idea that true music comes from the soul, not from external praise.
6. In the story, Sant Haridas is a humble teacher who refuses to sing for the emperor, showing humility.
7. The emperor Akbar is portrayed as a kind and open-minded ruler, different from other rulers who might be angry if a musician refuses.
8. A *phrase* is a group of words that does not contain a subject or main verb; a *clause* contains a subject and a main verb.
9. The sentence “The musician laid his tanpura on the carpet” is a phrase because it lacks a main verb for the subject.
10. The sentence “There is someone who sings far better” contains a clause because it has a subject and a verb.
11. True/False: “He had been Tansen’s music teacher and he lived the life of a hermit” – this is a clause.
12. The story encourages students to ask questions, write sentences, and create plays based on the narrative.
13. Vocabulary: *exquisite* (very fine), *exasperated* (irritated), *hypnotised* (captured attention), *divine* (like God).
14. Matching exercise: Identify sentence types – exclamatory, interrogative, statement, imperative, negative.
15. Activity: Collect stories of Akbar and Birbal to practice reading and presentation skills.

options: A fixed combination of 5 to 6 notes
quiz.explain: A Raag is a melodic framework using 5-6 basic notes.

quiz.q: Which instrument is NOT an Indian classical instrument?
quiz.explain: Piano is a Western instrument.

quiz.explain: Sant Haridas is Tansen’s music teacher.

quiz.explain: Akbar admires Tansen’s singing.

options: I am long past the age for singing.
quiz.explain: Exclamatory sentences end with an exclamation mark.

options: He is a humble lover of music
quiz.explain: Tansen says he will sing only for a guru.

options: A phrase has a subject, a clause does not
A clause has a subject and verb, a phrase does not
quiz.explain: A clause contains a subject and verb; a phrase does not.

quiz.explain: All three sentences are true.

quiz.explain: Exasperated means very irritated.

options: Drawing a picture of a musician

quiz.explain: The chapter suggests collecting Akbar and Birbal stories.

subject: English
notes: - The Two Gentlemen of Verona is a short story by A.J. Cronin about two brothers, Nicola and Jacopo, who work hard to pay for their sister’s tuberculosis treatment.
- The narrator meets the brothers first when he sees them selling wild strawberries and later when they are shining shoes in a public square.
- The brothers do odd jobs like selling newspapers, shining shoes, and helping the narrator in various ways.
- They wish to visit the village Poleta to get a lift for their sister’s treatment.
- The story shows that even after war and loss, the brothers remain determined and self‑less, illustrating the proverb ‘Where there is a will there’s a way.’
- Key terms: narrator, odd jobs, tuberculosis, war, will, way, self‑less, dedication.
- Important points for revision: focus on the brothers’ motivation, the narrator’s role, the setting (Alps, village), and the moral of the story.

notes: 1. A vet (veterinarian) is a doctor who treats animals and birds.

subject: English
chapter: 4.2 P. V. Sindhu - An Icon of Success
notes: P. V. Sindhu is an Indian badminton player from Andhra Pradesh, born 1995.
She started playing badminton at age 8 after being inspired by Pullela Gopichand.
Her first major win was the 5th Servo All India Ranking Championship (under‑10).
She won the 2009 Sub‑Junior Asian Championships (bronze) and 2010 Uber Cup squad selection.
In 2012 she won the Asia Youth Under‑19 Championship and 2013 Malaysian Open Grand Prix Gold.
2013 she became the first Indian woman to win a World Badminton Championship medal (silver).
In 2015 she won the India Open Superseries title and received Padma Shri and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna awards.
2016 she won the silver medal at Rio Olympics, the first Indian woman to reach an Olympic badminton final.
She has won multiple Grand Prix Gold titles and is ranked in the world top 10.
Key traits: dedication, never‑say‑die spirit, strong work ethic, positive attitude.
Awards: Padma Shri (2015), Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2016).

quiz.explain: She received Padma Shri in 2015.

subject: English
notes: - Friendship is a golden chain that grows stronger with time.
- A true friend is like a precious jewel, more valuable than gold.
- Friendship cannot be bought or sold; it is priceless.
- The poem uses figurative language: simile, metaphor, antithesis, alliteration.
- Simile uses words like ‘like’ or ‘as’ to compare (e.g., ‘as bright as a star’).
- Metaphor compares without using ‘like’ or ‘as’ (e.g., ‘Riya is the star of our class’).
- Antithesis shows opposite ideas in the same line (e.g., ‘up and down the hill’).
- Alliteration repeats the same consonant sound at the start of words (e.g., ‘bright bright’).
- A golden chain symbolizes a strong, lasting bond.
- A precious jewel symbolizes rarity and beauty.
- A priceless gift symbolizes something that cannot be measured in money.
- True friendship lasts as long as memory lives.
- Friendship is a strong and blessed tie that binds kindred hearts.
- Friendship is compared to an evergreen forest, an ever-flowing river, and a rainbow after heavy rains to show its enduring nature.
- Acrostic poems use each letter of a name to start a line of praise.
- True friendship is a gift that grows more precious each year.
- The poem’s lines are examples of figurative language that enhance meaning.
- Remember to read the poem carefully before answering questions.
- The poem’s structure helps students identify different figures of speech.

quiz.q: Which figure of speech is used in the line ‘Twinkle Twinkle Little Star, like a Diamond in the sky’?
quiz.explain: The word ‘like’ indicates a simile.

quiz.explain: It compares time to money without using ‘like’ or ‘as’.

options: ‘Up and down the hill, they flew.’
‘The stormy sea, as dark as coal.’
‘Old mighty tree, your branches span the sky.’
quiz.explain: Opposite ideas ‘up’ and ‘down’ appear together.

quiz.q: True or False: Friendship can be bought or sold.
quiz.explain: The poem states friendship cannot be bought or sold.

quiz.q: What is friendship compared to in the poem?
quiz.explain: The poem explicitly says ‘Friendship is a golden chain’.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a figurative language used in the poem?
quiz.explain: The poem does not use personification.

quiz.q: The line ‘For as long as memory lives’ is an example of which figure of speech?
quiz.explain: The repeated ‘l’ sound is alliteration.

quiz.q: Which of these is a reason why friendship is the best gift?
options: It grows more precious as each year passes
It can be bought for a price
quiz.explain: The poem states it grows more precious.

quiz.q: Which statement is true about friendship according to the poem?
options: Friendship can be destroyed by time
Friendship is a real rare and precious jewel
quiz.explain: The poem compares it to a rare jewel.

quiz.q: Which figure of speech is used in ‘Friendship is a priceless gift’?
quiz.explain: It is a metaphor because no ‘like’ or ‘as’ is used.

subject: English
notes: The Titanic was the largest luxury ship in 1912 and was called ‘Titanic’ meaning huge.
It was called the unsinkable ship because builders believed it could never sink and only a few lifeboats were fitted.
The ship set sail on 10 April 1912 from Southampton to New York and carried more than 2,000 passengers.
On 14 April the ship struck an iceberg at 11:40 p.m. and water flooded the lower decks.
Captain Smith sent radio distress calls at 12:15 a.m.; the Carpathia reached the Titanic after 3 hours and rescued about 700 people.
Only 700 of the 2,200 passengers survived; about 1,500 people drowned.
After the sinking, regulations were changed: all ships must have enough lifeboats for everyone and keep radios on at all times.
In 1985 the wreck was found at a depth of about 4,000 m (13,000 ft) on the ocean floor.
A simile uses ‘as … as’ or ‘like’ to compare two different things, e.g. ‘as tall as a building’.
A compound word is formed by joining two words, e.g. ‘everything’ or ‘life‑skills’.
Root words are the base part of a word, e.g. ‘sink’ in ‘unsinkable’.
Prefixes add meaning before the root (anti‑, dis‑, non‑, re‑).
Suffixes add meaning after the root (‑ful, ‑ous, ‑less, ‑ly).
Simple sentence: one subject and one predicate (e.g. ‘They felt safe.’).
Complex sentence: one main clause + subordinate clause (e.g. ‘Captain Smith knew that there were icebergs nearby.’).
Compound sentence: two or more independent clauses joined by a coordinator (e.g. ‘He fought hard, but the ship changed direction slowly.’).
The Titanic’s unsinkability claim led to complacency and fewer lifeboats, contributing to the disaster.
The Carpathia’s late arrival was due to its distance and the fact that it was not on radio duty at the time.

quiz.q: What does the word ‘Titanic’ mean?
quiz.explain: Titanic means huge.

quiz.q: How many passengers did the Titanic carry?
quiz.explain: It carried more than two thousand passengers.

quiz.q: Why did people call the Titanic an unsinkable ship?
options: Because it was built with steel
Because builders believed it could never sink
Because it was the fastest ship
quiz.explain: Builders were sure it could never sink.

quiz.q: Which ship answered the Titanic’s distress calls?
quiz.explain: The Carpathia responded.

quiz.q: What was the depth of the Titanic wreck found in 1985?
quiz.explain: The wreck lies at about 4,000 m.

quiz.q: What is a simile?
options: A comparison using as…as or like
quiz.explain: Simile uses as…as or like.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a compound word?
quiz.explain: Every + thing = everything.

quiz.q: What does the prefix ‘anti‑’ mean?
quiz.explain: Anti‑ means against.

quiz.q: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
options: Captain Smith knew that there were icebergs nearby.
He fought hard, but the ship changed direction slowly.
Most passengers heard nothing and they slept on.
quiz.explain: It contains a main clause and a subordinate clause.

quiz.q: How many people survived the Titanic sinking?
quiz.explain: About 700 people were rescued.

subject: English
notes: Festivals are special days celebrated with joy and traditions.
In North East India, festivals are linked to agriculture and seasons.
Assam’s chief festival is Bihu, celebrated three times a year for sowing, harvesting and reaping.
Bihu dance is performed by young men and women with brisk steps and traditional instruments like dhol and pepa.
Arunachal Pradesh’s new year festival is called Losar; people clean homes and discard old items to welcome the new year.
Manipur’s Ningol Chakouba celebrates the bond between married girls and their parents with feasts and gifts.
Mizoram’s Spring Festival or Chapchar Kut is celebrated with folk dances and traditional songs.
Meghalaya’s Wangala is a harvest festival where men and women dance in parallel lines while beating drums.
Tripura’s festivals involve dances that represent hunting, fishing and food‑gathering.
Nagaland’s Moastu festival is celebrated after sowing season with colourful clothes and headgear.
Festivals in the seven states often involve music, dance, food, and a sense of community.
They help preserve oral history and cultural identity.
Festivals also bring out natural talent and encourage artistic activities.
Common features of festivals: music, dance, food, decorations, and communal participation.
Festivals are important for thanking gods, seeking protection, and celebrating harvests.

quiz.q: Which festival is celebrated three times a year in Assam to mark the stages of agriculture?
quiz.explain: Bihu has three sets marking sowing, harvesting and post-harvest.

quiz.q: The new year festival celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh is called?
quiz.explain: Losar is the New Year festival of Arunachal.

quiz.q: Which festival involves a hundred drums and is celebrated by the Garos of Meghalaya?
quiz.explain: Wangala is the hundred‑drum festival of the Garos.

quiz.q: In Tripura, the festivals’ dances represent which activities?
quiz.explain: Tripura dances depict hunting, fishing and food‑gathering.

quiz.q: The festival that revives the relationship between married girls and their parents is?
quiz.explain: Ningol Chakouba strengthens ties between married girls and parents.

quiz.q: Which instrument is a wind instrument made from a buffalo horn used in Bihu dance?
quiz.explain: Pepa is a buffalo‑horn wind instrument in Bihu.

quiz.q: The festival celebrated by the people of Manipur in April is called?
quiz.explain: Cheiraoba is Manipur’s New Year festival in April.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a common feature of all festival celebrations?
quiz.explain: Fireworks are not universal to all festivals.

quiz.q: The festival celebrated by the people of Mizoram is known as?
quiz.explain: Chapchar Kut is the Spring Festival of Mizoram.

quiz.q: Which festival is celebrated by people of all religions, castes and tribes in Assam?
quiz.explain: Bihu is celebrated by all groups in Assam.

subject: English
notes: - Androcles was a kind slave who escaped from a cruel master.
- He found a wounded lion in the forest and helped it by removing a thorn from its paw.
- The lion showed gratitude by licking Androcles’ arm and later by following him and sharing food.
- Soldiers captured both Androcles and the lion and put them in a cage in the city.
- In the emperor’s circus, the lion stopped attacking Androcles and instead petted him, showing friendship.
- The emperor was moved by this act and freed both Androcles and the lion.
- Lions are called the king of the jungle, belong to the cat family, are carnivorous, have a mane only on males, live in groups called a pride, and attack only when hungry.
- Key vocabulary: courteous, bound by law, clutches, coward, flee, piteously, moaned, cautiously, whimpered, distress, summoning up courage, intention.
- The story teaches that kindness and bravery can change hearts and earn freedom.

quiz.q: What did Androcles do when he found the lion wounded?
quiz.explain: Androcles carefully removed the thorn from the lion’s paw.

quiz.q: Why were slaves like Androcles forced to work?
quiz.explain: Slaves had no freedom or rights and were forced to obey their masters.

quiz.q: What is the correct term for a group of lions?
quiz.explain: A group of lions is called a pride.

quiz.q: Which word best describes the lion’s initial reaction to Androcles?
quiz.explain: The lion looked at Androcles piteously, showing pain.

quiz.q: What happened to Androcles in the emperor’s arena?
options: He was chained and then freed
quiz.explain: He was chained, then freed after the lion showed friendship.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a primary auxiliary verb?
quiz.explain: Can is a modal auxiliary, not a primary one.

quiz.q: How did the emperor reward Androcles?
quiz.explain: The emperor freed Androcles from slavery.

quiz.q: What does the word 'distress' mean?
quiz.explain: Distress means great trouble or pain.

quiz.q: Which sentence contains an auxiliary verb?
quiz.explain: ‘Can’ is an auxiliary verb.

quiz.q: What was the lion’s reaction after Androcles helped it?
quiz.explain: The lion licked Androcles’ arm to show gratitude.

subject: English
chapter: 1.3 Trees are the Kindest Things I Know
notes: Trees are the kindest things we know – they never hurt anyone.
They give shade, fruit, wood and firewood for cooking.
They help birds and animals by providing food, shelter and nesting places.
At sunrise the tree’s leaves catch the first rays of light.
At sunset the tree’s branches hold the last light of the day.
Trees are called harmless because they only grow and never attack.
During Halloween in the West it is autumn – leaves are burned to keep the forest clean and to celebrate the harvest.
People use trees for building houses, making paper, and as food sources.
Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen – they clean the air.
They also prevent soil erosion by holding the ground with their roots.
The poem “Trees are the kindest things I know” shows trees as gentle and caring.
The poem uses personification – trees are described as humming and singing lullabies.
The poem mentions trees giving fruit, wood, shade, and firewood for Halloween.
Trees are the first to greet the morning sun and the last to keep the evening light.
They are a symbol of patience, strength and kindness in many cultures.
The poem’s rhyme scheme is simple and easy to remember for children.
The poem teaches us to respect and protect trees for future generations.
Trees are a living part of the environment that supports many life forms.
They are also a source of medicine, food, and shelter for humans and animals.
The poem encourages us to think about how trees help us in everyday life.
Trees are a natural resource that should be preserved and not cut down without reason.
They provide a quiet place for children to play and learn from nature.

quiz.q: Which part of a tree first catches the morning sun?
quiz.explain: Leaves are the first to receive sunlight.

quiz.q: Why are trees called harmless?
quiz.explain: Trees do not harm anyone; they only grow.

quiz.q: What is the main reason leaves are burned on Halloween in the West?
quiz.explain: Burning leaves keeps the forest clean and celebrates the harvest.

quiz.q: Which line of the poem shows personification?
quiz.explain: The poem says trees hum a lullaby, giving them human action.

quiz.q: What does the poem say trees do for small kids?
quiz.explain: The poem mentions shade, fruit, and lullabies for children.

quiz.q: Which season is Halloween celebrated in?
quiz.explain: Halloween falls in autumn (October) in the West.

quiz.q: What is the first line of the poem?
options: Trees are the kindest things I know
quiz.explain: The poem starts with “Trees are the kindest things I know.”

quiz.q: Which part of the day is referred to in the line “They are the last to hold the light, when evening changes into night”?
quiz.explain: The line refers to the evening.

quiz.q: What is the main benefit of trees for the environment?
quiz.explain: All listed benefits are provided by trees.

quiz.q: Which figure of speech is used when the poem says “humming trees”?
quiz.explain: Personification gives human action to trees.

subject: English
notes: Miss Slippery is a story about a girl named Sayali who is teased by classmates and faces difficulties at home.
She often forgets things and gets nervous, which makes her feel like she is always ‘slipping’ even when she is careful.
The teacher gives her responsibilities to help her feel useful and to build confidence.
Key words: all‑devouring look (frightening look), went blank (could not remember), vociferous (noisy), inevitable (certain), stern (strict).
Compound words are formed by joining two words, e.g., homework, kind‑hearted.
Irregular verbs do not follow the regular -ed pattern, e.g., go – went – gone, break – broke – broken.
Continuous tense shows an action in progress (was coming). Perfect tense shows a completed action (has asked).
Polite requests use modal verbs: Could I…, Would you mind…, May I…
Anagrams are words formed by rearranging letters, e.g., state – taste.
Traffic signs give instructions; students should learn them for safety.

quiz.q: What did the teacher ask Sayali to do after the teasing?
options: Take the class to the park
Bring the register, chalk and duster
Write a letter to the principal
quiz.explain: The teacher assigned her the task of bringing school supplies every morning.

quiz.q: Which word best describes Sayali’s feeling when she could not remember anything?
quiz.explain: ‘Went blank’ means she could not remember.

quiz.q: What does the word ‘vociferous’ mean?
quiz.explain: Vociferous means loud and forceful.

quiz.q: Which tense is used in the sentence ‘I was coming down the school stairs’?
quiz.explain: The verb ‘was coming’ shows a past continuous action.

quiz.q: What is a compound word?
options: Two words joined to form a new word
quiz.explain: Compound words combine two words, e.g., homework.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an irregular verb?
quiz.explain: Go – went – gone is irregular.

quiz.q: Which sentence is in the perfect tense?
options: I haven’t said a word to you.
You are going to be responsible for it.
quiz.explain: ‘I haven’t said’ uses present perfect.

quiz.q: How can you politely ask for directions?
options: Show me the way to post office.
Could you show me the way to post office?
Take me to the post office.
quiz.explain: Polite requests use modal verbs like ‘Could you’.

quiz.q: Which word means ‘very expensive’?
quiz.explain: Extravagant means very expensive.

quiz.q: What does ‘in a jiffy’ mean?
quiz.explain: ‘In a jiffy’ means very quickly.

subject: English
notes: Try again is a poem about perseverance and courage.
Key idea: keep trying even if you fail at first.
Courage means the willingness to keep going.
Persevere means to keep trying until you succeed.
Patience is the ability to wait without losing hope.
If you fail, try again – do not give up.
If you lose a race, do not feel ashamed; keep trying.
When others succeed, you can too if you are patient.
Success is more valuable when earned after hard work.
A proverb is a simple truth that is widely accepted.
The poem can be used as a poster or a web activity.
Anagrams in the poem help remember words like ‘rainy tag’ = ‘try again’.
The poem’s lines can be matched with meanings: ‘heed’ = pay attention, ‘strive’ = try hard, etc.
Opposite words: succeed ↔ fail, punishment ↔ reward, courage ↔ fear, stop/quit ↔ continue, lose ↔ win.
The lesson: never give up; keep trying and you will win.
Use the poem to create a poster or a web diagram of ‘Trying again leads to success’.
Remember: Try again, keep courage, stay patient, and you will conquer.

quiz.q: What is the main message of the poem "Try Again"?
quiz.explain: The poem encourages perseverance and trying again after failure.

quiz.q: Which word is a shortened form of "It is" in the poem?
quiz.explain: ’Tis is the contraction for "It is".

quiz.q: What does "persevere" mean?
quiz.explain: Persevere means to keep trying until you succeed.

quiz.q: Which line is a proverb?
options: Try again; If you fail, try again
All that other folk can do
quiz.explain: The first line is a proverb about perseverance.

quiz.q: Which word is an antonym of "succeed"?
quiz.explain: Fail is the opposite of succeed.

quiz.q: What should you do when you fail at first?
quiz.explain: The poem says to try again after failure.

quiz.q: Which word means "to try very hard"?
quiz.explain: Strive means to try very hard.

quiz.q: What is the meaning of "patience" in the poem?
options: Capacity to accept delay without losing hope
quiz.explain: Patience is the ability to wait without losing hope.

quiz.q: Which line conveys that success is more valuable when earned with difficulty?
options: Try again; If you fail, try again
All that other folk can do
quiz.explain: The line about time bringing reward implies effort leads to value.

quiz.q: What does the poem suggest about people who lose a race?
quiz.explain: The poem advises to try again after losing.

subject: English
notes: Architect designs the building structure.
Engineer finalises details and ensures safety.
Building contractor hires workers and supervises construction.
Mason builds walls, floors and ensures quality of stone and bricks.
Carpenter makes wooden framework for doors and windows.
Tiler lays tiles on floors and walls.
Interior decorator beautifies the inside of a home.
A syllable is a single sound containing a vowel.
Words with one vowel sound are one‑syllable words.
Two‑syllable words have two vowel sounds, e.g. father, mason, builder.
Three‑syllable words have three vowel sounds, e.g. engineer, carpenter, construction.
Retirement is leaving a job after a long career.
People retire when they reach a certain age or after many years of work.
Reasons for retirement include age, health, or desire for rest.
After retirement people may spend time with family or hobbies.
A mason’s dedication, diligence and persistence made him highly sought after.
A contractor rewards good work with a good salary and appreciation.
A legal ownership document is given when a house is handed over.
Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings.
Examples: hair – hare, waist – waste, knew – new.
Understanding syllables helps in pronunciation and spelling.

quiz.q: Which professional designs the structure of a house?
quiz.explain: An architect plans and designs the structure.

quiz.q: What does a mason primarily do?
quiz.explain: A mason builds walls, roof, etc. and does plastering.

quiz.q: Which term means ‘to put great effort into something’?
quiz.explain: Strove means to make great efforts.

quiz.q: What is the main reason the mason decided to retire?
options: He was offered a better job
quiz.explain: He retired after becoming a grandfather.

quiz.q: In the story, what did the contractor give to the mason as a gift?
quiz.explain: The contractor gave ownership documents as a gift.

quiz.q: Which of the following words has three syllables?
quiz.explain: Engineer has three syllables.

quiz.q: What does the word ‘recompensed’ mean?
quiz.explain: Recompensed means paid for work done.

quiz.q: Which phrase best completes: "She does her job ______"?
quiz.explain: The correct phrase is ‘with full dedication’.

quiz.q: What is a homophone?
options: A word that sounds like another but differs in spelling
A word that is spelled incorrectly
quiz.explain: Homophones sound alike but have different spellings and meanings.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a professional mentioned in the chapter?
quiz.explain: Electrician is not listed among the professionals in the chapter.

subject: English
notes: The Little River is a poem that describes a river in two seasons – summer and monsoon.
In summer the river is only knee‑deep, easy to cross, and the banks are not steep.
During monsoon (Ashadh) the river rises, becomes a spate, and the current grows strong.
The poem uses figures of speech such as alliteration (repeated initial sounds) and onomatopoeia (words that imitate sounds).
Alliteration examples: "meanders along", "mystic moon", "mirthful murmur" – the initial sound is repeated in each line.
Onomatopoeia examples: "babbling", "roar", "swish", "beep" – words that mimic the sound of water or animals.

Key words: meanders (flow with twists), slime (thick slippery substance), kash (tall grass), gamchha (cotton towel), in spate (sudden flood), babbling (talking rapidly), scour (scrub), rife (full of), wade (walk in shallow water).
The poem shows how people use the river for bathing, washing clothes, and cooking, and how the river changes with seasons.
The riddle at the end describes a river: it runs, murmurs, has a bed and a mouth, falls but cannot climb up.
Students should remember that rivers can be clean or polluted; we must keep them clean by not dumping waste.
Alliteration and onomatopoeia add musicality and vividness to poetry.
The poem also highlights the importance of nature and the rhythm of rural life.
In the poem, the river’s banks are described as not too steep, only knee‑deep, and having cool shade.
The poem contrasts summer (calm, shallow) with monsoon (flood, strong current).
The poem encourages us to appreciate the beauty of nature and to respect it.

quiz.q: What season is described when the river is only knee‑deep?
quiz.explain: In summer the river is shallow and easy to cross.

quiz.q: Which figure of speech repeats the initial sound in a line?
quiz.explain: Alliteration repeats the same initial sound.

quiz.q: Which word in the poem is an example of onomatopoeia?
quiz.explain: Babbling imitates the sound of water.

quiz.q: What does "in spate" mean?
quiz.explain: In spate refers to a sudden flood.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a non‑English word from the poem?
quiz.explain: Meanders is an English word.

quiz.q: The poem mentions "mynahs". What are they?
quiz.explain: Mynahs are birds.

quiz.q: Which season is associated with the word "rainy" in the poem?
quiz.explain: Monsoon is the rainy season.

quiz.q: What activity do the girls and boys do at the riverbank?
quiz.explain: They bathe and splash with gamchhas.

quiz.q: Which of these words describes the river’s current during monsoon?
quiz.explain: During monsoon the current is strong.

quiz.q: What does the riddle at the end describe?
quiz.explain: The riddle describes a river.

subject: English
notes: - Excuses are reasons given when we are late or miss something.
- Punctuality means arriving on time; it shows respect and responsibility.
- Direct speech records exact words spoken; indirect (reported) speech conveys the meaning without quoting.
- In indirect speech, pronouns, tenses, and time words often change (e.g., tomorrow → next day).
- Common excuses for being late include traffic, bad weather, illness, or family problems.
- Teachers may use humour or jokes to make learning about excuses fun.
- A skit is a short play that helps students practice speaking and listening.
- When writing excuses, use polite words like “I’m sorry” and give a brief reason.
- In a story‑writing contest, students must follow the given theme and time limit.
- Good excuses are honest, brief, and show that the student cares about the situation.
- Teachers can correct lateness by setting clear rules, giving reminders, and encouraging punctuality.
- The chapter encourages students to think about why being on time matters in life and school.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of the skit "Excuses!" in the chapter?
options: To illustrate different types of excuses
quiz.explain: The skit is used to show how students give excuses for being late.

quiz.q: Which type of speech is used when the exact words of a speaker are reported?
quiz.explain: Direct speech reports the exact words spoken.

quiz.q: In the conversation, why did Sharvari say she was late?
options: She saw a road sign that said ‘Go Slow’
quiz.explain: Sharvari used the road sign ‘Go Slow’ as her excuse.

quiz.q: What does the word "investigate" mean in the context of the skit?
quiz.explain: Investigate means to search for the truth about an incident.

quiz.q: Which event happened first according to Ritesh’s story?
options: The thief ran out of the shop
The groaning man joined the thief
quiz.explain: Ritesh first heard a scream from the main road.

quiz.q: What was the teacher’s reaction when Ritesh told the story?
quiz.explain: The teacher was skeptical and asked for details.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT an excuse mentioned in the skit?
options: A thief running out of a shop
quiz.explain: A broken school bus was not mentioned.

quiz.q: What does the phrase "accounts for" mean in the context of the skit?
quiz.explain: Accounts for means to explain or report what happened.

quiz.q: Why did Ritesh refuse to take part in the story-writing competition?
options: He didn’t think he could write a story
quiz.explain: Ritesh said he was not good at making up stories.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a correct indirect speech transformation of "Ritesh: I am sorry, Ma’am!"?
options: Ritesh told Ma’am he was sorry.
Ritesh told Ma’am he would be sorry.
quiz.explain: Indirect speech reports the content, not the exact words.

subject: English
notes: Anchor – a T‑shaped iron bar that holds a ship in place.
Beam – the widest part of a ship, measured from side to side.
Bow – the front end of a ship.
Bilge/Keel – the bottom part of a ship, running along the centre.
Bridge/Cockpit/Wheel House – the control cabin where the ship is steered.
Crow’s Nest – a small tower or post at the top of a ship from where a sailor can look out.
Hull – the main body of a ship that is above the water level.
Part holes – small windows on the side of a ship.
Grace Darling – a brave girl who rescued shipwreck survivors in 1838.
Lighthouse – a tall tower with a light that warns ships of dangerous rocks.
Shipwreck – a ship that is destroyed by hitting rocks or sinking.
Rescue – to save people from danger.
Oars – poles with blades used to row a boat.
The story shows courage, self‑lessness and determination.
Grace’s father was wise, educated and taught honesty and bravery.
Grace was small but strong and believed she could row as well as a man.
The rescue took place near the rocks on the east coast of England.
Grace and her family became famous through newspapers and public praise.
The story teaches that courage can come from anyone, regardless of gender or size.

quiz.q: Which part of a ship is the broadest side-to-side section?
quiz.explain: The beam is the widest part of a ship.

quiz.q: What is the main function of a lighthouse?
options: To provide a place for fishermen
To warn sailors of dangerous rocks
To serve as a tourist attraction
quiz.explain: Lighthouses warn sailors of hazards at sea.

quiz.q: Who was Grace Darling?
quiz.explain: Grace was the daughter of a lighthouse keeper.

quiz.q: In which year did the shipwreck that Grace helped rescue occur?
quiz.explain: The wreck happened in 1838.

quiz.q: What did Grace do to help the stranded sailors?
options: She rowed a boat to the rocks
She sent a message to the coast guard
quiz.explain: Grace rowed a boat to rescue them.

quiz.q: Which of the following best describes Grace’s character?
quiz.explain: Grace was brave and unselfish.

quiz.q: How many people were rescued from the wreck?
quiz.explain: Nine men and women were rescued, but the boat could carry four at a time.

quiz.q: What reward did Grace and her father receive?
quiz.explain: They were given a special reward for their heroism.

quiz.q: Which part of a ship is the control cabin?
quiz.explain: The bridge is the control cabin of a ship.

quiz.q: What does the term 'crow’s nest' refer to?
quiz.explain: The crow’s nest is the highest lookout point on a ship.

subject: Hindi
notes: • मातृभूमि वह देश है जिसे हम अपने दिल से प्यार करते हैं।
• मातृभूमि के प्रति भक्ति और सेवा को ‘भक्ति‑सेवा’ कहते हैं।
• ‘भक्ति‑सेवा’ के तीन प्रमुख गुण: समर्पण, बलिदान और निष्ठा।

subject: Hindi
chapter: लकड़हारा और वन एकांकी अरविंद भटनागर ३०-३३
notes: लकड़हारा एक ग्रामीण व्यक्ति है जो पेड़ काटकर रोटी कमाता है।
कथा में लकड़हारा, भगवान (ग्रामीण के रूप में), और पेड़ के बीच संवाद है।
कथा का मुख्य संदेश है: पेड़ और वन का संरक्षण ज़रूरी है।
लकड़हारा की कुल्हाड़ी पानी में गिर जाती है, जिससे वह निराश होता है।
ग्रामीण (भगवान के रूप में) तीन बार कोशिश करता है और अलग-अलग धातुओं की कुल्हाड़ी निकालता है।
कथा में भगवान लकड़हारे से शर्त रखता है कि वह हरे-भरे पेड़ों को नहीं काटेगा।
कथा में पेड़ भी बोलता है, यह बताता है कि पेड़ हवा, पानी और भोजन देता है।
कथा का दूसरा दृश्य लकड़हारे की पत्नी के साथ है, जहाँ वह लकड़हारे को सोने के लिए प्रेरित करती है।
कथा में पेड़ के साथ संवाद से यह सिखाया जाता है कि प्रकृति के साथ सहजीवन ज़रूरी है।
कथा के अंत में लकड़हारा सहमत होता है और पेड़ को काटने से परहेज़ करता है।
कथा में पेड़ को बोलने की कल्पना करके प्रकृति के प्रति सम्मान दिखाया गया है।
कथा में कुल्हाड़ी के धातु (चाँदी, सोना, लोहे) का उल्लेख है, जो प्रतीकात्मक हैं।
कथा से यह सीख मिलती है कि मेहनत और ईमानदारी से ही धन मिलता है।
कथा में भगवान की शर्त है कि लकड़हारा लालच से बचे और पेड़ काटे नहीं।
कथा में पेड़ और लकड़हारे के बीच संवाद से प्रकृति की भूमिका स्पष्ट होती है।

quiz.q: कथा में लकड़हारे की कुल्हाड़ी क्यों गिर गई?
quiz.explain: कथा में बताया गया है कि कुल्हाड़ी नदी के गहरे पानी में गिर गई।

quiz.explain: भगवान ने शर्त रखी कि लकड़हारा हरे-भरे पेड़ों को नहीं काटेगा।

quiz.q: कथा में पेड़ ने लकड़हारे को क्या बताया?
quiz.explain: पेड़ ने बताया कि वह हवा, पानी और भोजन देता है।

quiz.explain: पहली बार ग्रामीण ने चाँदी की कुल्हाड़ी निकाली।

subject: Hindi
notes: व्याकरण में शब्दों को दो प्रकारों में बाँटा जाता है – विकारी और अविकारी।
विकारी शब्दों में सर्वनाम, विशेषण, क्रिया, संज्ञा आदि आते हैं।
अविकारी शब्दों में अव्यय, वाच्य, परिमाणवाचक आदि शामिल हैं।
सर्वनाम को निश्चित और अनिश्चित दो भागों में बाँटा जाता है।
विशेषण को जातिबाचक, व्यक्तिबाचक, परिमाणवाचक आदि में बाँटा जाता है।
क्रिया को सकर्मक, अकर्मक, अनिश्चयवाचक, निश्चयवाचक आदि में बाँटा जाता है।
वाक्य के प्रकार – विधानार्थक, प्रश्नार्थक, आज्ञार्थक, विस्मयादिबोधक, निषेधार्थक आदि।
वाक्य के चार प्रमुख घटक – कर्ता, क्रिया, कर्म, वाच्य।
वाक्य की रचना में काल – वर्तमान, भूत, भविष्य, अपूर्ण आदि।
मुहावरे और कहावतें भाषा को रंगीन बनाती हैं।
पत्र लेखन में औपचारिक और अनौपचारिक दोनों प्रकार होते हैं।
ई‑मेल लिखने के नियम – विषय, संबोधन, मुख्य भाग, समापन।
वृत्तांत लेखन में घटना, समय, स्थान, व्यक्ति का वर्णन होना चाहिए।
कहानी लेखन में शीर्षक, कथानक, संवाद और संदेश होना अनिवार्य है।
विज्ञापन लेखन में आकर्षक भाषा, संक्षिप्त वाक्य और स्पष्ट उद्देश्य होना चाहिए।
भाषा बिंदु – उपसर्ग, प्रत्यय, मूल शब्द आदि का अध्ययन करना चाहिए।
विरामचिह्न – पूर्ण विराम, अल्पविराम, प्रश्नवाचक चिन्ह, विस्मयादिबोधक चिन्ह आदि।
संज्ञा के लिंग और वचन के अनुसार वाक्य में बदलाव करना चाहिए।
समूहवाचक शब्द – सभी, कुछ, कोई आदि।
संबंधवाचक शब्द – जो, जिस, जिसके आदि।
सहायक क्रिया – है, है, रहा, रहे आदि।
प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया – करना, देना, लेना आदि।
वाक्य शुद्धि – त्रुटि रहित वाक्य लिखना।
वर्णविच्छेद – शब्दों को सही ढंग से लिखना।
भाषा का प्रयोग – उपयुक्त शब्द चयन और शैली।

5. भाव वह मनोभाव है जिसे लेखक पाठक तक पहुँचाना चाहता है।
6. शैली वह तरीका है जिससे लेखक विषय और भाव को प्रस्तुत करता है।
7. भाषा में शब्द चयन, वाक्य रचना और लय का ध्यान रखना चाहिए।
8. चित्रण शब्दों के माध्यम से दृश्य, ध्वनि, गंध आदि को जीवंत बनाता है।
9. रचना लिखते समय भाव को स्पष्ट रखने के लिए रूपक, उपमा, अतिशयोक्ति आदि का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
10. रचना के प्रकार: कविता, गीत, नाटक, कहानी, निबंध, लेख आदि।
11. कविता में तुक, लय और छंद का विशेष महत्व होता है।
12. गीत में संगीत के साथ तालमेल और भाव की गहराई पर ध्यान दिया जाता है।
13. नाटक में संवाद और क्रिया के माध्यम से कहानी को प्रस्तुत किया जाता है।
14. कहानी में कथानक, पात्र और परिवेश का संतुलन आवश्यक है।
15. निबंध में तथ्य, तर्क और निष्कर्ष स्पष्ट रूप से प्रस्तुत किये जाते हैं।
16. रचना लिखते समय विषय का चयन, भाव की पहचान और शैली का निर्धारण पहले किया जाता है।
17. रचना में शब्दों का सही प्रयोग और वाक्य विन्यास पाठक को समझने में मदद करता है।
18. रचना के लिए प्रेरणा स्रोत: प्रकृति, समाज, अनुभव, इतिहास, भावनाएँ।
19. रचना की समीक्षा में भाषा, भाव, शैली और चित्रण का विश्लेषण किया जाता है।
20. रचना के मूल्यांकन में मौलिकता, अभिव्यक्ति और प्रभाव को मापा जाता है।

subject: Hindi
notes: गाँव-शहर नवगीत का विषय समाज में बदलाव और उसकी चुनौतियों पर प्रकाश डालता है।
गाँव में परंपरागत जीवनशैली और शहर में आधुनिक जीवन के बीच अंतर को स्पष्ट किया गया है।
कविता में ‘काँटे बोने वाले’, ‘चुभने वाली’, ‘फटने वाले’ जैसे शब्दों का प्रयोग करके कठिनाई और संघर्ष को दर्शाया गया है।
‘काँटे बोने वाले’ का अर्थ है जो कठिन परिश्रम करता है।
‘चुभने वाली’ का अर्थ है जो दर्द देता है या परेशान करता है।
‘फटने वाले’ का अर्थ है जो अचानक टूटता या फटता है।
कविता की अंतिम चार पंक्तियों में जीवन के संघर्ष और आशा का संदेश है।
उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय को पहचान कर मूल शब्द को अलग करना शब्द ज्ञान बढ़ाता है।
भाषा बिंदु: भारतीय, आस्थावान, व्यक्तित्व, स्नेहिल, बेबात, निरादर, प्रत्येक, सुयोग – ये शब्द समाज के विभिन्न पहलुओं को दर्शाते हैं।
यातायात की समस्याएँ: भीड़, प्रदूषण, दुर्घटनाएँ, ट्रैफ़िक जाम। उपाय: सार्वजनिक परिवहन, साइकिल चलाना, पैदल चलना, सड़क सुधार।
हिंदी साप्ताहिक पत्रिकाएँ और समाचार पत्र प्रेरक कथाएँ और निबंध लेखन के लिए उपयोगी स्रोत हैं।
कविता में ‘काँटे बोने वाले’ शब्द का अर्थ ‘कठिन परिश्रम करने वाले’ है।
‘चुभने वाली’ शब्द का अर्थ ‘दर्द देने वाला’ है।
‘फटने वाले’ शब्द का अर्थ ‘अचानक टूटने वाला’ है।
उपसर्ग/प्रत्यय अलग करके मूल शब्द लिखना शब्द निर्माण की समझ बढ़ाता है।

quiz.q: कविता की अंतिम चार पंक्तियों का मुख्य संदेश क्या है?
quiz.explain: कविता संघर्ष और आशा पर बल देती है।
