quiz.q: Which month has 30 days?
quiz.explain: April has 30 days.

quiz.q: What is the last month of the year?
quiz.explain: December is the last month.

quiz.q: How many days are in February during a leap year?
quiz.explain: Leap year February has 29 days.

quiz.q: Which month is the first month of the Indian calendar?
quiz.explain: Chaitra starts the Indian calendar.

quiz.q: Which month is the last month of the Indian calendar?
quiz.explain: Phalgun ends the Indian calendar.

quiz.q: Which month has 30 days and is the 9th month?
quiz.explain: September is the 9th month with 30 days.

quiz.q: Which month has 31 days and is the 12th month?
quiz.explain: December is the 12th month with 31 days.

subject: Maths
notes: - The symbol ‘<’ means ‘smaller than’.
- The symbol ‘>’ means ‘greater than’.
- To compare two one‑digit numbers, look at the larger digit.
- For two‑digit numbers, first compare the tens digits.
- If the tens digits are different, the number with the larger tens digit is bigger.
- If the tens digits are the same, compare the units digits.
- The number with the larger units digit is bigger.
- Example: 52 > 37 because 5 > 3 in the tens place.
- Example: 72 < 78 because 2 < 8 in the units place.
- When the tens digits are equal, the units digit decides.
- The larger number is the one that comes later on a measuring tape.
- You can write the comparison as “43 < 46” or “84 > 86”.
- Practice by comparing pairs of numbers and writing ‘<’ or ‘>’ between them.
- The symbol ‘<’ is read as “less than” and ‘>’ as “greater than”.
- If two numbers are equal, write ‘=’.
- Comparing numbers helps in ordering them from smallest to largest.
- Use the rules for any two‑digit numbers you see.

quiz.q: Which symbol means ‘smaller than’?
quiz.explain: The ‘<’ symbol is read as ‘less than’.

quiz.q: Which number is greater: 52 or 37?
quiz.explain: 52 has a larger tens digit (5 vs 3).

quiz.q: Compare 72 and 78: 72 ______ 78
quiz.explain: Units digit 2 < 8, so 72 < 78.

quiz.q: What is the result of 43 < 46?
quiz.explain: 43 is smaller than 46, so the statement is true.

quiz.q: If the tens digits are equal, which digit decides the comparison?
quiz.explain: Units digit decides when tens are equal.

quiz.q: Which symbol is read as ‘greater than’?
quiz.explain: The ‘>’ symbol means ‘greater than’.

quiz.q: Which number is smaller: 31 or 33?
quiz.explain: 31 has a smaller units digit (1 vs 3).

quiz.q: Write the comparison: 84 ______ 86
quiz.explain: 84 is smaller than 86.

quiz.q: Which rule decides if 52 > 37?
quiz.explain: Tens digit 5 > 3 decides.

quiz.q: What does ‘31 < 33’ mean?
quiz.explain: ‘<’ means 31 is smaller than 33.

subject: Maths
chapter: Neighbouring numbers on each side numbers
notes: - A number line is a straight line with marks for numbers.
- Zero is the starting point on the left side.
- Numbers are written at equal distances to the right of zero.
- On a number line, the neighbour to the left of any number is one less.
- The neighbour to the right is one more.
- Numbers can be arranged in ascending (smallest to largest) order.
- Numbers can also be arranged in descending (largest to smallest) order.
- To find the smallest number, compare pairs and pick the smaller one.
- To find the largest number, compare pairs and pick the larger one.
- After finding the smallest or largest, cross it out and repeat with the remaining numbers.
- The final list shows the numbers in the chosen order.
- In ascending order we write: smallest < next < largest.
- In descending order we write: largest > next > smallest.
- Practice by arranging sets of three numbers in both orders.
- Remember: on a number line, left neighbour = number-1, right neighbour = number+1.

quiz.q: On a number line, what is the neighbour to the left of 5?
quiz.explain: The left neighbour is one less than the number.

quiz.q: Which of the following is the smallest number in the set 17, 23, 36?
quiz.explain: 17 is less than both 23 and 36.

quiz.q: Arrange the numbers 25, 12, 54 in ascending order.
quiz.explain: 12 is smallest, then 25, then 54.

quiz.q: Arrange 47, 26, 19 in descending order.
quiz.explain: 47 is largest, then 26, then 19.

quiz.q: On a number line, what is the neighbour to the right of 9?
quiz.explain: The right neighbour is one more than the number.

quiz.q: Which set is in ascending order: 43<60<76<89 or 89>76>60>43?
quiz.explain: Ascending order uses < symbols.

quiz.q: What is the largest number in the set 62, 85, 50?
quiz.explain: 85 is greater than 62 and 50.

quiz.q: In descending order, how would you write 15, 522, 975?
quiz.explain: Largest first: 975, then 522, then 15.

quiz.q: If a number line shows 22, 23, 24, what number comes immediately after 23?
quiz.explain: The right neighbour of 23 is 24.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a correct ascending order?
quiz.explain: 23<17<36 is not ascending because 23 > 17.

subject: Maths
notes: - A two‑digit number has a tens digit and a units digit.
- The tens digit cannot be 0 because then it would be a one‑digit number.
- To make the smallest two‑digit number from two digits, put the smaller digit in the tens place and the larger in the units place.
- To make the largest two‑digit number, put the larger digit in the tens place and the smaller in the units place.
- If the two digits are the same, the only number you can make is that digit repeated (e.g., 33).
- You can make two different numbers from two different digits (e.g., 47 and 74).
- When you have more than two digits, you can mix any two of them to form a two‑digit number.
- The number of different two‑digit numbers you can make from n different digits is n(n‑1).
- If a digit can be used more than once, you can make 10 two‑digit numbers from a single digit (11, 22, …, 99).
- You never write a number like 05 or 09; 5 and 9 are single‑digit numbers.
- The smallest two‑digit number you can make from the digits 2 and 3 is 23.
- The largest two‑digit number you can make from the digits 2 and 3 is 32.
- In a game, you can write numbers on discs and pick any two discs to make numbers.
- The smallest number you can make from the digits 4 and 7 is 47.
- The largest number you can make from the digits 4 and 7 is 74.
- When you have the digits 2, 3, 8, you can make 23, 28, 32, 38, 82, 83.
- Count all the different two‑digit numbers you can make to find the smallest and the largest.
- Practice by writing down all the numbers you can make and then picking the smallest and the largest.
- Remember: the tens digit is the leftmost digit and the units digit is the rightmost digit.
- Use the same rules when you play the number‑making game with your friends.

quiz.q: What is the smallest two‑digit number that can be made from the digits 4 and 7?
quiz.explain: Put the smaller digit in the tens place.

quiz.q: How many different two‑digit numbers can be made from the digits 2, 3, and 8?
quiz.explain: Choose any two of the three digits and arrange them: 2×1 + 2×1 + 2×1 = 6.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a two‑digit number?
quiz.explain: 05 is written as 5, a single‑digit number.

quiz.q: If you have the digits 5 and 5, how many two‑digit numbers can you make?
quiz.explain: Only one number 55 can be made.

quiz.q: You pick two discs with the numbers 3 and 7. Which of these is the largest two‑digit number you can make?
quiz.explain: Largest is 73.

quiz.q: How many two‑digit numbers can be made using the same digit repeatedly?
quiz.explain: 11, 22, …, 99 gives 9 numbers, but 00 is not allowed, so 9.

quiz.q: If you have the digits 1, 2, and 3, which is the smallest two‑digit number you can make?
quiz.explain: 12 is the smallest.

quiz.q: Which of these is the largest two‑digit number that can be made from the digits 6 and 9?
quiz.explain: 96 is largest.

quiz.q: You have the digits 4 and 4. Which of these is a valid two‑digit number?
quiz.explain: Only 44 is possible.

quiz.q: If you can use each digit only once, how many two‑digit numbers can you make from the digits 7 and 8?
quiz.explain: You can make 78 and 87.

subject: Maths
notes: Cardinal numbers give the amount of something, e.g. one, two, three.
Ordinal numbers tell the order or position, e.g. first, second, third.
The word ‘cardinal’ comes from the Latin *cardinalis* meaning ‘principal’ or ‘chief’.
In English we write cardinal numbers as 1, 2, 3, … and ordinal numbers as 1st, 2nd, 3rd, …
The first, second, third are the most common ordinals; after that we use –th (fourth, fifth, sixth).
Ordinal numbers are used when we talk about places in a line, a race, a book chapter, etc.
Cardinal numbers are used when we count objects: two apples, five books.
The word ‘cardinal’ is also used in mathematics for important numbers like 0, 1, 2, 3, …
Ordinal numbers can be written in words (first, second) or in symbols (1st, 2nd).
When we say ‘the third child’ we use the ordinal ‘third’ to show position.
If we say ‘three children’ we use the cardinal ‘three’ to show how many.
Cardinal numbers are the same in all languages, but ordinal words differ.
In a race, the winner is the first place, the runner‑up is second place, etc.
In a book, chapter 1 is the first chapter, chapter 2 is the second chapter.
Remember: cardinal numbers count, ordinal numbers order.
Use the correct form in sentences: ‘I have two apples’ (cardinal) vs ‘I am the second in line’ (ordinal).

quiz.q: Which word is a cardinal number?
quiz.explain: ‘fourth’ is a cardinal number; the others are ordinal.

quiz.q: What does the ordinal number ‘second’ tell us?
quiz.explain: ‘Second’ indicates the position in a sequence.

quiz.q: If there are five students in a line, which ordinal number shows the last student?
quiz.explain: The last student is in the 5th position.

quiz.q: Which of these is a correct ordinal form of 8?
quiz.explain: The correct ordinal is ‘eighth’.

quiz.q: In the sentence ‘I have three books’, ‘three’ is a ______?
quiz.explain: ‘Three’ counts books, so it is a cardinal number.

quiz.q: Which word is NOT a cardinal number?
quiz.explain: ‘Seventh’ is ordinal, the others are cardinal.

quiz.q: The runner who finished in 4th place finished how many places behind the winner?
quiz.explain: 4th place is three places behind 1st.

quiz.q: In a race, the 1st place is also called the ______?
quiz.explain: The first place is the winner.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a cardinal number in a sentence?
options: She is the third child in her family.
quiz.explain: ‘12’ counts apples, so it is cardinal.

quiz.q: What does the ordinal number ‘first’ indicate?
quiz.explain: ‘First’ shows the position in a sequence.

subject: Maths
notes: Observe the picture and count the items shown.
Count the number of vegetable carts, fruit sellers, boys, girls, and people with cloth bags.
Look at the vehicles and note which ones stop at a red signal and which move at a green signal.
Identify vehicles that cause air pollution – cars, buses, rickshaws, motorcycles.
Find out which type of vehicle is most common in the picture.
Count cars of different colours on a road and decide which colour is most popular.
Count birds that come to pick grains and see if the same bird returns.
Use a flow chart to record the number of vehicles seen.
Remember to write numbers in the boxes correctly.
Use simple words to describe what you see.
Practice counting with a parent or guardian.
Use a picture to help you answer questions.
Check your answers with a teacher or friend.
Keep the picture handy for reference.
Use the same picture for all related questions.

quiz.q: How many vegetable carts are shown in the picture?
quiz.explain: The picture shows four vegetable carts.

quiz.q: Which vehicles stop at a red signal?
quiz.explain: Bicycles and cars are stopped at the red signal.

quiz.q: Which vehicles move at a green signal?
quiz.explain: Bicycles and cars move at the green signal.

quiz.q: Which vehicle causes the most air pollution?
quiz.explain: Cars cause the most air pollution.

quiz.q: Which type of vehicle is most common in the picture?
quiz.explain: Bicycles are the most common.

quiz.q: If you count cars of different colours, which colour is likely to be most popular?
quiz.explain: Yellow cars are usually most popular.

quiz.q: How many boys are seen in the market?
quiz.explain: There are three boys in the market.

quiz.q: How many girls are seen in the market?
quiz.explain: There are three girls in the market.

quiz.q: How many people have brought their own cloth bags?
quiz.explain: Two people have brought cloth bags.

quiz.q: How many fruit sellers are there?
quiz.explain: There are two fruit sellers.

subject: Maths
chapter: A special way to add-by carrying over
notes: - In addition, we add the units (ones) first and then the tens.
- The units place can only hold numbers 0 to 9.
- If the sum of units is 10 or more, we write the remainder in the units place and carry the tens (the number of tens) to the tens place.
- Carrying over means moving the tens part of the units sum to the tens column.
- After carrying, add the tens column together with any carried tens.
- The final answer is written as tens followed by units.
- Example: 23 + 17 → 3+7=10, write 0 in units, carry 1 to tens: 2+1+1=4, answer 40.
- If the units sum is less than 10, no carrying is needed.
- When adding two-digit numbers, always start from the rightmost column (units).
- The result of carrying is always a whole number of tens (1, 2, 3, …).
- Carrying over helps keep the numbers in the correct place value.
- Remember: 10 units = 1 ten.
- In the book, sticks or beads are used to visualize carrying.
- A bundle of 10 sticks represents one ten.
- The teacher can use real objects to practice carrying.
- The tens column after carrying shows how many tens are in the final sum.
- Carrying is a special way to add numbers that keeps the numbers neat.
- Keep the units column always between 0 and 9.
- Carrying over is the same as “moving a bundle of ten” to the next column.
- The final answer is read as “tens, units”.
- Practice with many examples to become comfortable with carrying.

quiz.q: What is the first step when adding two-digit numbers?
quiz.explain: We start with the units column.

quiz.q: If 7 + 8 = 15, what do we write in the units place?
quiz.explain: Only the remainder 5 stays in units.

quiz.q: How many tens are carried over from 7 + 8?
quiz.explain: 10 units make 1 ten.

quiz.q: What is 23 + 17?
quiz.explain: 23+17=40 after carrying.

quiz.q: When adding 14 + 29, how many tens do we have after carrying?
quiz.explain: 4 tens (40) and 3 units.

quiz.q: If the units sum to 9, do we carry?
quiz.explain: No carry needed.

quiz.q: What does a bundle of 10 sticks represent?
quiz.explain: It represents one ten.

quiz.q: After carrying 1 ten, what is added to the tens column?
quiz.explain: Add original tens plus carried ten.

quiz.q: What is the units place of 9 + 6?
If 4 + 9 = 13, how many tens are carried?
quiz.explain: 13 units give 1 ten.

subject: Maths
notes: - Addition means putting two numbers together to find the total.
- Subtraction means taking one number away from another to find the difference.
- Numbers are written in columns: the tens digit on the left and the units digit on the right.
- When adding, start from the units column and move to the tens column.
- If the sum of the units column is 10 or more, carry 1 to the tens column.
- When adding 10 or 20, simply add 1 or 2 to the tens column and keep the units column the same.
- When subtracting 10 or 20, subtract 1 or 2 from the tens column and keep the units column the same.
- Stories help us practice addition and subtraction with real‑world examples.
- Always read the question carefully to know what is given and what is asked.
- Practice with small numbers first, then try numbers that need carrying or borrowing.
- Remember: 10 = 1 ten, 20 = 2 tens, 30 = 3 tens, etc.
- Check your answer by adding or subtracting back to the original number.
- Use a pencil and paper to write the numbers in columns for clarity.
- If you get a negative result, it means the first number is smaller than the second.
- Keep practicing stories like Gauri’s money, Salma’s handkerchiefs, and the farmer’s cattle.
- You can make your own stories to practice addition and subtraction.

quiz.q: Gauri had 15 rupees and her mother gave her 26 more. How many rupees does Gauri have now?
If Salma stitched 34 handkerchiefs yesterday and 38 more today, how many does she have stitched in two days?
Wasim had 25 marbles and won 13 more. How many marbles does he have?
A shopkeeper had 35 kites and brought 19 more. How many kites does he have?
Add 22 and 24. What is the sum?
Subtract 20 from 57. What is the result?
Add 30 and 19. What is the sum?
Subtract 20 from 49. What is the result?
If you add 10 to 6, what do you get?
If you subtract 10 from 29, what do you get?

subject: Maths
chapter: Let’s untie a ten in order to subtract
notes: - Subtraction can be done by *untying a ten* (borrowing).
- When the units digit of the minuend is smaller than the units digit of the subtrahend, we borrow 1 ten (10 units).
- Borrowing turns a 10 in the tens place into 0 and adds 10 to the units place.
- Example: 35 – 17 → borrow 1 ten from 30 to make 25, then 25 – 17 = 8.
- We always keep the tens digit the same after borrowing (30 → 20).
- If the units digit is enough, no borrowing is needed.
- After borrowing, the tens digit decreases by 1 and the units digit increases by 10.
- Subtraction is the opposite of addition.
- We write the answer below the line, aligning tens and units.
- Remember: 10 = 1 ten + 0 units.
- 1 ten = 10 units.
- When borrowing, the tens column becomes 0 if it was 1.
- The result of borrowing is always a smaller number in the tens column.
- Always check if the units digit of the minuend is less than that of the subtrahend before borrowing.
- Subtraction helps us find how many are left after giving or taking away.
- Use a number line or counters to visualize subtraction.
- Keep the numbers in the same column (tens with tens, units with units).
- When the answer is a single digit, write it in the units column.
- If the answer has two digits, write the tens digit in the tens column and the units digit in the units column.
- Always write the minuend (the larger number) on top and the subtrahend (the smaller number) below.

quiz.q: What do we do when the units digit of the minuend is smaller than the units digit of the subtrahend?
quiz.explain: We borrow 1 ten, turning 10 units into the units place.

quiz.q: In 35 – 17, after borrowing, what is the new minuend?
quiz.explain: Borrowing 1 ten from 30 gives 20, and 10 units added to 5 makes 15, so 20+15=35 becomes 25.

quiz.q: Which of these is a correct subtraction using borrowing?
quiz.explain: 29 – 7 = 22 (no borrowing needed).

quiz.q: If we have 74 – 25, how many do we borrow from the tens place?
quiz.explain: We borrow 1 ten (10 units) because 4 < 5.

quiz.q: What is the result of 30 – 12 after borrowing?
Which statement is true about borrowing?
options: The units digit stays the same
quiz.explain: Borrowing decreases the tens digit by 1.

quiz.q: How many red counters are there if 70 counters are placed and 42 are green?
If Swara had 92 beads and gave 59 to Pari, how many does she have left?
Aqi made 67 karanjis and 48 anaras. By how many is the number of anaras less than karanjis?
In a class of 81 students, 78 took part in a gathering. How many did not take part?

subject: Maths
chapter: Do you know Notes and Coins ?
notes: • A note is a piece of paper money that has a value written on it.
• A coin is a small piece of metal that also has a value written on it.
• In India, common notes are ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500 and ₹2000.
• Common coins are ₹1, ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10.
• You can use notes and coins together to make any amount of money.
• If you have ₹100, you can change it into smaller notes or coins in many ways.
• A shopkeeper can give you change in different combinations of notes and coins.
• When you buy something, you pay the exact amount or give more and get change back.
• The total price of items is the sum of the prices of each item.
• You can count money by adding the values of all notes and coins you have.
• It is important to keep track of the money you spend and the money you have left.
• Money can be used to buy food, toys, books, and other things you need.
• Always check that the amount of change you receive matches what you should get back.
• Money is a way to trade goods and services with others.
• Learning to count money helps you become independent and responsible.

quiz.q: What is the value of a ₹10 note?
quiz.explain: A ₹10 note is worth ten rupees.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a coin?
quiz.explain: ₹5 is a coin, not a note.

quiz.q: If you have a ₹100 note and you want to buy a toy that costs ₹30, how much change should you get?
quiz.explain: ₹100 - ₹30 = ₹70, so you should get ₹70 back, but the smallest change you can give back is ₹20 if you only have ₹20 notes.

quiz.q: Which combination can make ₹15 using coins?
If you buy a ball for ₹8 and a car for ₹12, what is the total cost?
You have a ₹50 note and a ₹10 coin. How many rupees do you have in total?
What is the smallest coin in India?
quiz.explain: The ₹1 coin is the smallest.

quiz.q: If you need ₹200 and you only have ₹100 notes, how many notes do you need?
quiz.explain: Two ₹100 notes make ₹200.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a valid Indian currency?
quiz.explain: ₹3 is not a valid currency.

quiz.q: You buy a notebook for ₹5 and two pencils for ₹2 each. How much do you spend?

subject: Maths
notes: - A line is a straight path that goes on forever in both directions.
- A straight line is what we call a 'line' in this book.
- If you pull a thread tight it becomes a straight line.
- If the thread is loose it becomes a curved line.
- A vertical line goes up and down.
- A horizontal line goes left and right.
- An inclined (or standing) line goes at an angle.
- You can make a vertical line by folding a paper and drawing along the fold.
- You can make a horizontal line by folding a paper the other way and drawing along the fold.
- You can make an inclined line by folding the paper at an angle and drawing along the fold.
- A ruler helps you draw a straight line accurately.
- You can also draw a straight line by hand if you keep it straight.
- Lines are used to draw shapes like squares, rectangles, triangles and circles.
- Colouring shapes helps you see the lines that make them.
- Practice drawing vertical, horizontal and inclined lines to get better.
- Remember: a straight line is the shortest distance between two points.
- A line has no thickness, only length.
- Lines can be inside or outside shapes.
- Lines can be straight or curved, but in this book we only talk about straight lines.
- A straight line can be drawn on paper, on a board, or in the air with a marker.
- The word 'line' in maths means a straight line, not any curve.
- When you draw a line, think of it as a thin, endless path.
- Drawing a line with a ruler gives a perfect straight line.
- Drawing a line by hand needs practice to keep it straight.

quiz.q: What happens to a thread when you pull it tight?
quiz.explain: Pulling tight makes the thread straight.

quiz.q: Which line goes up and down?
quiz.explain: Vertical lines go up and down.

quiz.q: What tool helps you draw a perfect straight line?
quiz.explain: A ruler gives a straight line.

quiz.q: If a thread is loose, what shape does it form?
quiz.explain: Loose thread forms a curve.

quiz.q: Which line goes left and right?
quiz.explain: Horizontal lines go left and right.

quiz.q: What do you fold to show a vertical line?
quiz.explain: Fold lengthwise to get a vertical line.

quiz.q: Which line goes at an angle?
quiz.explain: Inclined lines are at an angle.

quiz.q: You can draw a line by hand if you keep it ______?
quiz.explain: Keep it straight to draw a straight line.

quiz.q: Colouring shapes helps you see the lines that make them. Which colour is used for red?
quiz.explain: Red colour is used for red.

quiz.q: What does the book say about the word 'line'?
quiz.explain: In this book, 'line' means a straight line.

subject: Maths
notes: - Length is the distance from one end of an object to the other.
- We can measure length with a stick, a ruler, or a measuring tape.
- A stick can be used as a unit of measurement if we know its length.
- If a stick is 1 meter long, then 4 sticks equal 4 meters.
- To find the length of a wall, place the stick along the wall and count how many sticks fit.
- When measuring a table, use the same stick to keep the measurement consistent.
- For making garlands, we need to add extra thread so that the garland fits and can be tied easily.
- The extra length is usually 2 hand spans at each end of the garland.
- Hand span is the distance from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger when the hand is spread.
- We can estimate the length of a door or gate by measuring its width with a stick or a tape.
- The measured length is used to decide how many garlands or how long a table we can buy.
- Always check the measurement before buying or cutting.
- A ruler with numbers helps us read the exact length.
- A measuring tape can be unfolded to measure long objects.
- When we write the length, we use the unit “meter” (m) or “centimeter” (cm).
- Remember: 1 meter = 100 centimeters.
- Practice measuring everyday objects to become good at estimating lengths.

quiz.q: Yash measured the wall with a stick and found it was 4 sticks long. If each stick is 1 meter, how long is the wall?
quiz.explain: 4 sticks × 1 meter each = 4 meters.

quiz.q: Which table will Yash choose if he wants the longest table that fits on the wall?
quiz.explain: The longest table that fits is the one that is 5 sticks long.

quiz.q: Rama added 2 hand spans extra at each end of her garland. Why?
quiz.explain: Extra thread lets her tie the garland without cutting.

quiz.q: If a hand span is about 15 cm, how many centimeters of extra thread does Rama add to each garland?
quiz.explain: 2 hand spans × 15 cm = 30 cm.

quiz.q: What tool can you use to measure the width of a door?
quiz.explain: All listed tools can be used.

quiz.q: Which unit is used to measure the length of a table?
quiz.explain: Length is measured in meters.

quiz.q: If Yash wants a table that is 3 sticks long, how many sticks will he need to measure?
quiz.explain: The table itself is 3 sticks long.

quiz.q: Rama wants to make garlands for a classroom door that is 2 meters wide. If each garland needs 2.5 meters of thread, how many garlands can she make with 10 meters of thread?
quiz.explain: 10 ÷ 2.5 = 4 garlands.

quiz.q: What is a hand span?
options: The distance from thumb to little finger
quiz.explain: Hand span is from thumb tip to little finger tip.

quiz.q: Why is it important to measure before buying a table?
quiz.explain: We need to know if the table fits the space.

subject: Maths
notes: - A balance is a simple scale with two pans that help us compare weights.
- If one pan is heavier, the object on that pan is heavier.
- We can use a balance to find out which of two objects is heavier or lighter.
- A balance works by keeping the two pans level when the weights are equal.
- A green grocer uses a balance to weigh vegetables before selling.
- Bholu the bear brought a balance to help Chintoo and Bittoo share jaggery equally.
- We can make our own balance using a ruler, a string, and a small weight.
- Old people used different kinds of weights like stones, wooden sticks, and metal bars.
- When we want to know if two things are equal, we put them on the two pans of a balance.
- If the pans stay level, the two things weigh the same.
- If one pan goes down, the thing on that pan is heavier.
- A balance is a useful tool for learning about heavier and lighter objects.
- We can also use a balance to learn about equal shares of food or sweets.
- A balance is a simple machine that helps us compare weights easily.
- Using a balance helps us be fair when sharing things with friends.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a balance?
quiz.explain: A balance is used to compare the weights of two objects.

quiz.q: If the left pan of a balance goes down, what can we say?
quiz.explain: When a pan goes down, it means that side is heavier.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a tool a green grocer might use?
quiz.explain: A green grocer uses a balance to weigh vegetables.

quiz.q: What did Bholu bring to help share jaggery?
quiz.explain: Bholu brought a balance to make equal shares of jaggery.

quiz.q: If two objects are on a balance and the pans stay level, what does that mean?
quiz.explain: Level pans mean the objects weigh the same.

quiz.q: What can we make at home to learn about heavier and lighter objects?
quiz.explain: A homemade balance helps us compare weights.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a type of old weight?
quiz.explain: Old weights were stone, wood, or metal, not rubber bands.

quiz.q: When we want to share food equally, what tool can help?
quiz.explain: A balance helps make equal shares.

quiz.q: What happens if the right pan of a balance goes down?
quiz.explain: Down means that side is heavier.

quiz.q: Which of these is a correct way to use a balance?
options: Put one object on each pan
Put both objects on the same pan
Put a weight on one pan only
quiz.explain: To compare two objects, each goes on a different pan.

subject: Maths
notes: - A vessel is a container that can hold liquid.
- Capacity is the amount of liquid a vessel can hold.
- We can compare capacities by filling vessels with the same unit of liquid, like a small bowl or a cup.
- The vessel that needs the most bowls to fill has the greatest capacity.
- The vessel that needs the fewest bowls has the least capacity.
- Vessels can be of different shapes: mug, bucket, tumbler, bottle, etc.
- To measure capacity, first guess how many bowls it might take, then count the bowls used.
- The difference between the guessed number and the actual number shows how accurate the guess was.
- Capacity can be expressed in terms of the number of bowls or cups used.
- When measuring medicine, a small cup is used to fill a bottle’s lid and then poured into a glass or tumbler.
- The same method works for any liquid: water, medicine, juice.
- Counting bowls is a simple way for young children to understand volume.
- Repeating the activity with many vessels helps practice estimation and counting.
- Always use the same size of bowl or cup for fair comparison.
- The activity helps develop observation, estimation, and basic arithmetic skills.

quiz.q: Which vessel holds the most water?
quiz.explain: The bucket is usually the largest and holds the most.

quiz.q: What do we use to measure the capacity of a vessel?
quiz.explain: We fill the vessel with a small bowl of water and count how many bowls are needed.

quiz.q: If a tumbler needs 3 bowls to fill, and a mug needs 2 bowls, which has greater capacity?
quiz.explain: More bowls mean more capacity.

quiz.q: What is the first step before filling a vessel?
quiz.explain: We first guess how many bowls it might take.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a vessel?
quiz.explain: A table is not a container for liquid.

quiz.q: When measuring medicine, what is used to fit over the bottle’s lid?
quiz.explain: A small cup is fitted over the lid to measure medicine.

quiz.q: If a bottle needs 5 bowls to fill and a glass needs 2 bowls, which holds more liquid?
quiz.explain: More bowls mean more liquid.

subject: Maths
notes: - A pattern is a repeated arrangement of shapes, numbers or letters.

- In maths, we use patterns to solve problems and to understand numbers.
- A pattern can be written as a list of items separated by commas or vertical bars.

- A pattern may start with one item and then add one more each time (e.g., 1, 2, 3, 4).

- Patterns can be made with letters: A, B, C, A, B, C, ...

- We can use patterns to make art, like drawing repeating shapes or colours.

subject: Maths
chapter: Let’s read and write in words
notes: Numbers in words are written in one standard way, e.g. 47 is written as "forty-seven" and not as "forty and seven".
The numbers 1 to 100 are written in words using the pattern "tens‑unit".
For the tens place we use the words: ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety.
If the unit digit is zero we write only the tens word, e.g. 30 is "thirty".
If the unit digit is not zero we join the tens and unit words with a hyphen, e.g. 34 is "thirty‑four".
The unit words are: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine.
The word "and" is not used in the standard writing of numbers in this textbook; the hyphen is used instead.
The numbers 1 to 20 have special names: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty.
For 21 to 99 we use the tens word followed by a hyphen and the unit word, e.g. 57 is "fifty‑seven".
The number 100 is written as "one hundred".
Children are expected to be able to read numbers up to 100 and write numbers up to 50 in words.
When writing a number, use only one form; do not mix forms such as "forty and seven" and "forty‑seven".
The hyphen is used to connect the tens and units; there is no space before or after the hyphen.
The word "and" is used only in some other contexts (e.g. in fractions) but not for writing whole numbers in this chapter.
The pattern for writing numbers is: <tens word>‑<unit word> (if unit is not zero).
The book lists the numbers 21–99 in a table for quick reference.
The numbers 31, 41, 51, 61, 71, 81, 91 are written as "thirty‑one", "forty‑one", "fifty‑one", "sixty‑one", "seventy‑one", "eighty‑one", "ninety‑one" respectively.

subject: Maths
chapter: What is the meaning of ‘Place Value’ ?
notes: Place value means the value of a digit depending on its position in a number.
In a two‑digit number the leftmost digit is in the tens place and the rightmost digit is in the units place.
The tens place represents ten times the digit’s value. For example, 3 in the tens place of 35 means 3×10 = 30.
The units place represents the digit’s value itself. For example, 5 in the units place of 35 means 5×1 = 5.
The number 35 is made of 30 (tens) + 5 (units).
The number 50 is made of 50 (tens) + 0 (units).
If a digit is 0 in the tens place, its place value is 0×10 = 0.
If a digit is 0 in the units place, its place value is 0×1 = 0.
To find a digit’s place value, multiply the digit by 10 if it is in the tens place, or by 1 if it is in the units place.
The place value of 1 in the tens place of 18 is 10.
The place value of 8 in the units place of 18 is 8.
The place value of 2 in the tens place of 23 is 20.
The place value of 3 in the units place of 23 is 3.
The place value of 6 in the tens place of 65 is 60.
The place value of 5 in the units place of 65 is 5.
A number can have more than two digits; each position has a different place value (hundreds, thousands, etc.).
When you write a number, the rightmost digit is always the units place.
The leftmost digit of a two‑digit number is always the tens place.
Place value helps us read and write numbers correctly.
Understanding place value is the first step to learning addition and subtraction.
Place value is the same for all numbers, no matter how big or small.
The digit 5 in 50 is in the tens place, so its place value is 50.
The digit 0 in 50 is in the units place, so its place value is 0.
When a digit is 0, its place value is always 0.
Place value is a key concept in the Maharashtra State Board Maths curriculum for Standard 2.

quiz.explain: 5 is in the tens place, so 5×10 = 50.

quiz.q: What is the place value of 8 in the number 18?
quiz.explain: 8 is in the units place, so its value is 8.

quiz.q: The number 35 can be written as 30 + 5. What does 30 represent?
quiz.explain: 30 comes from the tens place (3×10).

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a place value?
quiz.explain: 100 is a place value but not used in a two‑digit number.

notes: संख्येचे विस्तारित रूप म्हणजे त्या संख्येतील प्रत्येक स्थानिक किंमतीचे गुणाकार दाखवणे.
१० च्या पटीतील अंकाला दशकस्थानी म्हणतात, १ च्या पटीतील अंकाला एककस्थानी म्हणतात.
विस्तारित रूप लिहिताना प्रथम दहाच्या स्थानिक किंमतीचे गुणाकार लिहा, नंतर एककस्थानीचे गुणाकार.
९४ चे विस्तारित रूप ९० + ४ आहे.
६० चे विस्तारित रूप ६० + ० आहे.

४९ चे विस्तारित रूप ४० + ९ आहे.
विस्तारित रूपातून संख्या शोधण्यासाठी सर्व भागांची बेरीज करावी.

एककस्थानी अंक ० किती वेळा येतो हे १० ते ९९ या संख्यांमध्ये मोजू शकतो.
विस्तारित रूपावरून संख्या लिहिताना दहाच्या स्थानिक किंमतीचे गुणाकार व एककस्थानीचे गुणाकार एकत्र जोडावे.
विस्तारित रूपात ० असलेल्या स्थानिक किंमतीसुद्धा लिहायला हवे, जसे ६० = ६० + ०.

notes: संक्यांना टप्प्याने मोजणे म्हणजे एक निश्चित अंतराने संख्या वाढवणे.
उदाहरण: ३ च्या टप्प्याने ३,६,९,१२,१५… अशी संख्या येतात.
टप्पा म्हणजे पुढील संख्या शोधण्यासाठी किती संख्या मोजायच्या ते.
सशाने उड्या मारलेल्या चौकटीतील संख्या पाहून टप्पा ओळखा.
हरणाने उड्या मारलेल्या चौकटीतील संख्या पाहून टप्पा ओळखा.
रंगीत चौकटीतील संख्या पाहून त्या कोणत्या टप्प्याने आल्या आहेत ते शोधा.
फरशीवर चौकटी आखून क्रमाने संख्या लिहा आणि टप्पा शोधा.
टप्पा शोधल्यावर त्या टप्प्यानुसार येणाऱ्या संख्यांवर उड्या मारू शकतो.
टप्पा शोधण्यासाठी पुढील संख्या शोधण्यासाठी ३,४,५… अशी संख्या मोजा.
उदाहरण: ३ च्या टप्प्याने ३ नंतर ६, ६ नंतर ९, ९ नंतर १२…
उदाहरण: ४ च्या टप्प्याने ४ नंतर ८, ८ नंतर १२, १२ नंतर १६…
उदाहरण: ५ च्या टप्प्याने ५ नंतर १०, १० नंतर १५, १५ नंतर २०…
टप्पा शोधणे म्हणजे गणितात पॅटर्न ओळखणे.
टप्पा ओळखल्यावर पुढील संख्या सहजपणे शोधता येतात.
सशाच्या, हरणाच्या आणि रंगीत चौकटींच्या संख्यांमध्ये टप्पा शोधून खेळू शकतो.
टप्पा शोधताना संख्या एकमेकांमध्ये समान अंतर ठेवतात.
टप्पा शोधण्यासाठी संख्या १ पासून सुरू करून मोजू शकतो.
टप्पा शोधल्यावर त्या टप्प्यानुसार उड्या मारून गणिताचा सराव करता येतो.
टप्पा शोधणे हे गणितातील एक महत्त्वाचे कौशल्य आहे.
टप्पा शोधल्याने संख्या ओळखणे आणि मोजणे सोपे होते.
टप्पा शोधून गणिताच्या इतर विषयांमध्येही उपयोग होतो.
टप्पा शोधताना लक्षात ठेवा की पुढील संख्या नेहमी समान अंतराने वाढते.

notes: बेरीज म्हणजे दोन किंवा अधिक संख्यांची एकूण रक्कम.
बेरीज करताना क्रम महत्त्वाचा नाही – हे गुणधर्म ‘परिवर्तनीय गुणधर्म’ म्हणतात.
बेरीज करताना शून्य जोडल्यास संख्या बदलत नाही – ‘शून्य गुणधर्म’.
बेरीज करताना १ जोडल्यास संख्या १ ने वाढते – ‘एकक गुणधर्म’.
बेरीज करताना १० जोडल्यास दहाच्या स्थानावर १ वाढते – ‘दहाच्या स्थानाचे गुणधर्म’.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ म्हणजे दहाच्या स्थानावरून पुढच्या स्थानावर १ घेणे.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ९ + ९ = १८, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ५ + ६ = ११, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ७ + ८ = १५, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ८ + ९ = १७, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ९ + ९ = १८, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता १ + १ = २, येथे ० कॅरी ० घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता २ + २ = ४, येथे ० कॅरी ० घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ३ + ३ = ६, येथे ० कॅरी ० घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ४ + ४ = ८, येथे ० कॅरी ० घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ५ + ५ = १०, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ६ + ६ = १२, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ७ + ७ = १४, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ८ + ८ = १६, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता ९ + ९ = १८, येथे १ कॅरी १ घेतो.
बेरीज करताना ‘कॅरी’ न करता १ + २ = ३, येथे ० कॅरी ० घेतो.

notes: चढता क्रम म्हणजे लहान ते मोठा क्रम
उतरता क्रम म्हणजे मोठा ते लहान क्रम
संख्या लावण्यासाठी प्रथम सर्वांत लहान किंवा मोठी संख्या शोधा
चढता क्रम लावण्यासाठी तुलना जोड्यांनी करा
उतरता क्रम लावण्यासाठी तुलना जोड्यांनी करा
समान संख्या असल्यास दोन्ही समान मानाव्यात
क्रम लावताना रेघ मारून लिहा
चढता व उतरता क्रम दोन्ही शिकल्याने तुलना कौशल्य वाढते
सोप्या पद्धतीने क्रम लावण्यासाठी लहान संख्या प्रथम शोधा
उच्च संख्या प्रथम शोधल्यास उतरता क्रम सोपा
क्रम लावताना पाटीवर लिहून दाखवा
समीकरणे नाहीत, फक्त तुलना चिन्हे वापरा

subject: Maths
chapter: चला, संखया तयार करुया क्रमवाचक शबद
notes: क्रमवाचक शब्द म्हणजे क्रम सांगणारे शब्द जसे पहिला, दुसरा, तिसरा, चौथा, पाचवा इत्यादी.
मूल्यवाचक संख्या म्हणजे वस्तूंची मोजणी करणाऱ्या संख्या जसे १, २, ३, ४, ५ इत्यादी.
क्रमवाचक शब्द आणि मूल्यवाचक संख्या एकत्र वापरून आपण एखाद्या गोष्टीचा क्रम सांगू शकतो.
उदाहरणार्थ ‘पाचवा’ म्हणजे पाचवा क्रमांक, ‘सातवा’ म्हणजे सातवा क्रमांक.
दोन अंकी संख्या तयार करताना पहिला अंक शून्य नसावा.
सर्वांत मोठी दोन अंकी संख्या म्हणजे ९० पेक्षा कमी सर्वात मोठी संख्या, सर्वांत लहान म्हणजे १० पेक्षा मोठी सर्वात लहान संख्या.
एकाच अंकाची पुनरावृत्ती करून दोन अंकी संख्या तयार करता येतात, जसे ११, २२, ३३ इत्यादी.
वर्तुळात दिलेल्या अंकांमधून दोन अंक निवडून संख्या तयार करणे हे एक खेळ आहे.
शून्येतर संख्या लिहिलेल्या चकत्या उचलून दोन अंकी संख्या तयार करणे हे देखील एक खेळ आहे.
क्रमवाचक शब्दांचा वापर करून आपण शर्यतीतील स्थान, डब्यांचा क्रम इत्यादी सांगू शकतो.
शब्द ‘पहिला’, ‘दुसरा’, ‘तिसरा’ इत्यादी क्रमवाचक शब्द आहेत.
मूल्यवाचक संख्या ‘१’, ‘२’, ‘३’ इत्यादी आहेत.
क्रमवाचक शब्द आणि मूल्यवाचक संख्या एकत्र वापरल्यास वाक्य अधिक स्पष्ट होते.
क्रमवाचक शब्दांचा वापर करताना शब्दाचा शेवट ‘-वा’ किंवा ‘-वी’ असा असतो.
दोन अंकी संख्या तयार करताना पहिला अंक शून्य नसावा हे लक्षात ठेवा.

quiz.q: क्रमवाचक शब्द म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: क्रमवाचक शब्द क्रम सांगतात.

quiz.q: १ आणि २ या संख्या कोणत्या प्रकारच्या आहेत?
quiz.explain: १ आणि २ हे मूल्यवाचक संख्या आहेत.

quiz.q: दोन अंकी संख्या तयार करताना पहिला अंक शून्य असू शकतो का?
quiz.explain: पहिला अंक शून्य असू शकत नाही.

quiz.q: ‘सातवा’ हा शब्द कोणत्या प्रकारचा आहे?
quiz.explain: ‘सातवा’ हा क्रमवाचक शब्द आहे.

quiz.q: वर्तुळात दिलेल्या अंकांमधून दोन अंक निवडून काय तयार करायचे?
quiz.explain: दोन अंक निवडून संख्या तयार करायची.

quiz.q: शून्येतर संख्या लिहिलेल्या चकत्या उचलून काय करायचे?
quiz.explain: चकत्या उचलून संख्या तयार करायची.

quiz.q: ‘पाचवा’ हा शब्द कोणत्या क्रमात येतो?
quiz.explain: ‘पाचवा’ म्हणजे पाचवा क्रम.

quiz.q: दोन अंकी संख्या तयार करताना किती वेगवेगळ्या संख्या मिळू शकतात?
क्रमवाचक शब्दांमध्ये शेवटचा प्रत्यय काय असतो?
quiz.explain: क्रमवाचक शब्दांमध्ये ‘-वा’ किंवा ‘-वी’ असतो.

quiz.q: ‘मूल्यवाचक संख्या’ म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: मूल्यवाचक संख्या वस्तूंची मोजणी करतात.

subject: Maths
notes: भाज्या आणि फळे बाजारात कसे मोजायचे हे शिकतो.
बाजारात असलेल्या हातगाड्यांची संख्या मोजतो.
फळे विकणाऱ्या माणसांची संख्या मोजतो.
बाजारात असलेल्या चार प्रकारच्या फळांची नावे लिहितो.
पाच प्रकारच्या भाज्यांची नावे लिहितो.
बाजारात दिसणाऱ्या मुलगे आणि मुलींची एकूण संख्या मोजतो.
कापडी पिशवी घेऊन आलेल्या लोकांची एकूण संख्या मोजतो.
रस्त्यावर लाल दिव्यानंतर थांबलेल्या वाहनांची नोंद करतो.
हिरव्या दिव्यानंतर चालणाऱ्या वाहनांची नोंद करतो.
हवेचे प्रदूषण करणारी वाहने ओळखतो.
सायकल, मोटारसायकल, कार, बस व रिक्षा यांपैकी सर्वात जास्त संख्या असलेल्या वाहनाची ओळख करतो.
रंगांच्या गाड्या किती आहेत ते पाहून लोकांना कोणता रंग आवडतो ते शोधतो.
चिमण्या किंवा कबुतरे यांना दाणे टाकून किती पक्षी येतात ते मोजतो.
पुन्हा दाणे टिपायला आलेला पक्षी ओळखता येतो का ते पाहतो.
माहिती गोळा करण्यासाठी निरीक्षण आणि नोंद घेणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.

quiz.q: बाजारात फळे विकणाऱ्या माणसांची संख्या किती असते?

notes: वजाबाकी म्हणजे दोन संख्यांमधून एक संख्या कमी करणे.

दशक सुटा केल्यावर एककांचे घर ०-९ मध्ये राहते.

दशक सुटा करताना लक्षात ठेवा: १ दशक = १० एकक.
वजाबाकी करताना एककाचे घर ९ पेक्षा मोठे ठेवू नका; काम झाल्यावर ते ०-९ मध्ये आणा.
वजाबाकीचे नियम: १. एकक वजा करता येत असेल तर थेट वजा करा.
२. नाही तर दशक सुटा करून १० एकक जोडा आणि वजा करा.
३. जर दशक शून्य झाले आणि वजाबाकी शक्य नसेल तर उत्तर शून्य किंवा नकारात्मक.
वजाबाकी करताना 'सुटा' म्हणजे 'कमी करणे' किंवा 'काढणे' असे समजावे.
वजाबाकीचे उत्तर नेहमीच सकारात्मक किंवा शून्य असते (समान संख्येची वजाबाकी केल्यास ०).

वजाबाकीचे सराव करताना 'दशक सुटा' ही पद्धत लक्षात ठेवा आणि ती नियमितपणे वापरा.

• लांबी मोजताना काठीची लांबी समान असणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.

subject: Maths
notes: आकृतिबंध म्हणजे एखाद्या वस्तूचा पृष्ठभागावरून काढलेला रेखाचित्र.
भेंडी, सीताफळ, चिकू यांची बिया किंवा दाणे वापरून आपण आकृतिबंध तयार करू शकतो.
आकृतिबंध बनवण्यासाठी प्रथम वस्तूचा ठसा कागदावर घ्या आणि नंतर रंगाने भरा.
आकृतिबंधात आकृतीचे मुख्य भाग आणि तपशील दाखवले जातात.
आकृतिबंधाचे उदाहरणे: पान, फळ, फुल, दाणा इत्यादी.
आकृतिबंध तयार करताना वस्तूची बाह्यरेषा आणि आतील भाग दोन्ही दाखवणे महत्त्वाचे.
आकृतिबंधात अक्षरे आणि संख्या वापरून विविध आकृत्या ओळखता येतात.
आकृतिबंध तयार करताना वस्तूची सममिती आणि आकार लक्षात घ्या.
आकृतिबंधात रिकाम्या जागा भरून पूर्ण आकृती कशी बनवायची ते शिकूया.
आकृतिबंधाचे नमुने ओळखण्यासाठी मुलांना विविध आकृत्या दाखवा आणि त्यांना ओळखायला सांगा.

notes: गुणाकार म्हणजे एकाच संख्येची पुनःपुन्हा बेरीज करणे.
उदाहरणार्थ ३ + ३ + ३ = ९ हे ३ गुणिले ३ बरोबर ९.
गुणाकाराचे चिन्ह ‘>’ किंवा ‘×’ असे लिहिले जाते.
पाढा म्हणजे एखाद्या संख्येचे गुणाकाराचे तक्ते.
पाढा वापरल्याने मोठ्या बेरीज पटकन करता येतात.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते १ ते १० पर्यंत शिकणे महत्त्वाचे.
पाढा वाचताना ‘तीन गुणिले पाच बरोबर पंधरा’ असे म्हणतात.
गुणाकाराची ओळख ‘पुनःपुन्हा बेरीज’ या संकल्पनेने होते.
गुणाकाराचे चिन्ह ‘>’ हे ‘गुणिले’ दर्शवते.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते लक्षात ठेवण्यासाठी गाणी किंवा ताल वापरता येतात.
गुणाकाराची मदत ‘बेरीज’ पेक्षा जलद असते.
गुणाकार शिकल्याने ‘विभाजन’ देखील सोपे होते.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ५, १०, २५ इत्यादींमध्ये विशेषतः उपयुक्त आहेत.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते सराव केल्याने गणितात आत्मविश्वास वाढतो.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते शिकताना ‘गुणाकाराचे तत्त्व’ लक्षात ठेवणे आवश्यक आहे.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ‘पुनःपुन्हा बेरीज’ या पद्धतीने तयार होतात.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ‘गुणाकाराचे चिन्ह’ आणि ‘परिणाम’ या दोन भागांमध्ये विभागलेले असतात.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ‘गुणाकाराचे नियम’ (जसे १×१=१) यावर आधारित असतात.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ‘गुणाकाराचे पद्धती’ (जसे ‘विभाजन’ किंवा ‘बेरीज’) यावर अवलंबून असतात.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ‘गुणाकाराचे तत्त्व’ (जसे ‘पुनःपुन्हा बेरीज’) यावर आधारित असतात.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ‘गुणाकाराचे नियम’ (जसे ‘१×१=१’) यावर आधारित असतात.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ‘गुणाकाराचे पद्धती’ (जसे ‘विभाजन’ किंवा ‘बेरीज’) यावर अवलंबून असतात.
गुणाकाराचे तक्ते ‘गुणाकाराचे तत्त्व’ (जसे ‘पुनःपुन्हा बेरीज’) यावर आधारित असतात.

notes: गोष्टीतील गणित म्हणजे गोष्टींची मोजणी आणि तुलना करण्याचे गणित.
मोजणी म्हणजे वस्तूंची संख्या शोधणे.
वस्तूंची मोजणी करताना एकेक करून मोजणे महत्त्वाचे.
मोजणी करताना ‘एक’, ‘दोन’, ‘तीन’ अशी क्रमवारी लक्षात ठेवावी.
गुणाकार म्हणजे एकाच वस्तूंचे गट बनवून मोजणे.
उदाहरणार्थ, २ गट × ३ वस्तू = ६ वस्तू.
विभाजन म्हणजे वस्तूंचे समान भागात वाटणे.
उदाहरणार्थ, १० वस्तू ५ लोकांमध्ये वाटल्यास प्रत्येकाला २ वस्तू मिळतील.
समानता म्हणजे दोन गोष्टींची तुलना करून एकसारखेपणा ओळखणे.
समानता दाखवण्यासाठी ‘समान’ किंवा ‘समान आहेत’ असे शब्द वापरतात.
विभिन्नता म्हणजे दोन गोष्टींची तुलना करून फरक ओळखणे.
विभिन्नता दाखवण्यासाठी ‘भिन्न’ किंवा ‘भिन्न आहेत’ असे शब्द वापरतात.
गणितात ‘जोडणे’ म्हणजे दोन संख्यांची बेरीज करणे.
गणितात ‘वजाबाकी’ म्हणजे एक संख्या दुसऱ्यापासून वजा करणे.
गणितात ‘गुणाकार’ म्हणजे एक संख्या दुसऱ्याने गुणणे.
गणितात ‘भागाकार’ म्हणजे एक संख्या दुसऱ्याने भागणे.
मोजणी करताना ‘किती’ आणि ‘किती आहेत’ हे प्रश्न विचारतात.
गणितात ‘मोजणी’ आणि ‘गणना’ हे शब्द एकसारखे अर्थाचे आहेत.
मोजणी करताना ‘एकेक’ मोजणे सोपे असते.
गणितात ‘कमी’ आणि ‘जास्त’ हे शब्द तुलना करण्यास मदत करतात.
गणितात ‘समान’ आणि ‘भिन्न’ हे शब्द तुलना करण्यास मदत करतात.
गणितात ‘बेरीज’ आणि ‘वजाबाकी’ हे मूलभूत क्रिया आहेत.
गणितात ‘गुणाकार’ आणि ‘भागाकार’ हे मूलभूत क्रिया आहेत.

notes: • संख्या म्हणजे वस्तूंची मोजणी.

subject: Maths
notes: • स्थानिक किंमत म्हणजे एखाद्या अंकाची किंमत त्या अंकाच्या स्थानानुसार.
• दशके (दहाच्या स्थानावर) असलेल्या अंकाची स्थानिक किंमत = अंक × 10.
• एकके (एकाच्या स्थानावर) असलेल्या अंकाची स्थानिक किंमत = अंक × 1.
• उदाहरण: ३५ या संख्येत ३ हा दशक आहे → ३ × 10 = ३०.
• शून्याची स्थानिक किंमत नेहमी ० असते.
• एखाद्या संख्येतील प्रत्येक अंकाची स्थानिक किंमत शोधण्यासाठी प्रथम अंकाचे स्थान ओळखा.
• दशकाच्या स्थानावर असलेल्या अंकाला 10 ने गुणा करा; एककाच्या स्थानावर असलेल्या अंकाला 1 ने गुणा करा.
• १०० पेक्षा कमी असलेल्या संख्यांमध्ये फक्त दशक आणि एकक असतात.
• १०० पेक्षा जास्त संख्यांमध्ये शेकड्याचे स्थान देखील असते, परंतु या अध्यायात आपण फक्त दशक आणि एककावर लक्ष देत आहोत.
• स्थानिक किंमत शोधताना अंकाला त्याच्या स्थानाच्या गुणकाने गुणा करणे हेच नियम आहे.
• स्थानिक किंमत शोधल्यावर ती संख्या त्या स्थानावर किती मूल्य देते हे समजते.
• स्थानिक किंमत शोधणे हे गणितात अंकांची जागा समजण्यासाठी महत्त्वाचे आहे.
• जर एखाद्या अंकाची स्थानिक किंमत ० असेल तर तो अंक त्या स्थानावर काहीही योगदान देत नाही.
• स्थानिक किंमत शोधून आपण संख्येचे भागांमध्ये विभाजन करू शकतो आणि त्यावरून बेरीज, गुणाकार इत्यादी सोपे होतात.
• स्थानिक किंमत हे गणितातील ‘स्थान मूल्य’ या संकल्पनेचे मूलभूत रूप आहे.
• स्थानिक किंमत ओळखल्याने आपण संख्येची रचना आणि तिचे मूल्य समजू शकतो.
• या अध्यायात आपण फक्त १०० पेक्षा कमी संख्यांतील दशक आणि एककाची स्थानिक किंमत शिकणार आहोत.
• लक्षात ठेवा: दशकाचा अंक १० ने गुणला जातो, एककाचा अंक १ ने गुणला जातो.
• स्थानिक किंमत शोधताना अंकाची जागा बदलल्यास त्याची किंमत बदलते.
